text: Should the WInS portfolio be the literal 2027 book (almost all Treasury ladder plus a small labelled surplus sleeve) rather than the post-2028 target mix now drafted?
anchor_quote: "The WInS portfolio represents each team’s implementation of its investment strategy during the competition. It does not determine Laura’s actual portfolio value at the beginning of 2027." (case p.4 L129-130); "The additional $150,000 contribution described in the Client Case Study will not be added to WInS." (SMApply Trading Details)
hypothesis: GUESS: The case text favours the 2027 book. 'During the competition' means Year 0; WInS cash was cut from $500k (R-W98) to exactly the $300k Year-1 deposit; the $150k is excluded. Under lock-early, that book is about $292k of ladder and about $8k of surplus (F-101/F-104, VERIFIED-REPO-FILE). The diversification criterion pulls the other way. Middle path: hold the 2027 book, put about 3% in equity as a labelled surplus sleeve, and state in the IPS which book WInS represents. New evidence on brief section 9 open item; seed 3's '$500k' premise is outdated (R-AN14).
would_change_detail: WInS weights now (the equity share differs by about 15-20 points from securities_and_allocation_v0 option (ii)); one IPS sentence on what WInS represents.
north_star: Shows Laura we treated her real first deposit, not a generic model portfolio, as the thing to rehearse.

text: How should our trading notes explain that long-duration Treasuries, whose prices swing more than the example's intermediate fund, reduce risk to Laura's promise, without echoing the example's 'reduce portfolio volatility' logic?
anchor_quote: "We are purchasing shares of an intermediate-term U.S. Treasury bond ETF to reduce portfolio volatility and begin preparing for Laura’s future operating commitment. ... as the residency funding date approaches." (TN guide p.2 L36-39)
hypothesis: GUESS: Wharton's example uses an asset-only, glide-path view. Our hedge holds long Treasuries: TLT's 3-year standard deviation is 13.74% versus IEF's 6.54% (F-201/F-202, VERIFIED-PRIMARY fact sheets). Such a hedge raises price volatility but lowers surplus risk, the gap between assets and the value of the ten payments. Each hedge note needs one plain clause saying the bond moves with the value of the payments. Do not state 'reduce volatility' as the purpose.
would_change_detail: The purpose clause in every hedge-trade WInS note from now on (notes cannot be edited) and in the Oct 23 reflections.
north_star: Proves we understand her promise, not just asset prices, which is exactly what the example-copying majority will miss.

text: Should every WInS note carry one dated, checkable data point, the Laura goal it serves and one named risk, going beyond Wharton's example, which contains no number?
anchor_quote: "your Trading Notes should document the research, analysis, and reasoning behind your investment decisions" (TN p.1 L8-9); "Include each Trading Note exactly as it appears in WInS." (TN p.2 L44)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The guide asks for 'research', but the 59-word example (R-T26) has no data. A dated fact, such as the 10-year Treasury at 5.17% on 25 Sep (F-001, VERIFIED-PRIMARY), proves the reasoning came before the outcome. Spec per note: action; which bucket; one dated number with its source named in words; the Laura goal; one named risk; about 60-90 words. No character limit is published.
would_change_detail: The template for every WInS note written from day 1, which becomes the Oct 23 TN quotes.
north_star: A statistics-trained client trusts reasoning that shows its evidence at the moment of decision.

text: When one strategic decision needs several trades (because of a position limit or a two-fund duration match), which trade carries the note, and should each note name its companion trades so it stands alone when quoted?
anchor_quote: "select three investment decisions that best illustrate your team’s strategic thinking" (TN p.1 L11) versus "Select three (3) Trading Notes from trades your team executed in WInS." (TN p.2 L42)
hypothesis: GUESS: The guide treats 'decision' and 'trade' as the same thing. A possible 25% per-security position limit (Stock-Trak default, UNVERIFIED for this season, guardrails G) would force the hedge into 3 or more trades. Write a full note on every trade; each names its companions ('one of three trades that together match...'); the largest or first trade is the TN candidate.
would_change_detail: The note-writing protocol for split trades now, and which trade is picked for the TN.
north_star: Each quoted note must show the whole decision for Laura, not a fragment.

text: Should the three Trading Notes between them cover the six dimensions the guide names, and should at least one show a decision that tested or refined the strategy rather than only reflected it?
anchor_quote: "including its approach to growth, risk, liquidity, funding reliability, financial flexibility, and future cash-flow needs" (TN p.1 L5-6); "reflected, tested, or refined the team’s developing strategy" (case p.4 L152-153)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Notes come before the IPS so that judges see a strategy developing (seed 13). The explicit protection for sells and changed approaches invites one real refinement: a rebalance after a rate move, a split forced by a discovered rule, or a sell. Picks: one note for the promise, one for growth and risk, one for a genuine refinement (liquidity or flexibility). Never stage a trade just for the notes: fabrication is banned (R-W28).
would_change_detail: Which three trades are selected, and whether a planned refinement trade happens before Oct 23.
north_star: Shows Laura a firm that learns and adjusts, as she did from comic to memoir, rather than a static shopping list.

text: Does the WInS rule 'no more than twice a security's current daily trading volume' use today's running volume, so that an overnight order from Australia filled at the open in a thin Treasury fund or individual bond could be rejected or only partly filled?
anchor_quote: "Your team may trade an amount equal to no more than twice a security’s current daily trading volume." (SMApply Trading Details)
hypothesis: GUESS: Stock-Trak probably uses the previous day's or average volume, but 'current' is undefined, and at the open today's volume is near zero. iBonds Dec 2036 (IBTR): 30-day average 68,915 shares at $23.63 (about $1.6m a day), net assets $34.2m. Dec 2034 (IBTP): 111,113 shares at $24.22 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, ishares.com, 2026-09-27). A $30-40k order is fine on an average basis but uncertain intraday. Test one small order first and read the Session Rules tooltip.
would_change_detail: Order timing, sizing and type in WInS now; whether thin defined-maturity funds or individual bonds are used.
north_star: Flawless compliance (last year's failure) is the entry ticket to being chosen at all.

text: How do we show 'appropriate diversification' when about two-thirds or more of the portfolio is Treasuries?
anchor_quote: "uses appropriate diversification" (criterion 1); "diversification across asset classes, sectors, industries, market capitalizations, geographic regions, risk characteristics, and funding purposes" (SMApply Trading Details)
hypothesis: GUESS: Use Wharton's own term 'funding purposes'. The portfolio is diversified by purpose first (promise hedge versus growth), then by geography and asset inside the growth sleeve (a global rather than U.S.-only equity fund). Say this explicitly in the IPS and Final Report so a skimming grader does not read 'concentrated'.
would_change_detail: The IPS diversification sentence; possibly the growth-sleeve choice (global versus U.S. equity).
north_star: Turns an apparent weakness into evidence that every dollar has a named job for Laura.

text: Which contingent 'if X, then Y' rules must be written into the IPS now, since the strategy cannot be revised after Nov 6 but the Final Report must give recommendations under varying outcomes?
anchor_quote: "Your team may not revise its investment strategy after the submission deadline." (IPS p.2 L73-74); "recommendations ... under varying investment outcomes" (IPS p.2 L77-78)
hypothesis: GUESS: Laura's money arrives in January 2027, after the freeze. The ladder cost more than $300k on 173 of 185 trading days in 2026 (F-111, VERIFIED-PRIMARY inputs), and P(cost > $300k on 1 Jan 2027) is about 24% (F-112, ASSUMPTION). A rule for that case written only in the Final Report would be a revision. The IPS needs 4-5 one-line rules (about 120-150 words): January 2027 purchase rule; smaller or late 2028 deposit; 2031 floor share; 2033 gift rule; rebalancing bands.
would_change_detail: The IPS structure and word budget, and the rule thresholds (numbers) fixed on Nov 6.
north_star: A plan that already knows what it will do in bad markets is what an IPS is for, and what earns a client's confidence.

text: Who decides what in the IPS decision-making framework: which decisions are automatic rules, which does the firm make, and which does Laura make?
anchor_quote: "Your portfolio manager (your team’s teacher/advisor who makes the final investment decisions for your firm’s portfolio)" (case p.1 L4-5); "Laura must decide how much of the remaining portfolio she can responsibly contribute" (case p.3 L101-102)
hypothesis: GUESS; new evidence: the 2021-22 and 2022-23 cases (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, Wharton archive, 2026-09-27) say analysts 'hope to one day become portfolio managers who make the final investment decisions for WGAM’s portfolio', and that WGAM 'currently manages a $100,000,000 portfolio'. So the line is inherited boilerplate about the firm's own book, orphaned this year. Framework: Laura approves the policy and makes the 2031 announcement and 2033 gift decisions; pre-set rules run the hedge and rebalancing; the firm recommends and reports yearly. Imply nothing about the real advisor deciding.
would_change_detail: The governance clause of the IPS.
north_star: Laura keeps the two decisions that are hers; she would choose a firm that respects that.

text: In an IPS that bans charts, which numbers and rules must appear in words, and are small tables or informal source mentions allowed?
anchor_quote: "Graphics, charts, images, attachments, external links, footnotes, and formal citations are not permitted." (IPS p.3 L123); "The IPS is not expected to include ... a final facility-contribution range" (IPS p.2 L68-69)
hypothesis: GUESS: Tables are not on the banned list, but a reader may count one as a graphic, and the penalty is exclusion, so use no tables. The word 'final' implies a provisional rule is fine. Carry about 6-10 numbers in words: bucket weights and bands, the certainty test (for example funded ratio of at least 100% at market prices), floor share, key dates. Name data sources informally in the text, never as citations. Count words with the same tool used for the final PDF, and leave a margin.
would_change_detail: IPS layout (no tables) and which figures appear in it.
north_star: Words-only clarity is where an authentic team voice either shows or disappears.

text: Should the deliverables tie each of the case's three wordings (certainty, confidence, reliability) to one object, and use them only that way?
anchor_quote: "a high degree of certainty" (case p.3 L91); "state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range" (p.3 L117-118); "Teams may reach different conclusions about ... funding confidence" (p.4 L127)
hypothesis: GUESS: The case uses 'certainty' for the payments and 'confident' for the facility range. 'Funding confidence' is listed among the things teams may disagree on, which points to the facility. Mapping: certainty for the payments (bought, market-consistent); confidence for the facility range (a stated probability); reliability for the portfolio property the IPS balances. Phrases like '95% confidence in the payments' would signal a careless reading to a statistics graduate.
would_change_detail: Terminology in every IPS and Final Report sentence on risk, plus a glossary line in the Final Report.
north_star: Precise words show a statistics graduate that we read her case as carefully as she would.

text: The case says Laura has financial resources outside the portfolio. Does that raise her capacity to take risk with the surplus, and should the IPS call this a dedicated goal portfolio rather than her whole wealth?
anchor_quote: "Laura’s living expenses and short-term financial needs will be covered by income and financial resources outside the portfolio." (case p.2 L61-63)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. 'Financial resources', not only income, means other assets. Capacity to bear loss on the surplus is higher than for a whole-wealth portfolio, while the promise stays ring-fenced by the ladder. This is case evidence for the 60-70% end of the open sleeve-equity band (F-407: median $205k/$207k/$209k, p5 $164k/$159k/$154k, VERIFIED-REPO-FILE script). The IPS risk-tolerance line: willingness from 'thoughtful risks', capacity from outside resources.
would_change_detail: Sleeve equity weight (50/60/70%), plus the IPS risk-tolerance sentence.
north_star: Tailors risk to her full situation, which a generic portfolio never does.

text: Should the Final Report give Laura one recommendation, or a small menu of options for her to choose from?
anchor_quote: "she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance" (case p.2 L71-74) versus "the investment strategy that Laura ultimately chooses" (p.1 L9)
hypothesis: GUESS: She chooses between firms, but within a firm she asked for a recommendation. Give one recommendation plus one line on what she would give up or gain one step more cautious or one step bolder (for example sleeve equity 50% versus 70%, with F-407 numbers).
would_change_detail: Structure of the Final Report's recommendation section.
north_star: Decisive yet respectful of her choice: the tone that earns a client's confidence.

text: What liquidity need does the case actually give Laura, and what should the IPS's required 'liquidity' sentence therefore say?
anchor_quote: "How does your strategy balance growth, risk, liquidity, funding reliability, and financial flexibility?" (IPS p.1 L20); "she will neither add to nor withdraw from the portfolio before 2033." (case p.2 L63-65)
hypothesis: GUESS: Liquidity needs are dated, not continuous: nothing before 2033; each 1 Jan from 2033 to 2042; the facility gift in 2033. Each is met by a maturing bond rather than a forced sale. Say this in one sentence so a reader does not think liquidity was ignored or that cash drag is needed.
would_change_detail: The IPS liquidity sentence.
north_star: Shows every requirement answered in her terms, with dates rather than jargon.

text: Would a former tech product manager recognise the plan as hers if it were framed as dated stage gates (2027 buy, 2028 top-up, 2031 announce, 2033 gift), each with conditions?
anchor_quote: "before beginning her career as a product manager in the technology industry" (case p.1 L16-17); the timeline lists only 2026, 2027, 2028, 2031 and 2033 (p.2 L49-57)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The case lists only the years when a decision falls (R-AN11), and product managers work in roadmaps and go/no-go gates. Framing the IPS and Final Report timeline this way is professional (X-23) and in her own working language, drawn from her stated career, not from identity. D6 should verify how she describes planning in her public professional writing.
would_change_detail: The organising frame of the IPS and the Final Report timeline chart.
north_star: Speaks the way she has actually worked, so the strategy feels like hers.

text: The case names no values or ESG preference this year, although every recent case had a social goal. Should our deliverables say her impact comes through the payout (the residency), not through screening the portfolio?
anchor_quote: 0 hits for "ESG", "values", "impact", "sustainab" across the four official documents (R-AN34, VERIFIED-REPO-FILE)
hypothesis: GUESS; new evidence: 2021-22 scholarship, 2022-23 start-up fund and wellness centre, 2024-25 Nigeria housing and youth centre (all VERIFIED-PRIMARY archive pages); 2025-26 asked teams to 'think beyond financial returns and consider how their strategies could support long-term community impact' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY finalists page). This year the impact sits in the goal, and the investing instructions are silent. So no ESG screens; one Final Report line: the promise uses the plainest instruments so every dollar of impact reaches the residency.
would_change_detail: No values screens in the portfolio; one rationale sentence in the Final Report.
north_star: Respects what her case actually asks, instead of projecting last year's client onto her.

text: Because Laura decides her 2033 facility contribution herself, should the confidence statement be the probability that the portfolio can afford the bottom of the range, combined with a rule that caps the gift at the top?
anchor_quote: "state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range" (case p.3 L117-118); "Laura must decide how much of the remaining portfolio she can responsibly contribute" (p.3 L101-102)
hypothesis: GUESS: The contribution is a decision, not a market outcome. Rule: gift = floor plus a share of the excess, capped at the top of the range. Under this rule the gift is in the range whenever the residual covers the floor, which is close to certain once the floor is bought in 2031 (brief section 8.7). Report two numbers: P(gift at or above the floor), about 100%; and P(reaching the top), from the model. The two-sided 'miss' problem (R-AN9) disappears. Most teams will present a portfolio-value forecast interval instead.
would_change_detail: The confidence levels stated with the range (Final Report and co-sponsor draft); a new contribution rule in strategy_mc.
north_star: Lets Laura promise co-sponsors something she can always keep, which protects the credibility her career runs on.

text: Should the recommended 'dollar range' be a fixed number computed today, or a rule Laura applies in 2031 with today's projection shown as an illustration?
anchor_quote: "In 2031, however, the value of her portfolio in 2033 remains uncertain." ... "Teams must recommend the dollar range Laura should communicate" (case p.3 L112-117)
hypothesis: GUESS: A fixed range computed in 2026 will almost certainly be off by 2031 (floor p5/p50/p95 $127k/$165k/$217k, F-402, VERIFIED-REPO-FILE script). Give both: the rule (bottom = the floor bought in 2031; top = floor plus a share of the remaining sleeve), and a 2026 illustration (median-case range, plus how it shifts in a bad or good 2027-31). This directly answers the case's request to explain favourable and unfavourable outcomes.
would_change_detail: The form of the range recommendation in the Final Report (rule plus illustration) and its illustrative numbers.
north_star: Gives Laura a tool that works in her real 2031, not a number that goes stale.

text: Since Laura will only 'begin' approaching co-sponsors in 2031, should the plan pre-schedule a 2032 update that narrows the range while the floor never falls?
anchor_quote: "Laura plans to begin approaching potential co-sponsors in 2031, two years before the residency is established." (case p.3 L109)
hypothesis: GUESS: 'Begin' implies continuing conversations from 2031 to 2033. One pre-announced 2032 update, with more of the sleeve locked and the top of the range narrowed, matches capital-campaign practice and can only surprise upward. Seed 8's 2-year Treasury point is already settled (brief section 8.7); this adds the update schedule. D5 to verify how campaigns update pledges.
would_change_detail: A 2031-2033 update rule in the IPS; one sentence in the co-sponsor draft.
north_star: Co-sponsors hear only good news after 2031, which is how her credibility compounds.

text: With the facility cost unknown, what makes Laura's contribution 'meaningful' to co-sponsors: its dollar size, its share of her capacity, or the certainty that it will be delivered, including her secured ten years of operations?
anchor_quote: "A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura’s commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute." (case p.3 L110-112)
hypothesis: GUESS: 'Meaningful' is undefined and the cost is unknown by design, so meaning comes from credibility and personal stake relative to her capacity. New link to seed 6: a building with no operating money is a stranded asset, and funders avoid running costs (BS-17, VERIFIED-PRIMARY SSIR via A3). So her secured $500k (nominal) of operations is part of the 'meaningful' signal. The draft should lead with total secured support and state the gift as a share of her investable portfolio, never as a share of the unknown cost.
would_change_detail: The headline and framing of the Final Report fundraising draft.
north_star: Presents Laura's commitment at its true size, which is what makes co-sponsors join.

text: Since the facility money is only what is left after the reserve, is it a residual claim? And should the Final Report show co-sponsors that matching the reserve early removes the leverage that would make the gift swing more than the whole portfolio?
anchor_quote: "At the beginning of 2033, before making the first operating payment or contributing to the facility, Laura will set aside a portion of the portfolio to fund the ten payments." (case p.3 L94-95); "how much of the remaining portfolio" (L101)
hypothesis: GUESS: The word order confirms seed 5 (promise first). If the reserve (about $395k on forwards, F-106) is bought only in 2033, the residual swings about 3 times as much, in percentage terms, as total assets. The outcome spreads already show this: growth-first surplus $20k/$226k/$540k versus lock-early $159k/$207k/$273k (brief section 8). What is new is the co-sponsor-facing reason the range is narrow: the promise is already paid for. Chart: a 1 Jan 2033 waterfall (reserve, first payment, gift, flexibility).
would_change_detail: One co-sponsor sentence and one Final Report chart specification (waterfall using F-106 and F-401).
north_star: Explains in one picture why her promise is steadier than other firms' plans.

text: How should financial flexibility be expressed when teams need not size a contingency fund? Is it simply the unpledged upside above the capped gift?
anchor_quote: "She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops." ... "Teams are not expected to determine the size or investment composition of a separate contingency fund or endowment." (case p.3 L102-107)
hypothesis: GUESS: Express it as a rule, for example 'at least X% of the post-reserve surplus is never pledged', with dollar values at p5/p50/p95. With the Q17 cap rule, flexibility falls out automatically, so one rule answers two requirements (a responsible gift and preserved flexibility). D3 should pick X so that p5 still leaves a buffer.
would_change_detail: The flexibility share X and its p5/p50/p95 dollar values in the Final Report; one IPS rule line.
north_star: Keeps room for a project that will change, as her own projects always have.

text: What would it cost to make the ten payments inflation-indexed, and should the Final Report show that the phrase 'not adjusted for inflation' is what makes the promise fit inside the first deposit?
anchor_quote: "For purposes of the competition, each payment is a fixed $50,000 and is not adjusted for inflation." (case p.3 L90)
hypothesis: GUESS: ASSUMPTION arithmetic (flat 5.359% nominal, which reproduces $292k per F-109; 2.35% inflation, close to the F-009 breakevens): fixed payments cost $292,273; indexed from 2033 they cost $321,971 (about +$30k, more than $300k); indexed in 2027 dollars $370,121. The 2042 payment is worth about $40.6k in 2033 dollars. 'For purposes of the competition' appears 3 times in the case, marking deliberate simplifications. Say plainly that inflation's cost passes to other operating funders. D1 should re-price on the real TIPS curve.
would_change_detail: A number pair and sentence in the Final Report assumptions section and the co-sponsor draft.
north_star: Honest about what her fixed promise buys over time: the credibility co-sponsors reward.

text: Funding after 2042 is out of scope, but a co-sponsor reading a ten-year pledge will ask about year eleven. What should the Final Report say without solving it?
anchor_quote: "Funding the residency beyond the final payment in 2042 is outside the scope of the competition." (case p.3 L92-93); "reliable support for its early operations" (L83)
hypothesis: GUESS: The case calls the ten years 'early operations', and a matched reserve runs to zero by 2042 by design. One boundary sentence: start-up support that ends on schedule, with the unpledged flexibility (Q22) as her optional, unpromised capacity. No numbers after 2042.
would_change_detail: A scope sentence in the Final Report and the co-sponsor draft.
north_star: Answers the question co-sponsors will ask, without overpromising.

text: The case fixes every payment date, yet asks teams to state assumptions about 'the timing of cash flows'. Which timing assumptions does it want?
anchor_quote: "All contributions and withdrawals occur at the beginning of the applicable year." (case p.2 L59); "Teams should identify and explain their assumptions about investment performance, the timing of cash flows, outside funding..." (p.4 L146-147)
hypothesis: GUESS: Real instruments do not pay on 1 Jan. TreasuryDirect: 2/5/7-year notes are issued on the last day of the month, and 10-year notes and 30-year bonds on the 15th of Feb/May/Aug/Nov (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, 2026-09-27; maturity = issue + term is an ASSUMPTION). iBonds terminate 'on or about October or December 15' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY ishares.com). S1 already costs the Nov-15 gap at +$2,124 ($294.4k ladder). The case also leaves open a late 2028 deposit and whether the facility gift is one payment or instalments. List four timing assumptions in the Final Report.
would_change_detail: The Final Report assumptions list, and which ladder cost is quoted ($294.4k versus $292.3k).
north_star: Precision on dates is the kind of care a promise-keeper wants from her firm.

text: Which market date should the Final Report's numbers be priced on: 25 Sep, the 6 Nov freeze, or the latest curve before 4 Dec?
anchor_quote: "Your portfolio and Final Report should reflect the strategy established in your IPS." (IPS p.2 L75); "Evaluators will consider the three deliverables together." (case p.4 L161)
hypothesis: GUESS: The 10-year yield moved about 120bp in 2026 and the ladder cost ranged from $292k to $326k (F-003, F-111, VERIFIED-PRIMARY inputs), so mixed pricing dates could make the deliverables disagree. Price the base case on 6 Nov, matching the frozen WInS book, and add one sensitivity line on the latest curve. The IPS should avoid a hard 'fits inside $300k' claim that one rate move could falsify.
would_change_detail: Every Final Report figure's pricing date; the IPS 'fits inside' wording.
north_star: Three deliverables that agree with each other read as one trustworthy firm.

text: The case never says why the residency is in Taiwan. Should our deliverables refuse to supply a reason, and guard against confusing Taiwan with her Wuhan birthplace?
anchor_quote: "Born in Wuhan, China, and raised in Texas" (case p.1 L13); "In 2033, Laura plans to establish a collaborative creative residency in Taiwan." (p.2 L76)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. A motive sentence such as 'returning to her roots' would invent facts, risk tokenism and conflate China with Taiwan (factually wrong and sensitive). Wharton says the scenario is invented (R-W4). Interview snippets mention professional time in Taiwan (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED); even if verified, they bear only on currency and cost context. Treat Taiwan as a location with currency (Q-A3-04) and cost facts (F-508, F-510) only.
would_change_detail: Removes or prevents any motive sentence in the Client Knowledge section and the co-sponsor draft.
north_star: Laura would notice immediately if we invented her reasons; restraint is respect.

text: What does the way Wharton's cases have changed across seasons reveal about what this year's designers want rewarded?
anchor_quote: "Teams are not expected to estimate that cost, prepare a construction budget, determine the project’s total funding gap, or develop a detailed business plan" (case p.4 L164-166); "not expected to determine the size or investment composition of a separate contingency fund or endowment" (p.3 L106-107)
hypothesis: GUESS: VERIFIED-PRIMARY archive pages: 2021-22 had a $5,000 scholarship 'for at least 10 years' and asked 'Should she keep $50,000 in cash?'; 2022-23 had 'use the interest ... to sustain the fund'; 2024-25 gave cost estimates ('$10,000 USD per housing unit'). 2025-26 targeted growth from $500k to $1.5m (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). This year removes cost estimates, endowment framing and growth targets and adds 'high degree of certainty'. Designers likely reward a precise definition of certainty, honest communication of uncertainty and restraint, not return-chasing. D7 should find how the 2021-22 winners funded the ten payments.
would_change_detail: Where Final Report pages go: less projection theatre, more on the certainty definition and co-sponsor communication.
north_star: Aligns our emphasis with what this year's case, and so Laura, is really asking for.

text: Should the fundraising draft be written as a 2031 document with clearly labelled illustrative figures from today's projection, or as a template with blanks?
anchor_quote: "Each team must also draft part of Laura’s fundraising materials describing this potential contribution for prospective co-sponsors." (case p.4 L123-124)
hypothesis: GUESS: It is used in 2031 but written in 2026. Blanks are lifeless; invented 'actual' 2031 numbers would be fabrication. Write it as a 2031 draft with every figure labelled as an illustration from the median case, plus one line on how the figures update. Choose which 'part' to write (probably her financial-commitment paragraph). Students write it themselves (R-W26); confirm against the Nov 9 instructions.
would_change_detail: The form and labelling of the Final Report fundraising draft.
north_star: A usable draft she could imagine sending is the clearest proof we built it for her.

text: What do the two official 2026-27 documents missing from the repo (the 5-page Investment Competition Guide and the Competition Phases Infographic, linked from the public SMApply 'guide' page) add to or change in our Phase A conclusions?
anchor_quote: Guide p.5: "You may identify decisions you would make differently, but you may not redesign your strategy after observing the results."
hypothesis: GUESS: they add few new facts but change three things. (1) Pre-commitment in the IPS becomes explicit. (2) Trade notes get four role words: growth, liquidity, risk management, future funding. (3) 'risk tolerance' and 'tradeoffs' are named, so the IPS should state both. Evidence: https://upenn.box.com/shared/static/b9kh53xila9czkyznk1xv5yegl3snlc1.pdf and .../l2p0l26svbbptmcizhmswyq5f7rbyp44.pdf, both reached via https://wghsinvcomp.smapply.us/res/p/guide/ (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, 2026-09-27; SHA-256 values in the working file).
would_change_detail: Add both PDFs to competition/official/2026_27 and the manifest, then re-run A1's cross-document X-checks against them. The IPS and TN checklists then take the Guide's wording.
north_star: A team that reads every official page designs to the judges' own checklist; most teams never open the Guide.

text: Should every WInS trade note written from now on name its role in the Guide's four words (growth, liquidity, risk management, future funding) and link it to one dated cash flow of Laura's?
anchor_quote: Guide p.3: "the Trading Note should capture the reasoning behind the decision, including its alignment with your strategy, the supporting research or analysis, and its expected role in growth, liquidity, risk management, or future funding."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Notes cannot be edited, and any three can become the Oct 23 submission. Wharton's own sample note already has a purpose, a link to Laura and a named risk. Guide PDF (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: A note template used from the next trade. It holds a role word, the cash flow served (2033-42 payments / 2031 range / 2033 facility), the research fact and the named risk.
north_star: Every trade visibly traces to one of Laura's dated needs, which stock-picking teams cannot show.

text: Should the three Trading Notes deliberately cover the three official verbs 'supported/tested/refined', so that at least one real, rule-triggered trade before Oct 23 tests or refines the strategy?
anchor_quote: Case: "This shows how selected investment decisions reflected, tested, or refined the team’s developing strategy."
hypothesis: GUESS: three initial 'buy' notes show only 'supported'. A duration-hedge rebalance or a correction after learning a WInS rule shows thinking. It must be triggered by a pre-stated rebalancing rule, not traded for the notes; the FAQ warns against 'a lot of buying and selling'. Infographic: 'supported, tested, or refined the developing strategy' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: Write a rebalancing or trigger rule into the WInS notes now, and plan which decisions are candidates for the Oct 23 notes.
north_star: Shows a firm that updates on evidence, which a statistics-trained client values.

text: Does this year's Trading Notes Analysis still expect one stock, one ETF and one team choice, as last season's reports show, or may all three notes be bond or ETF trades?
anchor_quote: TN guide: "Successful investing is not simply about selecting individual stocks." / "select three investment decisions that best illustrate your team’s strategic thinking."
hypothesis: GUESS: there is no asset-type quota this year, so a lock-early book with few or no single stocks is fine. Last season a team report showed 'ETF Selected: SPY / Stock Selected: AAPL / Team Choice: GOOGL' (Scribd 980515751, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). Confirm on the logged-in SMApply TN form.
would_change_detail: Whether the WInS book needs any single-stock position at all to satisfy the notes.
north_star: Freed from a stock-pick ritual, every note can serve Laura's promise.

text: Wharton cut WInS cash from $500k to exactly Laura's $300k deposit and replaced 'WInS can only accurately assess short-term investments' with 'The WInS portfolio represents each team's implementation'. So should the WInS book show her Year-1 (2027) portfolio rather than the post-2028 target mix?
anchor_quote: Case: "The WInS portfolio represents each team’s implementation of its investment strategy during the competition."
hypothesis: GUESS: WInS is sized to deposit 1, so a Year-1 mirror (~97% liability bonds plus a small growth surplus) is the most literal 'implementation' and the easiest to defend in the IPS. A ~65/35 post-2028 mirror is defensible only if labelled as the target after the second deposit. NEW evidence against the open item in brief section 9: the 2025-26 case said '10 weeks on WInS can only accurately assess the performance of short-term investments' (Scribd copy, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED), and the 2026-27 Guide p.3 says 'your portfolio provides evidence of the decisions your team made' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: The WInS target weights now, plus one IPS/FR sentence saying which book WInS represents.
north_star: Judges see Laura's own first-year portfolio, not a generic model.

text: Did Wharton drop the approved list and allow 'Any Government/Treasury Bonds from any exchange' so that liability-matching instruments can be used, and which 2032-2042 maturities does the WInS bond list actually offer?
anchor_quote: SMApply FAQ: "Any Government/Treasury Bonds from any exchange available on WInS."
hypothesis: GUESS: the opening was deliberate. In 2025-26 the rule was 'ETFs and treasury bonds from the approved lists' (2025 WInS User Guide, VERIFIED-PRIMARY [PRIOR]), and that list had no defined-maturity or zero-coupon funds. The WInS drop-down may still list only some maturities, so check inside WInS.
would_change_detail: Whether the WInS Treasury sleeve uses individual bonds matched to payment dates or a two-fund duration mix.
north_star: Using the tools Wharton just opened shows we understood why they opened them.

text: Why did Wharton remove all values language this year (2025-26: 'Every dollar invested reflects MTWB's values'), and should our deliverables say explicitly that no values screen is applied, or stay silent?
anchor_quote: R-AN34: 0 hits for "ESG", "values", "impact", "sustainab" across the four official documents.
hypothesis: GUESS: removed on purpose, to keep the case about certainty. The recommendation has three parts: (a) stay silent in the IPS; (b) add one FR clause saying no screen the case does not name was imposed, with the reason (cost and tracking of a fixed liability); (c) never use her identity as a reason for a screen. Evidence: 2025-26 values sentence (Scribd copy, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED); 2024-25 impact quote (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, Wharton 2024-25 case page); a 2025-26 team's 'Enhanced ESG' thematic portfolio (Scribd 977481046, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED).
would_change_detail: One FR client-knowledge clause, plus the decision to hold no thematic or ESG sleeve in WInS.
north_star: We respect Laura's actual stated wishes rather than importing last year's template.

text: How many teams will reuse last season's growth-target template (stock picks, return targets, thematic funds), and what one visible feature of our deliverables proves we did not?
anchor_quote: 2025-26 case copy: "Connor would like to grow his initial MTWB investment of $500,000 into a fund of at least $1.5 million" (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED)
hypothesis: GUESS: most teams will. That goal implies about 11.6% a year (DERIVED), and last year's sample reports lead with tech stocks and '9% annualized returns' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). The visible difference: the pitch opens with the promise already bought (price and date) and gives no return target.
would_change_detail: A specification for the elevator pitch: it must contain who it serves, the promise, how it is secured, and what the surplus is for.
north_star: The direct answer to 'why us': we solved her case, not last year's.

text: Since last season's 'compelling and clever pitch' and 'win Connor's business' became 'authentic team voice' and 'recommendations that can earn her confidence', should our deliverables drop pitch devices in favour of adviser-style disclosure?
anchor_quote: Criteria: "presents recommendations that can earn her confidence" / "in an authentic team voice"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Replace metaphors and branded framework names with: what we know, what we assume, what could go wrong. Evidence: 2025-26 case copy, 'How will you create a compelling and clever pitch to convince Connor to choose your strategy?' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED).
would_change_detail: The style checklist for the IPS and the Final Report.
north_star: Laura chooses the firm she can trust, not the one with the best slogan.

text: Since the 'portfolio manager ... makes the final investment decisions' sentence is copied word for word from the 2025-26 case, and the firm is now nameless and sizeless, should the IPS spend any words on governance beyond rules that any reviewer can apply?
anchor_quote: Case: "Your portfolio manager (your team’s teacher/advisor who makes the final investment decisions for your firm’s portfolio)"
hypothesis: GUESS: it is boilerplate (the identical sentence appears in the 2025-26 copy, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). The 2025-26 firm description ('$100,000,000') and the 2024-25 firm name ('WGAM', VERIFIED-PRIMARY) were dropped. So: no org chart in the IPS; pre-committed rules instead; fee and reporting terms stated in the FR as ASSUMPTIONs (CFA Asset Manager Code F.4.d).
would_change_detail: The IPS word budget: zero words on who decides, more on which rules decide.
north_star: Rules Laura can check herself beat an authority she must trust.

text: Why does every official document list 'liquidity' when the case removes every liquidity need before 2033, and what should 'liquidity' mean in our IPS?
anchor_quote: Case: "Laura’s living expenses and short-term financial needs will be covered by income and financial resources outside the portfolio."
hypothesis: GUESS: here liquidity means (a) paying each Jan 1 payment 2033-42 on time from maturing bonds and (b) turning the growth sleeve into cash for the 2033 facility without a forced sale. There is no cash buffer before 2033, and a generic 'keep 5% cash' signals the case was not read. The Guide p.2 lists 'liquidity needs' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: The IPS definition of liquidity, plus the WInS cash weight (small and explained).
north_star: Shows we read her case line by line.

text: Which rules must the IPS pre-commit so the Final Report can 'evaluate' them without 'redesign[ing] your strategy after observing the results'?
anchor_quote: Guide p.5: "A long-term strategy may include planned adjustments as funding dates approach, but it should not be rewritten simply because markets move or hindsight reveals a different outcome."
hypothesis: GUESS: one-line rules for six events. (1) Rates move before the Jan 2027 purchase. (2) The 2028 deposit is smaller or late. (3) How the 2031 range is set. (4) The 2033 order of use: reserve including payment 1, then facility, then flexibility. (5) Sleeve rebalancing bands. (6) Money left over after 2033. The Final Report then says each rule 'fired as written'. Guide (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: The IPS content checklist: which six rules appear, one line each.
north_star: A firm that commits in advance protects Laura from its own hindsight.

text: The case gives no 2027 prices ('Year 0 ... before any money has been invested'), so which price date should the projections use, and how should that assumption be stated?
anchor_quote: Case: "Year 0 is 2026, the present, before any money has been invested."
hypothesis: GUESS: base on the latest official curve (2026-09-25: $292,264), labelled as an ASSUMPTION. Show the ±50bp band ($278,198-$307,135) and P(cost > $300k) ≈ 24% (ASSUMPTION model, F-112), and link to pre-committed rule (1).
would_change_detail: The FR assumptions table: base cost plus band, and one sentence on the purchase date.
north_star: Honest about the one price we cannot know yet.

text: Does 'objectives that reflect ... her passion for innovation' justify any innovation, tech or AI tilt, or does 'innovation' describe the residency itself?
anchor_quote: Case: "Laura has identified several long-term financial objectives that reflect both her entrepreneurial mindset and her passion for innovation."
hypothesis: GUESS: it describes her goals, not asset choices (the only use of 'innovation' in the case, word check VERIFIED-REPO-FILE). Many teams will buy AI or tech names on this word. Any tech weight should come only from broad-market weights.
would_change_detail: Growth-sleeve composition: no thematic tech tilt in WInS or in the plan.
north_star: We invest for her goals, not for her adjectives.

text: Why may co-sponsors fund the facility but not Laura's commitment, and should the fundraising draft lead with the fully pre-funded ten years of operations as the credibility anchor, with the facility range second?
anchor_quote: Case: "Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement."
hypothesis: GUESS: funders least like to fund operations (BS-17, SSIR 2009, VERIFIED-PRIMARY via A3). Laura covering them removes their biggest worry, so pre-funded operations are the anchor and the facility range is the invitation.
would_change_detail: The order and emphasis of the FR fundraising draft: operations secured first, facility range second.
north_star: Turns a case rule into Laura's strongest fundraising fact.

text: Will co-sponsors read 'operating reserve' in its nonprofit sense (a few months of expenses held by the organisation) rather than the case's ten-year personal set-aside, and should the fundraising draft use a different, plainer label?
anchor_quote: Case: "This set-aside is called the operating reserve."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, there is a risk of misreading. The nonprofit norm is 'above 25% (equivalent to three months) is better' (https://www.nonprofitaccountingbasics.org/internal-reporting/operating-reserve-ratio, VERIFIED-PRIMARY 2026-09-27), so the case reserve is about 40 times that norm. Keep the case term in the IPS/FR, and describe it plainly for co-sponsors. The residency may still need its own short-term reserve, outside Laura's commitment.
would_change_detail: The vocabulary of the co-sponsor draft, plus one FR note distinguishing Laura's set-aside from the residency's own reserve.
north_star: We speak the co-sponsors' language on Laura's behalf.

text: Why does the case name an 'endowment' next to the contingency fund, and how should money left over after 2033 be described so co-sponsors do not assume a perpetual fund for years after 2042?
anchor_quote: Case: "Teams are not expected to determine the size or investment composition of a separate contingency fund or endowment."
hypothesis: GUESS: the designers expected teams to propose endowments. Describe leftovers as uncommitted flexibility governed by a rule, with no promise beyond 2042.
would_change_detail: The FR and fundraising-draft wording on leftover money and the post-2042 boundary.
north_star: Prevents an accidental overpromise, which the case warns against.

text: Does 'recommend the dollar range Laura should communicate' in 2031 ask for a range computed today (a 5-7-year forecast) or a rule Laura applies in 2031 (a 2-year forecast), and how do we give both without looking evasive?
anchor_quote: Case: "In 2031, however, the value of her portfolio in 2033 remains uncertain." / "Teams must recommend the dollar range Laura should communicate"
hypothesis: GUESS: give both. First, a 2031 rule: floor = amount secured in a 2-year Treasury; top = a stated percentile. Second, today's projected range under that rule, e.g. 2031 floor median ≈ $165k (F-402, ASSUMPTION model) with its spread. The two views differ a lot in width.
would_change_detail: The FR headline range and how its width is explained (rule vs today's projection).
north_star: Gives Laura a method she can reuse in 2031, not a guess that ages.

text: Because Laura herself decides the 2033 contribution, can 'will fall within that range' be made partly a policy outcome (contribute at most the top, keep any excess as flexibility), so that the stated confidence depends only on the low end?
anchor_quote: Case: "state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. With a cap rule, 'above range' cannot happen by design, so confidence = P(available ≥ floor), which is near-certain with a bought floor (barring U.S. default). Disclose that the top is a cap Laura chooses, not a forecast.
would_change_detail: The stated confidence percentage and the definition sentence for the range in the FR.
north_star: A confidence statement that a statistics-trained client would accept.

text: Given that the payments are fixed nominal amounts, where exactly must inflation appear (real value of projections, facility costs, real erosion of the $50k), and should every co-sponsor dollar figure be tagged as 2033 dollars or today's dollars?
anchor_quote: Case: "the effect of inflation on portfolio projections and facility costs"
hypothesis: GUESS: inflation belongs in three places. (1) Real values beside the nominal projections. (2) Facility costs at the Taiwan construction trend of ~3.5%/yr since 2021, not the 6.5% spike (F-508). (3) The fixed $50k's real erosion: $42.1k in 2033 and $33.7k in 2042 at 2.5% (F-114, in 2026 dollars). The 2024-25 case also flagged cost drift: 'material costs and market dynamics are always changing' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: Dollar-date tags on every co-sponsor figure, plus a real/nominal column in the FR projections.
north_star: Shows Laura what her money will actually buy in Taiwan.

text: How do we express 'financial flexibility' as a rule or ratio (for example, a share of the post-reserve surplus kept uncommitted until project milestones) instead of a contingency fund the case says we need not size?
anchor_quote: Case: "She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops."
hypothesis: GUESS: a share-based rule stated in the IPS and sized in the FR, tied to named project milestones.
would_change_detail: The flexibility share (%) in the FR, plus a one-line rule in the IPS.
north_star: Captures her own phrase, flexibility 'as the project develops', in a checkable rule.

text: With charts, citations and 'detailed financial calculations' excluded, which few numbers must the 500-word IPS still carry to be testable, and what counts as 'detailed'?
anchor_quote: IPS guide: "Focus on the strategy and decision-making framework that guide your portfolio rather than describing individual investments or presenting detailed financial calculations."
hypothesis: GUESS: carry 3-6 numbers (e.g. $50,000 × 10 from 2033, a funded-ratio test, a sleeve equity band, rebalancing bands, a flexibility share). Leave out tables, projections and the range.
would_change_detail: A list of the numbers allowed in the IPS draft.
north_star: Words alone prove the plan is checkable.

text: Which three tradeoffs should the IPS name explicitly, since the Guide, the Infographic and the FAQ all say strong teams explain 'reasoning, assumptions, and tradeoffs'?
anchor_quote: Infographic: "There is no single correct strategy. Strong teams explain the reasoning, assumptions, and tradeoffs behind their decisions."
hypothesis: GUESS: (a) certainty of the promise vs facility size; (b) sleeve growth vs a higher 2031 floor; (c) locking now vs waiting for rates. Each must say what Laura gives up. Infographic PDF (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: The IPS checklist: three named tradeoffs, each with its cost to Laura.
north_star: Shows Laura the choices were hers to see.

text: What makes a personal contribution 'meaningful' to co-sponsors when no facility cost exists: its dollar size, its share of Laura's own post-reserve assets, or how certain it is?
anchor_quote: Case: "A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura’s commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute."
hypothesis: GUESS: funders read a lead gift by commitment relative to capacity and by how firm it is. So present the floor as a share of what remains after the ten-year commitment is secured (needs D5 evidence).
would_change_detail: The framing of the fundraising draft: a share of capacity plus the certainty of the floor.
north_star: A contribution that is meaningful because it is certain, which matches her credibility.

text: Given that the FAQ still carries recycled text ('10 weeks of trading', 'long-term portion of your portfolio'), does 'Investments permitted (for BOTH contributions)' really limit Laura's long-term plan to instruments listed in WInS?
anchor_quote: SMApply FAQ: "Investments permitted (for BOTH contributions):" and "you are not trying to prove the worthiness of your long-term strategy through how your portfolio performs over 10 weeks of trading."
hypothesis: GUESS: 'BOTH' is probably a leftover. NEW evidence: trading this year is about 6 weeks, not 10 (FAQ, VERIFIED-PRIMARY), and the 2025-26 welcome email says 'Teams will have one portfolio' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED), which implies earlier multi-portfolio seasons. Safe course: name instrument types available in WInS, and mark any STRIPS for the real plan as not tradable in WInS.
would_change_detail: Whether the long-term plan in the FR may name STRIPS or other instruments not available in WInS.
north_star: Stay compliant without crippling the real-world plan.

text: Last season's written reports were screened by 'Wharton School student evaluators' plus 'a professional review panel of asset managers from Aberdeen Investments'; how much fixed-income precision and plain English should our written deliverables target?
anchor_quote: Wharton news (Jan 27, 2026): "with the help of our Wharton School student evaluators, as well as a professional review panel of asset managers from Aberdeen Investments in Philadelphia"
hypothesis: GUESS: two kinds of reader. A student screener needs plain English with one glossary line per term. A bond professional will check durations, cash-flow match and maturity dates, so errors are costly. Confirm whether the same set-up holds in 2026-27. Quote VERIFIED-PRIMARY.
would_change_detail: The depth of bond analysis and the glossary policy in the FR, plus a fact-check pass on every bond number.
north_star: Written for the people who actually choose the Top 50.

text: Which 'sources of uncertainty' should our deliverables name, and does the case's list of where the 2028 money comes from invite a deposit stress test despite 'will'?
anchor_quote: Guide p.3: "Study the Client Case Study, financial goals, future funding commitments, and sources of uncertainty."
hypothesis: GUESS: name five: markets; rates before 2027; the size and timing of the 2028 deposit; inflation and facility costs; the currency. Stress the deposit only as a labelled team scenario. Guide (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: The FR scenario set, plus one IPS sentence listing the named uncertainties.
north_star: Shows we understand her 2028 income comes from her own brand.

text: Why is the residency in Taiwan when the case gives Laura no link to Taiwan, and may we cite her public professional statement that she worked as a comic artist from Taipei as client knowledge?
anchor_quote: Case: "In 2033, Laura plans to establish a collaborative creative residency in Taiwan."
hypothesis: GUESS: a real professional link, not tokenism. Overachiever Magazine interview, 2021-03-15 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): "I’m currently in Taiwan, Taipei. My current day job is as a comic artist." Use at most one client-knowledge clause; the page also has personal material, which must not be used.
would_change_detail: One clause in the FR client-knowledge section (or none, if the team judges it too personal).
north_star: Shows research beyond the case, without using identity as decoration.

text: Was the $300,000 first deposit sized to be roughly the price of the ten payments at 2026 rates, so the IPS lock rule should read 'buy as much of the ladder as the 2027 deposit affords and complete it from the 2028 deposit' rather than rely on 'it fits inside $300k'?
anchor_quote: F-111: the same ladder priced on every 2026 curve date was 'Above $300k on 173 of 185 trading days; at or below $300k only on the 12 days since 2026-09-10'; the case PDF was created 2026-09-10 (case_register 1.1).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. A flat 5.09% makes $300k exactly buy the promise (DERIVED); at 4.0-4.5% it costs $317-333k (ASSUMPTION flat rates). The designers likely drafted when the ladder cost $302-325k, so our $7.7k cushion depends on a Sept-2026 rate peak (10y highest close since 2007, F-004). The rule should depend on rates and name the 2028 deposit as the completion source.
would_change_detail: IPS lock-rule wording becomes rate-conditional; WInS promise book sized as 'what $300k buys today' (~97%) with the gap stated; one TN reflection can say the rule was tested by rates.
north_star: Laura sees a plan that works in the world the case was written for, not one that needed lucky rates.

text: Should our narrative spine be 'the first deposit secures the promise; the second deposit and growth fund the facility and flexibility', which WInS cash (= deposit 1) seems to invite, and should the WInS book therefore mirror the Year-1 promise book?
anchor_quote: "The $300,000 is your team’s WInS simulator balance. The additional $150,000 contribution described in the Client Case Study will not be added to WInS." (R-W59); 2022 judge: "Cut slides, cut words, cut minutes" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, stated with the rate condition from the $300k-calibration question. WInS cash was $100k for 13 seasons, then $500k; this is the first time it equals a client deposit, and the calibration shows the tie is also economic. That settles the open 'Year-1 book vs post-2028 target' item in favour of Year 1 plus a small sleeve.
would_change_detail: WInS allocation mirrors the Year-1 book; the 50-word elevator pitch is built on 'two deposits, two jobs'.
north_star: The simplest true story of her money: each deposit has a job she can repeat to a co-sponsor.

text: Laura's case is the first in six seasons with no hobbies, family or city; did Wharton remove the 'hobby hooks' past teams turned into stock picks, and should we rule out every identity- or interest-themed security (Taiwan tilt, publishing, creator-economy themes)?
anchor_quote: Case word check: 0 hits for enjoy, love, free time, family, lives, partner (VERIFIED-REPO-FILE); 2024 Wharton news: "volleyball, a passion highlighted in Hilary Ash’s client profile that inspired great creativity among student teams’ competition investment strategies" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, deliberate. The 2021-22 and 2022-23 cases listed Peloton/yoga/wine and scuba/Muay Thai/yoga; a 2023-24 team bought Nike because it 'caters to Ms. Ash’s love of sports' (Teen Ink, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). Tailoring must now run through cash flows, constraints and professional mindset; drop the EWT/Taiwan tilt unless a cash-flow reason exists (none, the promise is USD).
would_change_detail: Drop themed positions from WInS now; the IPS gets one sentence on how we tailored (goals and cash flows, not tastes).
north_star: She is a person with a plan, not a theme; tailoring to her goals shows we listened.

text: The case is the first to say the client 'understands that investing involves uncertainty and periods of market volatility'; should our risk-tolerance statement and one Trading Note turn that into a stated sleeve drawdown she accepts while the payments carry no market risk?
anchor_quote: "Laura understands that investing involves uncertainty and periods of market volatility. Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career, she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance..." (case p.2; 'volatil' has 0 hits in the four earlier case texts).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Willingness is stated in the case, and ability is set by the promise. A number like 'the growth sleeve could fall about a third in a bad year; the ten payments would not change' turns an adjective into something she can hold us to. It also fixes Wharton's example note, which frames bonds as lowering volatility.
would_change_detail: A stated sleeve-drawdown number in the IPS risk section (sized by D3), plus one TN reflection explaining why hedge volatility is not risk to her promise.
north_star: It answers her own stated understanding of risk, not a generic questionnaire.

text: Laura is the first client in six seasons with a scheduled second contribution that depends on creative income; is a human-capital underweight (publishing, media) large enough to matter in a broad-index sleeve, or should we only state the link?
anchor_quote: "She will contribute an additional $150,000 at the beginning of 2028, using earnings from publishing advances, speaking engagements, licensing, and other entrepreneurial ventures." (R-C27); 2024 judge: "take a look at this person holistically" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: publishing and media are well under 2% of a U.S. broad index (to verify), so an underweight adds trades for little protection. The real link is the equity market as a whole (wrong-way deposit risk). State it, do not trade it. New evidence: earlier clients had 'steady jobs and incomes' (2024-25) or retirement covered (2021-22, 2022-23).
would_change_detail: Keep or drop the human-capital underweight idea in WInS and the IPS; the sector weight number goes in the FR's holistic paragraph.
north_star: We see her whole financial life without adding complexity she pays for.

text: Wharton asked a ten-payment question in 2021 at a 1.48% 10-year yield, when pre-funding cost ~95% of face; should our IPS and FR say why locking Laura's promise is right now (it costs ~58% of face in 2026), so readers see a choice for this rate world, not a reflex for safety?
anchor_quote: 2021-22 case: "she wants to be able to offer the scholarship for at least 10 years. Should she keep $50,000 in cash? Should she invest in stocks that pay dividends? Another option?" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Jordan's ten $5k payments were worth ~$47.3k at the 2021-09-27 FRED curve (0.946 of face, ASSUMPTION par-as-zero); Laura's $292,264 (0.585). At a flat 1.48%, Laura's promise would cost ~$429k of her $450k. The case works only in a high-rate world: cash is impossible ($450k < $500k) and rates are the main variable.
would_change_detail: An IPS 'why now' clause, and an FR chart of the promise's cost against the yield, marking 2021 and 2026.
north_star: Laura sees we understood why her promise is affordable today, not only that it is safe.

text: Judges have named the same two gaps since 2024, the client's emotions in a downturn and the whole person; which pre-commitment rule in the IPS answers the first, and which sentence answers the second?
anchor_quote: 2024 finale: judges urged teams "to consider behavioral finance and their clients’ emotions during a market downturn" and "When analyzing someone’s investments, take a look at this person holistically" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: (a) one line: a fall in the growth sleeve never changes the promise book, and we rebalance inside bands rather than sell into a fall; it must be pre-committed because the Guide forbids redesign after results. (b) One sentence joining her 2028 income, her credibility and the portfolio. Neither is in the current strategy.
would_change_detail: IPS gains a behavioural pre-commitment rule and a holistic sentence; FR gets a 'what Laura sees in a 2029 bear market' scenario.
north_star: She chooses the firm that has already planned how she will feel on a bad day.

text: With a statistics-degree client and an academic director who holds an M.A. in Statistics and runs the Wharton Financial Analytics Initiative, what would a statistically trained reader reject on sight in our certainty definition and 2031 confidence statement?
anchor_quote: Case: "She graduated in 2018 with a degree in Statistics & Information Decisions Management" (R-C12); main page: "his M.A. in Statistics and Ph.D. in Economics from the University of California at Berkeley" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: a bare '95%' with no model; calling a model probability a 'confidence'; a two-ended range whose top was never tested; i.i.d. lognormal returns presented as fact; no sample size or seed. Fix: a four-line FR 'model card' plus the market-priced certainty definition already chosen. The reader profile is the new evidence; it raises the bar on method disclosure.
would_change_detail: FR gets a model-card box; the IPS certainty sentence names its test.
north_star: A statistics graduate trusts a firm whose numbers say what they are and are not.

text: The committed outflow grew from 50% of the client's money (Jordan) to 111% (Laura), and this is the first case with no return target; should the Final Report spend most of its analysis on funding reliability, the facility rule and the co-sponsor range rather than on security selection?
anchor_quote: "uses reasonable assumptions and projections to evaluate funding reliability, the facility contribution, and financial flexibility under varying market outcomes" (R-S26).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, roughly two-thirds on promise, facility and co-sponsors and one-third on implementation. Past finales celebrated 'stock-filtering algorithms' (2023) and 'customized algorithms, AI innovations, portfolio optimizations' (2025), so repeat-school teams will over-weight security selection.
would_change_detail: Page allocation in the FR and the order of topics in the IPS.
north_star: Her problem is a promise; the firm that spends its pages on her problem is the one she picks.

text: The case vocabulary moved ('certainty' 0 to 6 hits, 'co-sponsor' 0 to 9, 'flexib' 0 to 5, 'stock' 2-4 to 0, 'pitch/convince/win' up to 8 to 0); should we adopt the new words, ban the old ones, and use the word table in the FR Articulation section as evidence of how we read the case?
anchor_quote: "Presents a compelling, well-organized narrative in an authentic team voice" (R-S28); 2025-26 case: "As you strive to win Connor’s business ... compelling and clever pitch" (Scribd copy, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. 'Beat the market', 'alpha' or 'win her business' read as last season's template. The word table is an honest process artefact for Articulation and costs one sentence or one small chart. New versus B1b's tone question: the counts make it a checklist.
would_change_detail: A use/ban vocabulary checklist for all three deliverables; a possible FR chart in Articulation.
north_star: We speak the language of her case (certainty, flexibility, credibility).

text: The 2026-27 Guide now defines the whole competition as helping a client 'meet future cash-flow needs'; should our first FR exhibit be a dated cash-flow calendar 2027-2042, and should every Trading Note name the dated cash flow it serves?
anchor_quote: Guide p.1: "designed to help a client achieve specific financial goals and meet future cash-flow needs" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY), versus the main page's "designed to help the client achieve their objectives" (R-W5).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The Guide is written generically ('a client') and so is likely the competition's frame from now on. A one-row-per-year table is the cheapest way to score on 'disciplined planning across Laura's changing time horizons and cash-flow needs'. New versus B1b's note-tagging question: the Guide's opening sentence.
would_change_detail: FR exhibit 1 = cash-flow calendar; TN habit: each note names its date; IPS uses 'cash-flow needs'.
north_star: Laura's plan is a calendar of promises; showing the calendar shows we understood her.

text: Past clients said what won them over (feeling 'seen', plans 'not just about the numbers'); with no personal hooks in Laura's case, which case-stated facts about how she thinks should every recommendation visibly mirror so she feels understood rather than analysed?
anchor_quote: 2022: Jordan "had never felt more “seen” in her life"; 2025: Ayoola: "not just about the numbers, but about understanding and connecting with people" (both VERIFIED-PRIMARY); case: "Thoughtful financial planning and long-term investing will play an important role in turning those ideas into reality."
hypothesis: GUESS: five mirrors, all from the case: ideas become reality through planning; statistics (certainty defined and tested); 'thoughtful risks' (risk only where the promise is safe); product manager (dated milestones 2027/2028/2031/2033 with decision rules); a public voice whose credibility is an asset (nothing overpromised). Any tailored claim that cites none of these is decoration.
would_change_detail: A checklist for the IPS client paragraph and each TN reflection's 'how it serves Laura' line.
north_star: She recognises her own way of thinking in our plan.

text: The pull quote is unattributed while every past case quoted the client in the first person, and last year's client framed success as confidence plus humility; is the case about turning private conviction into public credibility, and should the fundraising draft use the quote at all?
anchor_quote: "The only person who needs to believe in something is yourself." (R-C21, no attribution); Barwin (2026): "approach every problem with confidence that you can figure it out, and humility to know that you don’t have all the answers" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes to the theme. Not found on the Wharton Magazine, Overachiever, Mochi or Wikipedia pages (grep NO), so it is PARAPHRASE-UNVERIFIED as hers. Do not quote it as her words. Show conviction as money already committed ('ten years of operations funded') and humility as a range with a stated floor.
would_change_detail: Whether to quote the pull quote; the structure of the FR fundraising draft (conviction = funded promise, humility = floor plus range).
north_star: We turn what she believes into what others can check, which is what she needs in 2031.

text: Would framing the 2031 range as 'committed (already bought) plus stretch (with a stated probability)', in the language of her case-stated product-manager career, be more credible to co-sponsors than percentile language?
anchor_quote: "before beginning her career as a product manager in the technology industry" (R-C12); "Rather than promising one exact amount, she wants to communicate a credible range" (R-C67).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes for co-sponsors. Committed-vs-stretch is plain English and matches the floor-plus-upside design. It is professional, not identity, so it passes the tokenism rule. Percentiles belong in the FR method box.
would_change_detail: Wording and structure spec for the FR fundraising draft's range statement.
north_star: She reads her range in words she already uses to make promises.

text: All six clients pay something forward, and Laura's residency serves 'artists, writers, designers, entrepreneurs, and educators', her own roles; are the residents third parties who rely on the ten payments, and does that raise the bar for certainty and for how we describe it to co-sponsors?
anchor_quote: "Establishing the residency will require funding for the facility as well as reliable support for its early operations." (R-C41); Jordan: "What drives me is opening doors or creating opportunities for others like me." (VERIFIED-PRIMARY)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Residents plan their lives around a place, so a broken operating promise harms third parties. That is a Laura-specific reason for market-priced certainty beyond the case's 'must', and the strongest co-sponsor line: running costs, which funders fear, are already secured (BS-17).
would_change_detail: IPS objective sentence on why certainty; FR fundraising lead.
north_star: We protect the people her residency serves, which is why she is building it.

text: The case opens with Laura's belief that 'stories have the power to change how people see the world', and her first work answered misinformation; should the co-sponsor draft be a short story backed by numbers (problem, promise, proof, range) rather than a table-first term sheet?
anchor_quote: "Laura Gao believes stories have the power to change how people see the world." (R-C9); criterion 5: "communicates Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors" (R-S28).
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, with care. A four-beat story, each beat carrying one verified number. The tokenism risk is low because this is her case-stated belief about communication, not her identity. The failure mode is book-title puns, which the field will overuse.
would_change_detail: Structure of the FR fundraising draft; the Creativity-criterion device.
north_star: She will recognise a firm that tells the truth as a story, the way she does.

text: Top-50 lists show many client-themed team names, and a 2024 semifinal judge praised the ability to 'connect the client's objectives to an investment strategy'; under this year's 'authentic team voice', which creative element is authentic for us and which is decoration?
anchor_quote: 2024 semifinal judge: "The one thing that stood out to me was the ability to connect the client’s objectives to an investment strategy." (VERIFIED-PRIMARY); 2026 Top 50 includes "End Zone Equity" and "Lumen Field Investments".
hypothesis: GUESS: creativity that carries analysis is authentic: the 2021-vs-2026 cost-of-the-promise chart, or one Future Fund/superannuation analogy if it earns its place. Book-title themes are decoration. The judge said 'objectives', not hobbies.
would_change_detail: Choice of the FR's single creative device.
north_star: Our creativity is about her problem, so it reads as ours and as hers.

text: How did the 2021-22 finalists fund Jordan's ten scholarship payments (cash, dividend stocks, bonds), and does that show readers accept an answer suited to its rate regime, so a Treasury match in 2026 will not look 'too simple'?
anchor_quote: 2022 finale: teams showcased "client-focused talk of dividends and growth stocks, ESG and risk management" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
hypothesis: GUESS: they mostly used dividend and growth stocks, since there was nothing worth locking at 0-1.5%. If so, the FR adds a one-line 'alternatives rejected': cash (cannot reach $500k from $450k), dividend stocks (dividends cut in 2008 and 2020; to verify), growth-first (brief section 8).
would_change_detail: FR 'alternatives considered' sentence; confidence in keeping the core simple.
north_star: Shows Laura we tested the obvious answers and chose the one that fits her year.

text: The 2024-25 case wrote '$10,000 USD' for a Nigerian project, while the 2026-27 case names no currency for a Taiwan project; is currency a deliberate simplification (one disclosure line) rather than a hidden test (a modelled TWD scenario)?
anchor_quote: 2024-25 case: "Ladi believes it will cost about $10,000 USD per housing unit; however, material costs and market dynamics are always changing." (VERIFIED-PRIMARY)
hypothesis: GUESS: simplification. Last year USD was named because costs were given; this year no costs are given ('not expected to estimate that cost'). Keep TWD to a US$ label and one purchasing-power sentence. What is new versus brief section 8 item 15 is the prior-case contrast.
would_change_detail: A cap on FR words about TWD (about one sentence); no TWD positions in WInS.
north_star: We handle the Taiwan detail with care but keep her plan simple.

text: Since Wharton replaced 'shape the winning investment strategy', 'compelling and clever pitch' and 'would win him/her over as a client' with 'develop the investment strategy that Laura ultimately chooses' and 'recommendations that can earn her confidence', should every deliverable aim to earn trust rather than to persuade?
anchor_quote: Case 2026-27: "Your team hopes to develop the investment strategy that Laura ultimately chooses"; 2025-26 case (Wharton page source): "Your team hopes to shape the winning investment strategy that Connor and the Make the World Better foundation ultimately choose"; old criterion: "would win him/her over as a client"; 2026-27: "presents recommendations that can earn her confidence"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The persuasion scaffolding was removed deliberately, so trust signals count: claims stated with their assumptions, honest uncertainty, each note naming its own risk, and no superlatives or claims about rival teams. Evidence: 2025-26 case and old judging page read from Wharton's own page source through the REST interface (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, 2026-09-27).
would_change_detail: Tone rules for TN reflections, the 50-word pitch and the IPS: no 'best', 'optimal', 'guaranteed' or 'unlike other teams'; every claim carries its basis. The North Star is restated as 'the plan she can trust'.
north_star: Laura does not choose the most persuasive firm; she chooses the one whose claims hold up.

text: What will a semifinal reader look for first, given that Wharton's 2026-27 Guide never says 'choose' or 'win' and asks teams to explain 'why your strategy is appropriate for the client'?
anchor_quote: Guide p.5: "Your focus now shifts to evaluating your implementation, reflecting on what you learned, and explaining why your strategy is appropriate for the client."
hypothesis: GUESS: first, whether the team has found Laura's binding constraint (a fixed nominal promise no one else may fund); second, whether each decision follows from it. So each TN reflection and the pitch should name that constraint in the first clause. Guide read 2026-09-27 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY); the word check found no 'choose', 'win' or 'pitch' in the Guide.
would_change_detail: Order of content in each TN reflection and in the IPS pitch: constraint first, instrument second.
north_star: A firm that names her real constraint in its first sentence shows it listened.

text: Wharton's recent pull quotes state each season's value theme; does 'The only person who needs to believe in something is yourself' signal self-reliance, so that the ten payments she alone must fund are secured by her, while co-sponsors are invited to believe only in the facility?
anchor_quote: "The only person who needs to believe in something is yourself." / "Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Earlier seasons' quotes match their themes: 2024-25 "I want to feel like I’m making an impact" for an impact-led case; 2025-26 "Wharton made me think more about the sustainability of a nonprofit, and the importance of building strong partnerships" (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, Wharton page source). Read this way, private conviction = the promise she funds herself, and public proof = a range others can rely on.
would_change_detail: IPS central idea (prompt 1) and the order of the FR fundraising draft; the TN frame 'secure what only Laura can promise'. Attribution must be checked first (next question).
north_star: A plan built on her own stated principle, that the promise rests on her alone, is one she would see as hers.

text: Until the case pull quote is traced to a primary source, should our deliverables attribute it to the case profile rather than to Laura, even though Wharton's past cases printed pull quotes as the client's own words?
anchor_quote: Case p.1 sidebar: "The only person who needs to believe in something is yourself." (no attribution line in the text layer)
hypothesis: GUESS: probably her words, given the house pattern in 2022-23, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). But two web searches and greps of about ten interview pages found no primary source (2026-09-27), so it stays PARAPHRASE-UNVERIFIED. Safe wording: 'the case profile's quote'.
would_change_detail: Attribution wording wherever the quote appears in TN, IPS or FR.
north_star: Getting her words exactly right is the smallest proof that we will get her money right.

text: Laura's one documented career 'thoughtful risk' was leaving a steady tech job only after a book deal was secured; can the IPS use this 'floor first, then leap' pattern as evidence for 'lock the promise, then take risk with the surplus'?
anchor_quote: Case: "Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career, she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance between pursuing growth and protecting the capital required for her goals."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, once, labelled INTERPRETATION. Inverse (2022-03-07, VERIFIED-PRIMARY article text, a journalist's paraphrase): "Gao had misgivings about leaving a steady job in tech for life as an artist ... So when she got the book deal with HarperCollins, she gave Twitter her notice." Do not over-read one anecdote, and use no private detail.
