would_change_detail: IPS risk-tolerance sentence (willingness high, capacity for the promise near zero); a Laura-specific reason in the TN for the Treasury-core trades.
north_star: Our structure is the one she has already used in her own career.

text: Given that Laura interned at a trading firm (Belvedere Trading) and at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, what would she reject on sight: unlabelled probabilities, undisclosed costs or fees, or a sales tone?
anchor_quote: Case: "She graduated in 2018 with a degree in Statistics & Information Decisions Management"; Poets&Quants 2018: "Trading Intern at Belvedere Trading in Chicago", "Policy Analyst Intern at Consumer Financial Protection Bureau"
hypothesis: GUESS: all three. Every probability must name its model (or be replaced by 'bought, not forecast'). Costs must appear: WInS commissions now, a fee assumption in the FR (BS-01). The tone should follow the CFA Code's disclosure standard. Evidence: Poets&Quants profile, read via the publisher API post 11618 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, 2026-09-27).
would_change_detail: Add a cost and fee disclosure line to the FR projections with a Laura-specific reason; keep % claims out of the TN unless their basis is shown.
north_star: A client who has seen finance from the trading desk and the regulator trusts the firm that discloses first.

text: Because Laura taught financial literacy to high school students and the case calls her an educator, should each key concept (the certainty definition, the 2031 range) come with a one-line plain-English version she could repeat to a co-sponsor?
anchor_quote: Criterion 5: "communicates Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors"; Poets&Quants 2018: "I taught web development and financial literacy to high school students in West Philadelphia"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Wharton chose a client-educator for a high-school financial-literacy competition, and a concept she can teach is one she can defend in 2031. Evidence: Poets&Quants 2018 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: A D9 check that every technical term in the IPS has a plain version; the FR carries a student-written 'how Laura would say it' line for the certainty definition and the range.
north_star: She chooses the plan she can explain to others herself.

text: Laura once built a case competition around the client's own 'problem areas'; should our IPS and Final Report be organised one to one around the case's five required tests and the IPS guide's five clarity items?
anchor_quote: Case: "Each team must develop and justify an investment strategy that:" (five tests); Wharton Magazine 2017-10-30: "Gao asked city officials what problem areas they needed help with, and these problem areas became the basis for the case competition’s four subtopics"
hypothesis: GUESS: FR yes, one section or table row per test in the case's order; IPS no headings (R-I29), but each test answered by an identifiable sentence. Wharton Magazine quote verified verbatim with fetch_text --grep (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: FR table of contents; IPS paragraph checklist before Nov 6.
north_star: A client who has designed a case reads for 'did they answer my problems', and ours visibly does.

text: This is the first archived Wharton case with explicit certainty, volatility and uncertainty language, and the Guide adds 'management of risk and uncertainty'; must the IPS state Laura's risk tolerance in two parts, willingness versus capacity?
anchor_quote: Case: "Laura understands that investing involves uncertainty and periods of market volatility." Guide p.5: "The competition recognizes ... management of risk and uncertainty"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The archive word check (2017-18 to 2025-26 case pages) finds 0 hits for 'certain', 'volatil' and 'uncertain', and only 2020-21 'riskiness' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). The IPS should say willingness is high, capacity is zero for the promise and moderate for the surplus, and that the equity weight follows from this. New evidence on the open sleeve-weight item.
would_change_detail: IPS risk sentence; FR explanation of why the sleeve equity weight is what it is.
north_star: Separating what she is willing to risk from what she cannot afford to lose is the core of being understood.

text: Since the ten-payment ladder cost more than $300,000 on 173 of 185 trading days in 2026, and fell below that only on 2026-09-10 (the day the case PDF was created), did the designers intend the promise to absorb nearly all the money, and should the IPS make 'top up from the 2028 deposit' the base rule rather than a contingency?
anchor_quote: F-111: the same ladder was "Above $300k on 173 of 185 trading days"; case_register 1.1: case PDF "created 2026-09-10 15:19"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. At flat 3.5/4.0/4.5/5.0% the 2027 cost is $350k/$333k/$317k/$303k (ASSUMPTION arithmetic, computed 2026-09-27). So a full lock with the first deposit was probably not feasible at design time, and today's surplus is partly a gift of September 2026 yields. NEW relative to brief section 9 ('rule if rates fall'): design-time calibration evidence.
would_change_detail: IPS: state long-rungs-first plus a 2028 top-up as the base rule; FR sentence that the current surplus partly reflects unusually high yields; D1/D3 re-run the surplus at the 2026-average and Jun-30 curves.
north_star: A plan that also works in the rate world the designers probably had in mind is robust, not lucky.

text: Since the 2020-21 case spelled out a background-to-portfolio link ('cosmopolitan upbringing ... geographic diversity') and Laura's case states none, should we refuse to turn her biography (Wuhan, Texas, Taiwan residency) into investment tilts, and use the case's own wording for her degree?
anchor_quote: 2020-21 case: "Given his cosmopolitan upbringing, Florian expects some level of geographic diversity in his investments." 2026-27: no equivalent sentence; case degree: "Statistics & Information Decisions Management"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. When Wharton wants such a link it writes one, so the absence argues against tokenism. Any Taiwan exposure needs a cash-flow reason (NT$ costs), not biography. The degree wording differs across Poets&Quants ('Economics with a concentration in Business Analytics'), Wharton Magazine ('business analytics') and the case; the case wins. VERIFIED-PRIMARY for all three wordings.
would_change_detail: Drop or re-justify any EWT/Taiwan tilt in WInS and the IPS; fix the degree wording in all drafts.
north_star: Respecting her story means not using it as a stock-picking signal.

text: Given Wharton's guidance 'Don't use precious space repeating known facts about your client' and 'Don't just repeat the case study', how many of the IPS's 500 words should go to Laura's background, and which beyond-the-case facts earn a place?
anchor_quote: Old judging page: "Don’t use precious space repeating known facts about your client and defining concepts. However, it is okay to demonstrate that you understand your client beyond the case study." 2023-24 midterm: "Don’t just repeat the case study, show us that you have thought about how her personal circumstances will determine her financial needs."
hypothesis: GUESS: about 30-50 words, placed inside the rules rather than a biography paragraph. Only facts that change a decision earn a place: reputation-driven, uneven income (2028 deposit), quantitative training (certainty bought, not modelled), 'floor first'. Both old pages VERIFIED-PRIMARY via the Wharton REST interface.
would_change_detail: IPS word budget for client-specific reasoning (~30-50 of 500) and where it sits.
north_star: Showing that we understand how her life shapes her needs beats reciting her life.

text: Since the 2023-24 prompt 'Explain what makes your investment strategy unique compared to other teams' has been dropped, should our 50-word elevator pitch contain any comparison with other approaches?
anchor_quote: IPS guide: "Clearly communicate the central idea behind your approach and how it is designed to support your client’s financial goals and future funding needs." 2023-24: "Explain what makes your investment strategy unique compared to other teams in a maximum of 75 words."
hypothesis: GUESS: no. Spend the 50 words on the promise, the central rule, the growth-versus-protection balance and the link to the residency. Distinctiveness should be visible, not claimed. 2023-24 page VERIFIED-PRIMARY.
would_change_detail: A pitch checklist with no comparative claims.
north_star: She chooses the plan that talks about her, not about other teams.

text: In 2023-24 the Final Report's audience was the teacher-portfolio manager; with this year's audience unstated until Nov 9, whose voice and pronouns should the IPS use, given that it freezes first?
anchor_quote: 2023-24 deliverables page: "Final Report Audience: Your report should be directed to Wharton Global Asset Management’s (WGAM) portfolio manager (your team’s teacher/advisor)."
hypothesis: GUESS: write the IPS as the firm's policy for Laura (third person; 'the portfolio will ...'), decided under the students' framework, with no advisor decisions (real rules). This fits any likely FR audience. D10 re-checks on Nov 9. VERIFIED-PRIMARY (historical page).
would_change_detail: IPS voice and pronouns; the FR address line.
north_star: A policy written for her, in a consistent voice, reads as a firm she could hire.

text: The case says Laura 'has no shortage of ideas' but ties flexibility to the residency 'as the project develops'; should our flexibility rule reserve leftover money for the residency, the project she has chosen, unless Laura explicitly decides otherwise?
anchor_quote: Case: "Laura has no shortage of ideas for the future." / "committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The case ties flexibility to 'the project', and a client with many ideas benefits from a rule that protects the chosen project, with a documented override that only she can use. This differs from B1a Q22 (how to express flexibility): here the question is what flexibility is for.
would_change_detail: Purpose clause of the IPS flexibility rule; how the FR describes money left after 2033.
north_star: A firm that guards her chosen project against her many other good ideas is the one an idea-rich founder needs.

text: Every value word in the 2026-27 case describes Laura's work, not her money (2025-26 said 'Every dollar invested reflects MTWB's values'); should her values show up in how we communicate (accuracy, no overpromising) rather than in security selection?
anchor_quote: Case: "Originally intended as a response to misinformation and anti-Asian racism"; 2025-26 case: "Every dollar invested reflects MTWB’s values — community-first, locally rooted, and sustainability-minded."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The value that carries into finance is accuracy, applied to the co-sponsor range and the certainty definition, not to an ESG fund. The 2025-26 sentence is VERIFIED-PRIMARY. New angle beyond B1a Q16 / B1b Q7, which ask whether to mention the missing screen.
would_change_detail: One FR sentence (labelled INTERPRETATION) tying the range's honesty standard to her public work; no values screen in the IPS.
north_star: Honouring her values means not overpromising, which is exactly what her work fights.

text: Barwin's 2025-26 case quote about 'the sustainability of a nonprofit' and 'strong partnerships' reads like the brief for this year's design; should the fundraising draft present Laura's funded operating years as what makes the building sustainable, and invite co-sponsors as partners in the facility?
anchor_quote: Case: "Establishing the residency will require funding for the facility as well as reliable support for its early operations." 2025-26 case: "Wharton made me think more about the sustainability of a nonprofit, and the importance of building strong partnerships to keep the work going."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Funded operations lower the co-sponsor's biggest risk, an unfunded building. NEW relative to B1b Q15: primary evidence that this is the designers' through-line from last season (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: Order and framing of the FR fundraising draft: operations first, then the facility range, then the partnership invitation (students write it).
north_star: We turn her private promise into the public proof co-sponsors need.

text: Past clients praised teams that made them feel 'seen' (Jordan) and went beyond 'just ... the numbers' (Ayoola), but semifinal readers are not Laura; what written evidence shows those readers that the plan 'can earn her confidence'?
anchor_quote: 2022 finale: Jordan "had never felt more “seen” in her life as students worked to meet and exceed her specific financial goals"; 2025 finale, Ayoola: "not just about the numbers, but about understanding and connecting with people"
hypothesis: GUESS: traceability. A small FR table links each major decision to the case line or public professional fact behind it. No flattery or identity references. Both finale articles VERIFIED-PRIMARY.
would_change_detail: Add a 'decision → why it is hers' traceability table to the FR (not the IPS); every row is checked against the case.
north_star: A reader who is not Laura can see, row by row, why each choice is hers.

text: Should one clause of the fundraising draft cite Laura's record of building platforms and communities (The Sign.al; the city-backed Amazon HQ2 case competition) as evidence the residency will be run well, given the case says her contribution signals commitment and viability?
anchor_quote: Case: "A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura’s commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute."
hypothesis: GUESS: at most one clause, only if the draft needs it. The case asks for the part 'describing this potential contribution', so money comes first, and these were student-era projects that must not be overstated. Sources: Poets&Quants 2018 and Wharton Magazine 2017 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: At most one clause in the FR fundraising draft; otherwise omit.
north_star: Co-sponsors back founders with a record, and her record is building places where people explore their paths.

text: Does Laura's documented habit of keeping a daily 'comics diary' to see 'how far I'd come' give a Laura-specific reason for our dated decision log and the FR Articulation section, or would mentioning it be decoration?
anchor_quote: Wharton Magazine 2022-04-06: "Soon enough, I had a comics diary that I could not only decompress into, but also take pride in how far I’d come when I reread it."
hypothesis: GUESS: keep the dated log because the rules reward it (notes 'at the time it is made'); mention her habit in the FR only if a student honestly finds it meaningful, otherwise omit. Quote verified verbatim (VERIFIED-PRIMARY).
would_change_detail: Start a dated team decision diary now (WInS-now); the FR mention is optional.
north_star: A record of how our thinking changed is something she values in her own work.

text: Since 'Laura Gao believes stories have the power to change how people see the world' follows Wharton's house template ('Connor Barwin ... believes in the power of community'), should criterion 5's 'compelling narrative' be met with the plan's own 2027-2042 timeline story rather than book metaphors?
anchor_quote: Case: "Laura Gao believes stories have the power to change how people see the world." 2025-26 case: "Connor Barwin (WG’23) believes in the power of community."
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The narrative is what happens in 2027, 2028, 2031, 2033 and 2042 under good and bad markets, shown as one timeline chart in the FR. Book-title metaphors are what rivals will use (B7b). The template match is VERIFIED-PRIMARY.

The team is her own readership.

Counting on her earnings would rebuild, for the facility, the dependence we removed from the promise. Her income is upside.

Taiwan cultural-content agencies (UNVERIFIED) may fund translation and residencies. Low priority: this changes only the co-sponsor types addressed.

Do not name her banned book in a document written for her; keep the evidence in the team notes.

PW: 'fresh, frank, and tender' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Horn Book via Wikipedia: 'with insight and humor' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED for the original). Candour about uncertainty is the professional form of 'frank'.

north_star: A report that sounds like people she would want to work with, not a finance brochure.

text: What surplus buffer above 100% funded do pension practitioners require before calling a plan 'hibernated', and is Laura's 102.6% funded ratio (27bp cushion) enough to call the promise 'high certainty' before the 2028 deposit arrives?
anchor_quote: All ten payments must be funded by the investment portfolio with a high degree of certainty. (case p.3); funded ratio $300,000/$292,264 = 1.026 (F-117)
hypothesis: Guess: practitioners would call 102.6% 'funded but thin'. NISA (c.2021, VERIFIED-PRIMARY, nisa.com '95% is the new 105%') says plans 'greater than 95% funded' should hibernate and that a '105% funded plan has essentially no potential contributions (as measured at a 95% confidence level)', but those plans have sponsors; Laura has none after 2028. The 2028 deposit is the buffer that turns 'funded' into 'high certainty'.
would_change_detail: IPS certainty definition and FR evaluation: certainty = ladder bought AND a stated buffer (2028 deposit, then sleeve); possibly a stated buffer target number.
north_star: Shows Laura 'fully funded' was tested against how professionals define it, not merely declared.

text: Because the case bans outside money for the payments (including 'continued business income'), is Laura's sponsor backing nil after 2028, so that practitioner logic (UK 'employer covenant'; contrast with Australia's Future Fund) says the promise must be hedged, not invested for growth?
anchor_quote: Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. UK DB Funding Code para 29(a) (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, TPR Nov 2024): 'more risk can be allowed for where the scheme has access to sufficient employer cash flows'. Future Fund targets 'between four and five per cent above CPI' with the Commonwealth behind the pensions it pre-funds, and drawdowns start 'at least 2032–33' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, Treasurer's release) - the year Laura's payments start. Nobody stands behind Laura's promise: one plain reason to hedge.
would_change_detail: The IPS 'why this fits her' reason for hedging; an FR alternatives paragraph contrasting the Future Fund.
north_star: Explains why her plan follows from her one hard constraint rather than copying any famous fund; an Australian angle that earns its place.

text: Since the UK regulator treats a pension with a 10-year liability duration as 'significantly mature' and expects it to be at least 90% hedged, and Laura's promise has a duration of about 10 years from day one, should the team use this yardstick to justify full hedging in 2027 instead of the gradual glide path Wharton's Trading Note example implies?
anchor_quote: This trade supports our plan to balance continued growth with reliable future cash flows as the residency funding date approaches. (TN guide example)
hypothesis: Guess: yes, as FR evidence (not IPS jargon). TPR code para 22(a): 'For schemes with no cash balance benefits, the duration is 10 years'; para 20: hedging 'of at least 90%' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Laura's spot duration is 10.16y (F-105), 9.90y at 2027 (F-103). The UK uses its own funding basis, so claim 'about 10 years, at the threshold'.
would_change_detail: Confirms hedge-now over a calendar glide path; adds an FR sentence explaining the departure from Wharton's example.
north_star: An outside authority reaches the same answer as our model - the kind of confirmation a statistics graduate trusts.

text: Should the IPS describe the portfolio as following a funded-status glide path (de-risk as the funded ratio rises) rather than a calendar glide path, and then list the three planned changes (2028 top-up, 2031 floor, post-2033 run-off)?
anchor_quote: How will the portfolio’s asset allocation and composition change as future funding needs approach and payments are made?
hypothesis: Guess: yes. Institutional glide paths are mostly funded-status triggered (NISA notes 'the near ubiquity of glidepaths', VERIFIED-PRIMARY; Russell/BlackRock guides SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). At 102.6% funded on day one, a funded-status path says 'hedge fully now', which answers the IPS prompt without contradicting lock-early.
would_change_detail: The IPS answer to prompt 4 (what changes and why), and which three changes it names.
north_star: Answers the official prompt head-on while keeping the promise safe; most teams will write a calendar glide path by habit.

text: What fees will be charged on the reserve, do they un-fund a ladder with only $7.7k headroom, and should the IPS state that the reserve is held as directly owned Treasuries with all fees paid from the growth sleeve?
anchor_quote: All teams should review the CFA Institute’s Asset Manager Code and operate by these standards. (Rules page); headroom $7,736 (F-104)
hypothesis: Guess (ASSUMPTION arithmetic): PV of a yearly fee on the ladder ~ fee x $2,933,301 -> 0.15% fund expense $4.4k (57% of headroom); 0.5% advisory fee $14.7k (1.9x headroom); 1.0% $29.3k. JPM (Oct 2021, VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 'Hibernation strategies will burn through capital over time'. New vs BS-01: A3 modelled fees on the sleeve only.
would_change_detail: Net-of-fee funded ratio and the FR fee assumption; an IPS cost principle (direct Treasuries for the reserve; fees from the sleeve).
north_star: An honest firm shows Laura its cost; rivals that ignore fees overstate her facility money.

text: Should the IPS adopt APRA SPS 160's two-part rule as its rule if rates fall before January 2027: a stated 'shortfall limit' for the starting funded ratio and a 'restoration plan' that returns the promise to 100% funded by 1 Jan 2028 from the 2028 deposit first?
anchor_quote: Apart from the two contributions described above, she will neither add to nor withdraw from the portfolio before 2033.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. SPS 160 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, APRA handbook) defines a shortfall limit as the dip from which a fund can 'reasonably expect ... to be restored ... within one year' and requires restoration 'within a time period ... which must not exceed three years'. P(ladder cost > $300k on 2027-01-01) ~24% (F-112, ASSUMPTION). The council's waterfall has the substance; SPS 160 gives a recognised trigger, deadline and name.
would_change_detail: Parameters of the pre-funding rule (trigger level, rung order, deadline) and one IPS sentence.
north_star: Laura sees a pre-written plan for the one thing that can go wrong before she invests - trustee behaviour, not trader behaviour.

text: Can the plan borrow municipal finance's distinction between economic defeasance (Treasuries bought to cover payments) and legal defeasance (a formal escrow checked by an independent verification agent) to reconcile 'funded 2027, set aside 2033', and should the FR include a one-table sufficiency check of each rung against each $50k payment?
anchor_quote: explain how they evaluated that level of certainty
hypothesis: Guess: yes; this is NEW evidence for brief section 8 item 9. NABL (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): the Verification Agent is 'responsible for independently confirming that the investments purchased for the Escrow Fund will be sufficient to fund the Debt Service payments'; 'Once Bonds are legally defeased, they are generally considered no longer outstanding'. A hand-checkable table answers 'how they evaluated' with no model.
would_change_detail: FR reconciliation sentence plus a decision to add a sufficiency table to the FR certainty section.
north_star: A statistics graduate trusts a check she can redo in five minutes more than a simulated percentile.

text: Should the reserve be ring-fenced from 2027 in a separate, labelled account with a written rule that it pays only the ten payments, naming who can override it and when?
anchor_quote: Laura will set aside a portion of the portfolio to fund the ten payments. This set-aside is called the operating reserve.
hypothesis: Guess: yes, as a one-line governance rule; the legal form is out of scope. The likeliest real-world failure is the reserve drifting into a facility overrun. NABL (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) describes escrow for defeased bonds as an 'irrevocable Pledge'.
would_change_detail: An IPS governance clause, and an FR co-sponsor checklist item that operating money is held separately.
north_star: Protects Laura from her own generosity under pressure, and co-sponsors can see the separation.

text: Where does the team's 'high degree of funding certainty' sit next to published standards (Solvency II 99.5% one-year survival, UK low-dependency at least 90% hedged, planners' 75-90% confidence zones), and should the FR show that comparison?
anchor_quote: They should also define what they consider a high degree of funding certainty
hypothesis: Guess: one FR line. Solvency II: 'confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, EUR-Lex); TPR 'at least 90%' hedging (VERIFIED-PRIMARY); confidence zone 75-90% SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED. A bought, matched ladder is not a one-year probability, so it sits above all three in nominal terms. NEW vs brief 8.6: verified external benchmarks.
would_change_detail: FR certainty section: framing 'these standards are probabilities; ours is a purchase'; keep out of the IPS.
north_star: Speaks the statistician's language: which standard, over what horizon, measured how.

text: US public pensions discount promises at their assumed return (median 7.0%); at 7% Laura's payments would 'cost' about $250k instead of $292k - should the FR show this $42k gap to explain why growth-first plans under-reserve?
anchor_quote: use reasonable return assumptions consistent with their strategy
hypothesis: Guess (ASSUMPTION arithmetic): PV at 2027-01-01 at flat 7% = $250,386; at 6.7% = $257,485; on the Treasury curve $292,264; understatement $41.9k (14.3%). NASRA April 2026 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): the return assumption 'also serves as the discount rate' and 'A rate set too high will understate liabilities'; median 7.0% since FY21.
would_change_detail: FR portfolio analysis number and sentence; chart candidate: three bars of promise cost at 7%, 6.7% and the Treasury curve.
north_star: Shows Laura a trap many professionals fell into, and that her plan avoids it on purpose.

text: Is the lottery annuity (funded by U.S. Treasury securities, 'the higher the interest rates, the higher the advertised Grand Prize') a usable everyday precedent for 'bought, not forecast', or does it fail the credibility test next to the municipal escrow precedent?
anchor_quote: communicates Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors
hypothesis: Guess: at most a teaching line in the FR, never in the co-sponsor draft; the muni escrow is more dignified. Marketplace 2022-11-08 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) reports the annuity 'accrues interest from investments in U.S. Treasury bonds'; the Powerball FAQ wording is SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED.
would_change_detail: Whether any everyday analogy appears in the FR, and which one.
north_star: Plain English a founder would repeat to partners, without a gimmick she would find cheap.

text: Since Yale sets each year's spending from its endowment value 'from two years ago' for budget predictability, should Laura's 2031 range be framed as a Yale-style lagged rule (known in 2031, applied in 2033, part locked, part smoothed), and would naming the precedent help co-sponsors trust it?
anchor_quote: Laura plans to begin approaching potential co-sponsors in 2031, two years before the residency is established.
hypothesis: Guess: yes, as one FR line plus a rule design. Yale Provost FAQ (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 'we apply the targeted spending rate (5.25%) to the endowment’s year-end value from two years ago. Then we take 20% of that amount and add it to 80% of the total amount spent'. The 2031 floor in a 2-year Treasury is the same predictability idea taken further.
would_change_detail: Design of the 2031 range rule (locked floor plus a stated share of the unlocked sleeve) and an FR co-sponsor sentence.
north_star: Co-sponsors hear a method used by a famous endowment, not a hope.

would_change_detail: FR definition of 'responsible'; possibly an IPS clause.
north_star: Turns an undefined word into a standard professionals and courts already use.

would_change_detail: Structure of the 2031 range and the FR fundraising-draft checklist (which part is a commitment, which is conditional).
north_star: Co-sponsors can count her floor as real money - exactly the signal the case says a meaningful contribution should send.

hypothesis: Guess (INTERPRETATION): the case fixes the decision in 2033, not the payment date, so staging looks allowed but is unstated. Milestone disbursement is standard grant practice (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). It makes flexibility a mechanism (unpaid tranches) rather than a sized fund, but may fail the simplicity test.
would_change_detail: FR timing assumption for the facility contribution and the flexibility sentence.
north_star: Matches how a real building gets paid for, which an entrepreneur would recognise at once.

text: Should the growth sleeve lock part of the facility floor whenever it crosses pre-set levels between 2028 and 2031 (funded-status triggers, as pensions de-risk), instead of locking only in 2031, and how would that change the 2031 floor p5/p50 and the chance of landing within the stated range?

would_change_detail: 2031 floor distribution and the confidence of landing within the range in the FR; keep-or-drop decision on a ratchet rule.
north_star: Shows the plan protects Laura's good luck as well as her promise.

hypothesis: Guess: yes, one FR sentence. NACUBO (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): UPMIFA's optional 'rebuttable presumption of imprudence if an institution expends an amount greater than seven percent of fair market value of a fund, calculated in an averaging formula over three years'. Yale's 4.0-6.5% band is SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED.
would_change_detail: How flexibility is expressed in the FR (rule, not size).
north_star: Gives Laura room to adapt 'as the project develops' with a guard rail she can explain to partners.

text: Which governance elements from professional IPS templates must the 500-word IPS carry - who decides and monitors, dated review points (2028, 2031, 2033), event triggers (funded ratio below 100%, deposit short or late, residency delayed), and one rebalancing rule - and which can be cut?
anchor_quote: It helps investors stay focused on long-term objectives and make disciplined decisions during changing market conditions.
hypothesis: Guess: three governance lines suffice. CFA Institute Elements of an IPS (2010, VERIFIED-PRIMARY): '2b. Describe the process for reviewing and updating the IPS'; '4c. Define the process for rebalancing portfolios to target allocations'. UK SI 2005/3378 reg 2 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): review '(a)at least every three years; and (b)without delay after any significant change in investment policy.'
would_change_detail: Which governance clauses get IPS words (event-based review triggers; one rebalancing rule; roles consistent with the real advisor rules).
north_star: An IPS that still works when nobody from our firm is in the room is what a client hires.

text: What would a private banker pre-commit to for a 2029 bear market, and does holding the reserve as individual bonds rather than bond funds remove the biggest behaviour trap, given bond-fund investors captured only about half their funds' returns?
anchor_quote: Laura understands that investing involves uncertainty and periods of market volatility.
hypothesis: Guess: pre-commit to (1) report the promise's funded status first, (2) no transfers between hedge and sleeve, (3) a sleeve rebalancing band, (4) individual Treasuries for the reserve. Morningstar Mind the Gap 2025 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 1.2pp/yr investor gap; bond-fund investors captured 'only about half'; allocation funds 'nearly 97%'; recommends 'slightly haircutting projections'. Vanguard 2022 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): coaching '0 to > 200' bps.
would_change_detail: IPS behaviour rule; possible haircut on sleeve return assumptions in FR projections; FR sentence on the bad-year plan.
north_star: Laura hires a firm for the bad year; this shows we planned her bad year in advance.

text: Should the team keep, from the first WInS trade, a weekly hedge-effectiveness log (Treasury sleeve value change vs change in the ten payments' present value at ~$289/bp) so a reflection can show the strategy was 'tested': rates moved X bp, bonds moved $Y, the promise's cost moved $Z, funded status held?
anchor_quote: Your reflections should clearly explain how each decision supported, tested, or refined your overall investment strategy.
hypothesis: Guess: yes - highest-value WInS-now item here. Pension CIOs report funded status, not return (NISA and JPM papers, VERIFIED-PRIMARY, frame all decisions in funded status). With the 10y at its highest since 2007 (F-004), Treasury funds may fall during WInS; the log turns an apparent loss into evidence the hedge worked. Inputs: daily treasury.gov curve + official_curve_pv.py + WInS values.
would_change_detail: Start the log now; TN reflections cite it (Oct 23); FR 'how effectively it implemented that strategy' uses it.
north_star: Proves in six weeks, with real data, that the plan behaves as promised - something a growth-first book cannot show.

text: Should the FR report risk as 'expected negative years out of 20' (Australia's Standard Risk Measure) for the growth sleeve, and explain why that label and volatility both misstate the reserve, whose held-to-maturity payments stay certain even in negative mark-to-market years?
anchor_quote: uses reasonable assumptions and projections to evaluate funding reliability, the facility contribution, and financial flexibility under varying market outcomes
hypothesis: Guess: one plain-English FR line. ART (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): risk band 'based on the number of expected years of negative annual returns over any 20-year period'. ASSUMPTION arithmetic with JPM inputs: 100% US large cap ~6.7 of 20; 60/40 sleeve ~5.4; intermediate Treasuries ~2.5. Band thresholds SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED (FSC-ASFA PDF refused, 403).
would_change_detail: FR uncertainty communication: 'years out of 20' for the sleeve, plus a sentence on why market-value risk measures mislead for the reserve.
north_star: Reports uncertainty in words a non-investor understands, and shows why the usual risk number would mislead her.

text: Australian law (the Retirement Income Covenant) makes super trustees 'achieve and balance' maximising income, managing risks to 'sustainability and stability', and 'flexible access' - Laura's growth, certainty and flexibility; should the IPS state a priority order (promise, then flexibility, then growth) rather than a balance, and should the FR name the covenant as the team's inspiration?
anchor_quote: How does your strategy balance growth, risk, liquidity, funding reliability, and financial flexibility?
hypothesis: Guess: a stated order beats a 'balance' because the case itself orders things (the reserve comes 'before' the payment and the facility). Treasury EM, exposure draft 2021 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 'achieve and balance three objectives: maximizing their expected retirement income; managing expected risks to the sustainability and stability ...; and having flexible access to expected funds'. Enacted wording SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED (AustLII 403). Name it only in the FR Articulation section.
would_change_detail: IPS central idea (order vs balance) and an FR Articulation line on the Australian inspiration.
north_star: Our home country's law on long promises supports Laura's order of priorities - an authentic team-voice detail no other team has.

text: Given Chhabra's principle that risk allocation precedes asset allocation, is Laura's aspirational-risk bucket already full (her creative business, future books, the residency itself), so the portfolio should hold only personal-risk (reserve) and market-risk (broad sleeve) assets and refuse thematic, single-stock or country tilts?
anchor_quote: Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career
hypothesis: Guess: yes; this challenges the team notes' mapping 'flexibility = aspirational bucket'. Chhabra (2005, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED abstract): personal, market and aspirational risk; 'risk allocation should precede asset allocation'. Her 2028 deposit depends on the same entrepreneurial risk, so the portfolio should not add more of it.
would_change_detail: No thematic/Taiwan/AI tilts in WInS or the plan; an IPS principle sentence.
north_star: 'You already take the big bets in your life; our job is to make sure they never threaten your promise' - reads as hers, not generic.

text: Which named frameworks (cash-flow matching/LDI, funded-status de-risking, goals-based buckets, Yale-style lagged spending, UPMIFA prudence) map to which part of the plan, and should any be named in the IPS or only in one FR mapping table?
anchor_quote: Focus on the strategy and decision-making framework that guide your portfolio rather than describing individual investments or presenting detailed financial calculations.
hypothesis: Guess: name none in the IPS (plain words only; the council judge panel warned against 'LDI' and 'defeasance'); the FR carries one table showing each rule's professional ancestor, showing 'effective use of investment concepts' without jargon in the scored 500 words.
would_change_detail: Naming policy per deliverable; an FR framework-mapping table.
north_star: Judges see professional depth in the FR, while Laura reads an IPS in her own language.

text: Would a pension CIO consider buying the promise from an insurer (a deferred 10-year period-certain annuity, the 'buyout' option), and which Laura-specific reason rejects it: insurer credit risk, the 'for BOTH contributions' permitted list, or loss of liquidity if the residency changes?
anchor_quote: Investments permitted (for BOTH contributions) (SMApply FAQ, via R-AN15)
hypothesis: Guess: rejected. Under reading 1 of R-AN15 the permitted list binds the plan, and an annuity is not on it; a Treasury ladder can be sold if the residency is delayed or changes (BS-07), an annuity usually cannot. Worth one FR 'alternatives considered' line.
would_change_detail: FR alternatives-considered sentence.
north_star: Shows we chose Treasuries over a real alternative for reasons tied to Laura: flexibility, and certainty that does not depend on an insurer.

text: Should the team write a rebalancing band for the WInS book before the first trade, so a market move produces a rule-driven trade whose note shows the strategy being 'tested'?
anchor_quote: Your reflections should clearly explain how each decision supported, tested, or refined your overall investment strategy.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. A band would do, e.g. equity share of the book outside target +/-5 points, checked weekly, never trading the same fund twice on one U.S. day. CFA Institute (2010, VERIFIED-PRIMARY, rpc.cfainstitute.org IPS for Individual Investors, section 4c): 'If the policy is not to rebalance, this policy should be documented in the IPS.' Vanguard's '5% or so' threshold is SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED.
would_change_detail: Decision log gets a band rule before the first WInS order; the first band-triggered trade becomes a Trading Note candidate; the IPS gets one rebalancing clause.
north_star: Laura sees a firm that follows rules from week 1, not one that writes rules afterwards.

text: Of the four standard 'get back on track' levers, which can Laura use, and should the IPS pre-commit never to use 'add equity to catch up'?
anchor_quote: Apart from the two contributions described above, she will neither add to nor withdraw from the portfolio before 2033.
hypothesis: Guess: Morgan Stanley lists 'stretching your time horizon, scaling back the goal, increasing your equity investment, or saving more' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, morganstanley.com Stay on Track, 2026-09-27). The case closes saving more and fixes the dates. That leaves scaling back the facility (the designed shock absorber) and doubling down on equity, which should be ruled out in advance.
would_change_detail: IPS clause: the facility contribution is the only variable that absorbs bad markets, and risk is never raised to recover losses. This is also possible TN reflection content after a WInS down week.
north_star: It tells Laura in advance exactly what gives way in a bad market (her facility number, never her promise).

text: Should every WInS trade note name the goal ('funding purpose') it serves, using a fixed label set, as goals-based practitioners label each sub-portfolio?
anchor_quote: Your team may consider diversification across asset classes, sectors, industries, market capitalizations, geographic regions, risk characteristics, and funding purposes.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. Brunel builds 'module-built portfolios, each of which is driven by a client's expressed goals' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, CFA Conf. Proceedings Mar 2012). Wharton's own list makes goal-labelled diversification an official idea that counts toward 'appropriate diversification'. Notes cannot be edited, so the labels must be fixed before trade 1.
would_change_detail: A fixed three-label vocabulary (promise / 2031 floor / growth) is used in every WInS note from the first trade.
north_star: Every trade visibly answers 'which of Laura's goals does this serve?'

text: Is the team's Chhabra mapping wrong: should Laura's career and the residency be named as her 'aspirational' bucket, so the portfolio holds only the safety and market buckets?
anchor_quote: Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career, she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance between pursuing growth and protecting the capital required for her goals.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. Team notes map aspirational = flexibility reserve. Chhabra's aspirational bucket holds 'owning a small business, or leveraging unique human capital' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED; SSRN 403). Chhabra: 'For those things you must do, the emphasis is going to be on lowering the risk of your not achieving these goals' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, CFA Enterprising Investor 2015-08-05). Her aspirational risk already lives in her career.
would_change_detail: IPS risk-tolerance clause explains why a risk-taking founder gets a moderate portfolio; the FR framework section corrects the bucket names; the team notes are fixed before use.
north_star: It shows we understood why a bold entrepreneur wants a careful portfolio, in a framework from her own school's world.

text: On the UK regulator's willingness/capacity split, is Laura's capacity for loss on the growth sleeve actually high, and so is ~60% sleeve equity set by willingness and the 2031 promise rather than by capacity?
anchor_quote: Laura's living expenses and short-term financial needs will be covered by income and financial resources outside the portfolio.
hypothesis: Guess: FCA FG11/05 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) defines capacity for loss by whether a loss 'would have a materially detrimental effect on their standard of living'. The case puts her living costs outside the portfolio, so capacity on the sleeve is high. The team docs' 'moderate to low capacity' conflates this with career risk. Only the 2031 credibility statement caps sleeve risk, which supports 60% and argues against going below 50%.
would_change_detail: Sleeve equity weight (50/60/70% open item) and the IPS risk sentence, which should state willingness and capacity separately.
north_star: Separating 'can afford' from 'wants' is what a client hires a professional for; most teams write only 'moderate risk'.

text: Does the 2026 pension 'surplus glidepath' benchmark support our ~20% total equity after 2028, or imply that a ~1.5 funded ratio could carry more return-seeking assets?
anchor_quote: Sleeve equity 50/60/70% gives 17.0 / 20.4 / 23.8% of the whole portfolio (F-409)
hypothesis: Guess: Russell (2026-07-13, VERIFIED-PRIMARY) finds a 20/80-30/70 optimum at 110% funded even with no value on surplus, with risk rising 'modestly' above a defined surplus threshold, 'implemented incrementally'. Laura after 2028 is ~152% funded (DERIVED, ASSUMPTION inputs), so ~20% sits at the cautious edge of practice. The 5-year horizon and public 2031 statement justify it; 65-70% sleeve equity is also defensible.
would_change_detail: Sleeve equity weight (60% vs 65-70%), plus an FR sentence citing the practice; D3 reruns F-407 if the weight changes.
north_star: 'What the best pension professionals now do, adapted to your 2031 promise' beats a generic 60/40.

text: Do any of the three structural leaks in J.P. Morgan's critique of full pension hedging ('hibernation') apply to Laura's ten payments, and should the FR say they do not?
anchor_quote: For purposes of the competition, each payment is a fixed $50,000 and is not adjusted for inflation.
hypothesis: Guess: none apply. JPM AM (Oct 2021, VERIFIED-PRIMARY) cites corporate downgrades (~50bp/yr), longevity and experience losses. Laura's liability has no lives, no benefit formula and Treasury backing, so hers is the rare case where precise matching does not leak. New vs brief 8.1: this is the strongest outside professional objection, not our own alternatives.
would_change_detail: One FR sentence pre-empts 'professionals say full hedging is inefficient', with the three reasons it does not apply; nothing in the IPS.
north_star: Answering the best counter-argument shows we know the professional debate, not one side of it.

text: Brunel takes more risk for needs 6-15 years away; why is it right for us not to do so for the 2037-42 payments, and what sentence says why?
anchor_quote: Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement.
hypothesis: Guess: Brunel (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, 2012) raises the return assumption to 6% for years 6-15 'because we can take a little more risk'. His family's lifestyle spending can be cut and refilled; Laura's payments are fixed, cannot use outside money, and are the certainty test. His own warning applies: 'a random fluctuation in asset values can be turned into a permanent loss of capital'. New evidence is a named practitioner benchmark; F-108 costs stand.
would_change_detail: FR sentence justifying the full lock against goals-based practice.
north_star: It proves the plan is tailored to fixed promises, not copied from a template.

text: Top goals-based practice treats 'needs' as 90-95% goals; how do we present our 'bought' certainty as a deliberate client choice with a stated price?
anchor_quote: They should also define what they consider a high degree of funding certainty, explain how they evaluated that level of certainty
hypothesis: Guess: Brunel's goal-probability table (Das et al. JOIM 2018 Table 1, VERIFIED-PRIMARY) is Needs 90-95, Wants 80-85, Wishes 65-75, Dreams 50-60. Our certainty sits above 'needs'. Its price is ~$19k of median facility money (growth-first $226k vs lock-early $207k), and it protects the p5 ($159k vs $20k) (F-401).
would_change_detail: IPS certainty definition marks it as her 'needs' goal; the FR gets one line with the ~$19k median price and the p5 protection.
north_star: A statistics graduate sees a certainty level chosen on purpose and priced, not a software '95%'.

text: What does insisting on Treasuries rather than high-grade corporate bonds cost Laura, and does the saving survive expected downgrade losses?
anchor_quote: All ten payments must be funded by the investment portfolio with a high degree of certainty.
hypothesis: Guess: IG OAS 0.79%, AA 0.58% (FRED 2026-09-24, VERIFIED-PRIMARY). A ladder at +58-79bp would cost ~$16-22k less (DERIVED from F-102, ASSUMPTION of a flat spread). JPM's ~50bp/yr downgrade drag (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) leaves an expected saving of maybe $2-8k while adding default risk. So 'Treasuries only' is cheap in expectation.
would_change_detail: FR 'why Treasuries' sentence with its price; confirms no corporates in the reserve.
north_star: Showing what each safety choice costs is how a professional earns trust; almost no team will do it.

text: With the U.S. rated below AAA by all three agencies since Moody's May 2025 downgrade, what honest wording should replace 'certain barring U.S. default'?
anchor_quote: All ten payments must be funded by the investment portfolio with a high degree of certainty.
hypothesis: Guess: practitioners still treat Treasuries as the risk-free hedge but name default as a remote residual. Suggested wording: certain in nominal U.S. dollars, with the remaining risks named (U.S. default, operational error, loss of buying power to inflation), one clause each. The Moody's Aa1 downgrade of 2025-05-16 is SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED.
would_change_detail: Certainty definition wording in the IPS and FR.
north_star: Honest uncertainty language is the case's core credibility skill and what a statistician trusts.

text: What governance would a CFA-standard IPS contain here: who decides, an annual review, and which trigger events force a review (late or smaller 2028 deposit, rates falling before purchase, residency delay, the 2031 announcement)?
anchor_quote: Investment Policy Statement. This formally establishes the strategy and the team's decision-making framework.
hypothesis: Guess: CFA 2010 section 2 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) assigns responsibility for policy, execution and monitoring, with review 'no less frequently than annually'. One IPS sentence can give the roles, an annual review, three or four named triggers, and rules written so any PM could apply them. Few teams will name triggers.
would_change_detail: IPS governance clause, plus a decision on which triggers to name.
north_star: Laura is choosing a firm for 16 years; a named review process is what she would sign.

text: Which fee would a real adviser disclose for a $450k client, and must the IPS say that fees come only from the growth sleeve so the locked payments are never sold?
anchor_quote: At the beginning of 2027, Laura plans to invest $300,000 with an asset management firm.
hypothesis: Guess: the median AUM fee is ~1.0% at $500k-$1M (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED, Kitces/Cerulli), and private banks require ~$10M (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED), so she is a wealth-management client. A3 estimated -$17k/-$34k median surplus at 0.5%/1.0% (ASSUMPTION). A held-to-maturity ladder justifies little fee. Fees must come from the surplus or the lock breaks.
would_change_detail: Fee line in FR projections and the 2031 range; IPS sentence 'costs are paid from the growth money; the reserve is never sold to pay fees'.
north_star: A firm that discloses its own cost (as the CFA Asset Manager Code requires) is one she can trust.

text: If rates fall before January 2027 and the ladder costs more than $300k, do professional hedgers hedge in full when affordable, buy in stages, or wait for yield triggers?
anchor_quote: Above $300k on 173 of 185 trading days [of 2026]; at or below $300k only on the 12 days since 2026-09-10 (F-111)
hypothesis: Guess: pension practice raises hedge ratios by funded-status or yield triggers (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). Russell 2026 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) stresses a clearly defined threshold implemented incrementally. For Laura: hedge the longest rungs first up to $300k, fill the rest from the 2028 deposit, and never wait for better yields (that is a rate bet). This confirms longest-first, in a trigger/action/record format.
would_change_detail: Confirm or replace the 'rates fall first' rule and write it as an IPS clause.
north_star: A pre-written rule for the one move that could break the plan before it starts shows rare foresight.

text: Should the IPS state risk tolerance as the CFA standard models it: anchored to her known liabilities, with a stated intolerable loss for the growth sleeve?
anchor_quote: An Investment Policy Statement (IPS) outlines an investor's financial goals, risk tolerance, and guidelines for managing a portfolio.
hypothesis: Guess: CFA 2010 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 'Where possible, the IPS should account for known liabilities to lend some quantitative basis to the risk tolerance assessment.' It allows 'multiple levels of risk' by goal, and its example makes a 33% 12-month loss 'intolerable'. For Laura: zero tolerance for the payments (bought) and a stated tolerable sleeve fall (D3 to size, ASSUMPTION ~one third).
would_change_detail: IPS risk-tolerance sentence, and possibly a number for the tolerable sleeve loss.
north_star: The case never states her risk tolerance; deriving it in a measurable form shows client knowledge.

text: From 2027, should the promise assets be held and reported as a separate sub-account, as goals-based practice does, so that 'set aside in 2033' labels money already segregated?
anchor_quote: At the beginning of 2033, before making the first operating payment or contributing to the facility, Laura will set aside a portion of the portfolio to fund the ten payments.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. Brunel's module-built portfolios (VERIFIED-PRIMARY) and UBS's separate Liquidity pot (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED, UBS 403) both work this way. Brief 8.9 settled which number is the reserve; this is governance, making the 'funded 2027, set aside 2033' sentence concrete.
would_change_detail: IPS sentence saying the reserve is a separate sub-account from purchase; FR charts show two pots.
north_star: Laura can point to 'the residency's first ten years' as money that exists, which co-sponsors also want to see.

text: Which named frameworks fit which part of the plan and would be recognised, and which (e.g. endowment spending rules) should be deliberately left out?
anchor_quote: Demonstrates understanding and effective use of investment concepts and tools
hypothesis: Guess at the map: goals-based wealth management (Brunel/Das) for the structure; cash-flow matching/LDI for the reserve; Chhabra (corrected) for the risk budget; surplus glidepath (Russell 2026) for the sleeve; CFA IPS elements for governance. Endowment spending rules do not fit (a percentage of a fluctuating fund forever vs fixed dollars for ten years). No names in the IPS; at most four in an FR table.
would_change_detail: Which framework names appear in the FR table and which are dropped; the IPS stays jargon-free.
north_star: Using the right tool for each goal, and saying why a famous one does not fit, shows judgement, not name-dropping.

text: Should the plan commit to one progress measure (e.g. 'payments covered: yes; funded ratio') and report it the same way across all deliverables and every future report to Laura?
anchor_quote: Teams should use each deliverable for its intended purpose while maintaining a clear and consistent investment strategy across all three.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. CFA 2010 section 4b (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 'Inappropriate use of different metrics to highlight or disguise certain risks should be avoided.' Morgan Stanley reports 'Progress to Goals' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). One goal-progress metric stops bond price falls looking like broken promises.
would_change_detail: IPS names the one measure; TN reflections and FR charts reuse it for each year 2027-2033.
north_star: A single honest gauge Laura can read in five seconds marks a trusted adviser.

text: Should the FR cite 'behaviour gap' or 'adviser's alpha' figures to justify pre-commitment rules, given that a 2026 FAJ paper finds timing losses of only 0.10% a year versus Morningstar's 1.2%?
anchor_quote: All material referenced or generated by AI should be cited like any other reference material (with due consideration for the quality of the reference, which may be poor).
hypothesis: Guess: no big numbers. Morningstar 2025: 1.2pp gap (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Vanguard: behavioural coaching 150bp (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Fulkerson et al. FAJ 2026: 'poor timing ... costs them only 0.10% per year' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY abstract). Justify the rules by Laura's own decision dates (2031, 2033), and use Vanguard's line that the IPS 'sows the seed for future behavioural coaching opportunities' without the number.
would_change_detail: FR behavioural rationale drops contested statistics and anchors on her decision dates.
north_star: Refusing a flattering but contested statistic is the rigour a statistics-trained client looks for.

text: With the 2031 floor bought, the only way outside the range is above it; should the top end be set at a stated percentile (e.g. Brunel's 'wants' level, 80-85%) so that the confidence figure equals that percentile?
anchor_quote: state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. P(below floor) is ~0 because the floor is bought, so P(within) = P(at or below the top). A top at the 80th-85th percentile of the 2033 outcome (computed in 2031) gives 80-85% confidence, matching Brunel's 'wants' band (Das et al. 2018, VERIFIED-PRIMARY) and the 75-90% planning 'Confidence Zone' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED, MoneyGuidePro).
would_change_detail: The 2031 range's top end and the stated confidence in the FR.
north_star: A range whose confidence comes from a stated professional rule is the most credible thing Laura can tell co-sponsors.

text: Should the fundraising draft report uncertainty as dollar outcomes in named scenarios (practice: 'outcomes, not probabilities'), with at most one probability and wording that pre-empts the 'wrong side of maybe' reaction?
anchor_quote: communicates Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors.
hypothesis: Guess: Kitces (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): 'outcomes, not probabilities, are what matter to clients', and the 'wrong side of maybe' fallacy judges a forecast wrong from one outcome. Das et al. use two reference points (Target Wealth and Loss Threshold), which map to the range ends. Recipe: the floor stated as money already set aside; the top as an expectation with its percentile; 2-3 dollar scenarios tied to what the residency can do.
would_change_detail: Structure of the FR fundraising draft (the students write it).
north_star: Co-sponsors can plan around outcomes, which protects the credibility the case names as the key risk.

text: Once the range is communicated in 2031, what may change it before 2033, and should the IPS pre-commit that the floor never moves down and only the upside is revisited, like a guardrail?
anchor_quote: If Laura promises more than she can ultimately contribute, she could damage her credibility and lose the confidence or participation of co-sponsors.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. With Kitces guardrails, advisors state in advance 'the portfolio value that would trigger spending changes and the magnitude that would be prescribed' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). For Laura: the floor is fixed because bought, and the top is revised only upward or on one pre-announced date, so a promise can be beaten but never broken.
would_change_detail: IPS clause on the 2031 rule; FR communication plan.
north_star: A promise designed so it can only be beaten, never broken, is what a public figure would choose.

text: How much should Laura hold back after the facility contribution; do practitioner benchmarks (Brunel's 10% for 'opportunistic goals', UBS's 'Legacy' pot) give a defensible rule?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops.
hypothesis: Guess: Brunel's example family reserves '10 percent of their total wealth ... for what they call opportunistic goals' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, 2012); UBS's Legacy pot is SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED. One case study is weak evidence. State flexibility as a share of the post-reserve surplus (e.g. 10-25%), justified by overrun or delay risk; a percentage rule avoids sizing a contingency fund.
would_change_detail: Share held back after the facility, and so the recommended facility contribution in the FR.
north_star: It protects her ability to keep acting like an entrepreneur after 2033, which is who she is.

text: After the 2031 floor is locked, should the rest of the sleeve still hold equities, given that practitioners keep money needed within 3-5 years mainly in fixed income, and should the lock share equal the promised floor?
anchor_quote: In 2031, however, the value of her portfolio in 2033 remains uncertain.
hypothesis: Guess: Brunel: 'within the next three to five years, we build a portfolio composed principally of fixed-income securities' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). The unlocked 20% is unpromised upside, so equity is fine as long as the top end is rule-set. The lock share should be defined as 'whatever is promised as the floor', not a fixed 80%.
would_change_detail: 2031 lock share (80% vs 'equal to the promised floor') and the matching IPS clause.
north_star: Linking what she says in 2031 to what is locked in 2031 makes her words and money match.

text: Does an Australian benchmark earn a place: the Retirement Income Covenant's three objectives mirror the IPS guide's trio, and the Future Fund shows why a promise without government backing must be matched?
anchor_quote: How does your strategy balance growth, risk, liquidity, funding reliability, and financial flexibility?
hypothesis: Guess: yes, one sentence. APRA/ASIC 2023 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): trustees must 'achieve and balance the three objectives of: maximising expected retirement income; managing expected risks to the sustainability and stability of retirement income; and having flexible access'. The Future Fund targets 'at least the Consumer Price Index + 4 to 5 per cent' (Wikipedia, verbatim; futurefund.gov.au 403) because the Commonwealth backs it; Laura has no such backer.
would_change_detail: One FR Articulation sentence in an authentic Australian team voice.
north_star: An authentic voice grounded in a real regulatory parallel is distinctive and honest about who we are.

text: Should the first Treasury trade note name the 2026 real-yield window (real 10y 2.85%, highest since Nov 2008; term premium highest since Feb 2011) as the reason the ladder is affordable now, rather than 'rates are high'?
anchor_quote: 5.18% on 2026-09-24 is the highest daily close since 2007-07-06 (F-004); R-T9: "Explain the reasoning behind each decision, how it aligned with, tested, or refined your overall investment strategy"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. From the Feb 27 low to Sep 24 the 10y rose 121bp: +113bp real yield (1.72->2.85), +8bp breakeven (2.25->2.33); Kim-Wright term premium +50bp to 0.96% (FRED DFII10/T10YIE/THREEFYTP10, VERIFIED-PRIMARY inputs, derived). Laura is a natural long-term lender (hold-to-maturity liability), so she is paid a premium for a price risk she does not bear. The ladder became affordable through a real-yield window, not an inflation scare.
would_change_detail: Trading Note #1 reflection ('why this trade, why now') and one IPS reason: must contain the dated real yield or funded ratio, 'held to maturity', and a link to the ten payments; no rate forecast.
north_star: Shows Laura we bought her promise when the market was paying us to do it, without guessing rates.

text: Which dated events before Laura's January 2027 purchase could erase the 27bp cushion, and should the IPS write the purchase rule as a funded-ratio trigger rather than any rate view?
anchor_quote: Headroom under the $300k deposit | $7,736 = 27bp (F-104)
hypothesis: GUESS: the likeliest >27bp rally is energy de-escalation (Hormuz; Brent $114.89 on 9/22 vs $61.98 Jan 2, FRED VERIFIED-PRIMARY), a growth scare or an equity crash. Calendar (VERIFIED-PRIMARY): FOMC Oct 27-28 and Dec 8-9; Treasury refunding Nov 4 (2 days before IPS lock); CR expiry Dec 11 (cra.org); possible lame-duck debt-limit vote (NTU). 2y is ~100bp above fed funds mid, so markets price hikes; a rally needs a shock. The IPS locks Nov 6, so the rule must be mechanical: buy on arrival, longest rungs first, shortfall from the 2028 deposit, state the funded ratio on the purchase date.
would_change_detail: Form of the IPS purchase rule (ratio trigger, not date/forecast); FR scenario table adds a named 'de-escalation rally' row at -50bp = $307,135.
north_star: Laura gets a rule she can follow without trusting anyone's rate forecast.

text: Which of the three layers of 'default' (outright non-payment, technical payment delay, inflation-driven implicit default) does the Treasury ladder cover, and which must the certainty definition name?
anchor_quote: All ten payments must be funded by the investment portfolio with a high degree of certainty. / They should also define what they consider a high degree of funding certainty
hypothesis: GUESS: outright default not covered (and no USD asset can cover it; ratings AA+/Aa1/AA+ stable: Moody's page VERIFIED-PRIMARY, Fortune Jun 27 2026 read on page; 5y CDS ~36bp SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED); technical delay largely covered by maturities paying before the due date (1979 T-bill delays, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED); implicit default (inflation) not covered and falls on the residency's real budget. Definition must say 'nominal U.S. dollars', 'held to maturity', rests on Treasury paying on time, and discloses inflation risk.
would_change_detail: IPS certainty-definition sentence and FR assumptions list (R-C56).
north_star: A statistics graduate trusts a definition that says exactly what it does not cover.

text: Should the Final Report use Wharton's own Penn Wharton Budget Model estimate (25% chance of reaching the U.S. debt outer bound within 14 years, about 2040, inside the 2033-2042 payment window) to state honestly how certain 'certain' is in real terms?
anchor_quote: and identify the assumptions supporting their recommendation. (R-C56); PWBM: "there is a 25% chance of reaching it in 14 years"
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, once, as the reason the plan says 'nominal' aloud, labelled 'outer bound, not a forecast'. VERIFIED-PRIMARY (PWBM, Smetters & He, June 4 2026, verbatim): the bound is where "default of either explicit (Treasury) debt or implicit (pay-as-you-go) debt becomes a near certainty on a real (inflation-adjusted) basis"; lower-openness case "25 percent chance of reaching the ceiling by 2039"; median closure 2045-2051; also flags "AI bubble burst" as tightening the limit.
would_change_detail: One FR assumption sentence plus the named justification for an inflation stress case (Q09 number).
north_star: An honest limit drawn from her own university's research is more credible than 'risk-free'.

text: Does the projected debt-limit X-date of about February 2028, with Congress needing to act by January 1, 2028 (the day the $150k arrives), require a clause in the plan's 2028 top-up rule?
anchor_quote: $150,000 at the beginning of 2028 (F-601); NTU: "Congress would likely need to increase the debt limit by January 1, 2028"
hypothesis: GUESS: mostly a non-issue for 2032-2041 STRIPS, but the 2028 cash should not wait in T-bills maturing in the X-date window, and long rungs should be bought promptly (flight-to-quality in standoffs may make them dearer; ASSUMPTION, check 2011/2023). NTU (Aug 20 2026, read on page, secondary analysis): limit reached ~May 2027; X-date Feb 2028; headroom under $1.4T as of Aug 10 2026. 2028-01-01 is a Saturday.
would_change_detail: FR operating rule for where 2028 cash waits and when long rungs are bought; possibly one IPS clause.
north_star: Shows we checked the real 2027-28 political calendar against her exact cash-flow dates.

text: Do the reserve's Nov-15 maturities (paying ~47 days before each Jan-1 payment; 2033-01-01 is a Saturday) double as a buffer against a technical Treasury payment delay, and is that the stated reason to prefer them?
anchor_quote: Laura will make ten annual payments of $50,000 toward the residency's operating expenses, one at the beginning of each year from 2033 through 2042.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes and nearly free. S1 found early cash costs ~$2,124 (VERIFIED-PRIMARY inputs); that lead time controls both the non-business-day problem and a short technical delay (1979 delays lasted days to weeks, SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED). Fills operational-risk gap BS-18.
would_change_detail: Maturity choice (Nov 15 STRIPS vs Dec defined-maturity funds vs Feb 15) and one FR control line.
north_star: Her operators get paid on time even if Washington is late.

text: If an agency downgrades the U.S. again, what will the plan do, and should the IPS pre-commit to no forced selling of held-to-maturity Treasuries on a rating change?
anchor_quote: Investment Policy Statement. This formally establishes the strategy and the team's decision-making framework.
hypothesis: GUESS: a downgrade changes none of the ladder's cash flows; selling would turn a headline into a real loss; ~15 words of pre-commitment show discipline. S&P (Jun 2026, Fortune read on page): rating could slip over the next two years if deficits increase. CBO baseline deficit 5.8% of GDP 2026 to 6.7% 2036 (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED via CRFB; cbo.gov 403).
would_change_detail: IPS decision-rule clause ('hold, do not sell on rating actions'), or FR if IPS words are short.
north_star: Laura sees we will not panic on her behalf.

text: Since no U.S.-dollar asset is safer than a Treasury and every rival plan shares that floor, should the IPS spend only one clause on sovereign risk and use the words on the risks the ladder does not cover (inflation, TWD, operations)?
anchor_quote: "Investment Policy Statement" / "Maximum 500 words" (R-I18)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one clause in the IPS, one paragraph in the FR (INTERPRETATION: deposit insurance itself rests on the U.S. government). Most teams will either ignore it or over-dramatise it.
would_change_detail: IPS word budget: allocation of words between sovereign risk and inflation/currency/operational risk.
north_star: Clear priorities read as judgement rather than jargon.

text: What is the real value of the ten fixed $50k payments at the market's own inflation price and under one historically grounded stress, and who bears the erosion?
anchor_quote: For purposes of the competition, each payment is a fixed $50,000 and is not adjusted for inflation.
hypothesis: GUESS: the residency bears it by design (co-sponsors may fund operating support beyond her commitment). Derived: at 2.34% (10y breakeven, VERIFIED-PRIMARY) the 2042 payment is worth $34,534 in 2026 dollars (ten payments $384k); at 3.7% $27,958; at 5% $22,906; at 7% (~worst post-war 16-year U.S. CPI rate, 7.12% to 1982, FRED derived) $16,937. Headline CPI 3.71% vs core 2.76% (Aug 2026, FRED derived): energy drives the gap.
would_change_detail: FR inflation-assumption numbers (R-C85) and one fact in the co-sponsor draft.
north_star: She sees we told her what $50k will really buy in 2042.

text: Given the 2026 evidence (Fed independence upheld in Trump v. Cook, a 12-0 hike, 5y5y inflation anchored at 2.34%) against a highly partisan Fed-chair confirmation, should a 1970s-style inflation regime be a stress case rather than the base case for 2033-2042?
anchor_quote: FOMC 2026-09-16: "The Committee will deliver price stability."
hypothesis: GUESS: stress, not base; base = market breakeven. VERIFIED-PRIMARY: FOMC statement quote; Trump v. Cook decided June 29 2026, application denied (supremecourt.gov); Fed release May 15 2026 names Powell pro tem until Warsh sworn in; 5y5y 2.34% (2026 range 2.05-2.36). SNIPPET: Warsh confirmed 54-45.
would_change_detail: FR assumption sentence on the inflation regime and the choice of the stress rate used in Q09.
