text: Should any of Laura's upside above the floor be offered to co-sponsors as a matching or challenge offer instead of a plain range?
anchor_quote: A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura's commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute.
hypothesis: GUESS: no match. Huck & Rasul 2011: linear matching 'partially crowd[s] out' donors' own gifts; charities 'maximize donations given by simply announcing the presence of a lead gift' (VP abstract, RePEc). Rondeau & List 2008: 'challenge gifts positively influence contributions in the field, but matching gifts do not' (VP). Karlan & List 2007: 3:1 and 2:1 had 'no additional impact' over 1:1 (VP). A match also makes her 2033 amount depend on others' behaviour, which cannot carry a stated confidence.
would_change_detail: FR offer structure (firm announced lead gift, no match); one Articulation line on the rejected alternative.
north_star: A field-experiment-backed choice few of the ~2,300 final-report teams will have weighed.

text: Does the leadership-gift literature show that a founder's belief persuades others only when it is costly and unconditional, making the pull quote the private starting point and the bought floor its public proof?
anchor_quote: The only person who needs to believe in something is yourself.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Rondeau & List fn.3: 'when a large donor believes in the project by giving a gift this informational value affects an agent's beliefs regarding the value of the public good' (VP, NBER w13728). This links seed 15 to a checkable mechanism without tokenism. Caveat: the pull quote has no attribution in the PDF text layer; verify before presenting it as her words.
would_change_detail: FR narrative sentence linking her conviction to the bought floor; possibly the framing of the 50-word pitch.
north_star: Her own words become the design rule, which is what 'recognise as hers' means.

text: Do capital funders explicitly test whether operations are sustainable after the building is finished, which would make Laura's ten pre-funded operating years what unlocks facility money?
anchor_quote: Any remaining facility cost, and any operating support beyond Laura's commitment, may come from co-sponsors, grants, collaborators, program fees, continued business income, or other sources.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Kresge's campaign questions include 'Do you have a plan for sustaining support gained during the campaign after it concludes?' (VP). Andreoni 1998 models seed money solving a fixed-cost problem (VP abstract). This is new primary evidence for BS-17: put the operating commitment first in co-sponsor material, before the facility range.
would_change_detail: Order of the FR fundraising material (operating commitment first); one Articulation line explaining the case's asymmetry.
north_star: We answer the building funder's question before they ask it.

text: What funder calendar makes 2031 the right year, and does it imply a second checkpoint in late 2032, when annual public funders set 2033 budgets?
anchor_quote: Laura plans to begin approaching potential co-sponsors in 2031, two years before the residency is established.
hypothesis: GUESS: 2031 is the quiet-phase year for lead gifts. Kresge suggests 'at least 20 percent and sometimes as much as 50 percent' raised before applying, and pledges 'committed before the general public ever hears about the campaign' (VP). Lawson (2001), via Rondeau & List: 10-80% from leadership gifts before the public phase (VP). The Taiwan MOC artist-village subsidy is selected every year, with applications 1-30 November for the next year (VP, Lienchiang County notice). So a late-2032 reconfirmation may be needed. This extends B1a Q19.
would_change_detail: Whether the IPS framework adds a 2032 reconfirmation step or only one FR sentence.
north_star: The plan follows how her partners actually budget, not only how markets move.

text: What share of the 2031 sleeve should be locked as the floor, given that an 80% lock makes the 2033 range almost a single number while funders reward stretch gifts?
anchor_quote: Rather than promising one exact amount, she wants to communicate a credible range for her potential contribution.
hypothesis: GUESS: 80% may be too high for communication. ASSUMPTION illustration: at the median 2031 sleeve (~US$188k), 80% locked gives a floor of US$165k and 2033 capacity p5/p50/p95 of US$199k/207k/218k (about +/-5%). Kresge asks if leaders' gifts are 'the largest gifts they have ever made' (VP), but the case warns that committing everything limits flexibility. A 60-70% lock may leave a visible upper tier. D3 should tabulate the 50-80% locks.
would_change_detail: Lock share of the 2031 sleeve and the resulting FR range ends and P(top); the IPS floor rule parameter.
north_star: A range that is visibly a range, with a bottom that never moves, is credible to both a statistician and a funder.

text: Should co-sponsor material describe the operating commitment as US$500,000 nominal or at its 2033 value of about US$395k, given that professional recipients book multi-year pledges at present value?
anchor_quote: Laura will make ten annual payments of $50,000 toward the residency's operating expenses, one at the beginning of each year from 2033 through 2042.
hypothesis: GUESS: state both. PwC NFP guide 7.3.2.2: present value 'is the valuation technique typically used when measuring the fair value of a contribution due more than one year from the date of the promise' (VP). F-106 gives US$394,930 at 2033-01-01. Showing only US$500k may look naive to a finance-literate funder.
would_change_detail: Which figure headlines the operating commitment in the FR co-sponsor draft (nominal plus 2033 market value).
north_star: We show her promise the way her partners' accountants will see it.

text: How much of Laura's portfolio should co-sponsor material disclose to prove that the promise is Treasury-backed, without exposing her whole finances?
anchor_quote: Communicates Laura's potential facility contribution to co-sponsors clearly and credibly.
hypothesis: GUESS: disclose form and timing (Treasuries maturing each January 2033-2042; floor in a 2-year Treasury maturing January 2033), not the portfolio total or the sleeve holdings. PwC: collectability considers 'the donor's creditworthiness' (VP). PKF 2019: funders check 'whether the sources of potential revenue are reliable' (VP). Due diligence is on the grantee, not on the donor's wealth.
would_change_detail: Which portfolio facts appear in the FR co-sponsor draft.
north_star: Co-sponsors get proof and Laura keeps her privacy.

text: Because the case bans withdrawals before 2033, which words accurately describe Laura's 2031 floor as a promise backed by assets she still owns, so that 'set aside for the residency' does not overstate it?
anchor_quote: Apart from the two contributions described above, she will neither add to nor withdraw from the portfolio before 2033.
hypothesis: GUESS: the accurate category is a stated commitment backed by named Treasury holdings in her own portfolio that mature in January 2033. It is not a transfer, escrow or restricted fund. Kresge's 'organizational funds' are 'funds set aside by the organization and earmarked' (VP), which is recipient-held money, which her floor is not. This sharpens BS-05's verb choice.
would_change_detail: Verb and noun choice for the floor in the FR draft and in the IPS rule wording.
north_star: One precise verb protects her credibility better than any extra model.

text: Are Taiwan's public culture funders annual and project-based, so they can never give multi-year operating certainty, and which co-sponsor type is the range message really for?
anchor_quote: Any remaining facility cost, and any operating support beyond Laura's commitment, may come from co-sponsors, grants, collaborators, program fees, continued business income, or other sources.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. The MOC artist-village operating subsidy is selected every year, and multi-year grantees must file a self-improvement plan (VP, Lienchiang County notice of the 2022 call). Subsidy tiers up to 90% are SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED (law.moc.gov.tw 403). The facility range mainly addresses private and corporate capital funders; public money is annual and programme-level. Laura's ten years complement it.
would_change_detail: FR audience and emphasis of the co-sponsor draft (generic audience kept, emphasis shifted).
north_star: We show we know how arts money in Taiwan actually flows, without naming or contacting anyone.

text: Do Taiwan public subsidies require a self-funded share (自籌款), so that Laura's fixed US$50k makes the residency eligible for public operating money that could offset its real erosion?
anchor_quote: Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement.
hypothesis: GUESS: likely in some form. SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED: a different MOC programme caps grants at 50-70% of cost and requires '相對足額之自籌款'; the artist-village rules page returned 403. If true, her payments leverage public money beyond her commitment, never for it.
would_change_detail: FR sentence on who covers real erosion of the fixed US$50k and on the leverage value of the operating commitment.
north_star: Her fixed promise becomes the anchor other money attaches to.

text: If the residency is delayed or cannot open, what happens to Laura's facility money, and should co-sponsor material say so, given that a refund promise raised giving in the seed-money experiment?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops.
hypothesis: GUESS: one line. The facility money is released only when the project proceeds; until then it stays in Treasuries as flexibility; the reserve is untouched. List & Lucking-Reiley 2002: 'imposing a refund increased contributions by a more modest 20%' (VP abstract, RePEc).
would_change_detail: One FR sentence in the flexibility section and co-sponsor draft on the delay/cancellation case.
north_star: No dollar is spent on a project that does not happen, and both Laura and co-sponsors can see it.

text: Will co-sponsors see Laura's US$50k a year as the residency's dominant revenue and ask how that dependence falls before 2043, and how can the FR answer in one line without a business plan?
anchor_quote: Funding the residency beyond the final payment in 2042 is outside the scope of the competition.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Kresge asks 'Will you be able to change the mix of revenues that support your organization?' (VP). PKF: funders need to know how a grantee 'would respond to any unexpected revenue shortfalls' (VP). Answer with the case's own framing: 'early operations', the named outside sources, post-2042 out of scope, and flexibility money as optional capacity. Extends B1a Q24.
would_change_detail: One FR sentence in the co-sponsor draft / scope note.
north_star: We answer a funder's standard concentration worry in Laura's favour.

text: Since the seed-money effect is measured as a share of a known campaign goal and the facility cost is deliberately unknown, what can the FR honestly claim about why her contribution matters?
anchor_quote: The total cost of the facility has not been determined.
hypothesis: GUESS: no percentage effect can be claimed. LLR's effect is 'a change in seed money from 10% to 67% of the campaign goal' (VP abstract), which needs a goal. Huck & Rasul show that the 'mere existence of a substantial lead donor' matters (VP abstract), which needs no goal. Define 'meaningful' by firmness, timing and being first, not size. New evidence beyond brief 8.17; extends B1a Q20/B1b Q24.
would_change_detail: FR justification of the contribution; removes a possible over-claim.
north_star: No over-claim, which is itself the case's test.

text: Should one Trading Note reflection tie an executed Treasury purchase to co-sponsor credibility (locking the promise first lets her later range be honest), even though the co-sponsor draft is not expected yet?
anchor_quote: At this stage, your team is not expected to calculate the final size of the
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one clause in one note, no numbers. It shows client knowledge early and connects the three deliverables. The TN guide asks how a trade serves Laura's 'goals, funding needs, or risk' (VRF). The team should pick now which WInS Treasury trade will carry that note (notes cannot be edited, only added to).
would_change_detail: Content of one TN reflection; choice of which executed WInS Treasury trade carries the note text.
north_star: From the first deliverable, judges see a firm that trades for Laura's promises, not for returns.

text: Which single co-sponsor rule belongs in the 500-word IPS, given that the IPS excludes the final range but must set the approach to the facility contribution and then freezes?
anchor_quote: The IPS is not expected to include final operating-reserve calculations, detailed portfolio projections, a final facility-contribution range, or the draft communication to co-sponsors.
hypothesis: GUESS: one rule with no numbers. Its content: the public figure never exceeds what is already bought when announced; the upper tier carries a stated probability; the operating reserve is never a source. Setting it before the freeze protects every later FR range from looking invented.
would_change_detail: IPS content (about 25-40 of 500 words) for the co-sponsor communication rule.
north_star: The frozen IPS already contains the promise-keeping rule the FR later applies.

text: What is the minimum checklist a funder-grade founder contribution statement contains, and which items can be dropped to keep the FR 'part' short?
anchor_quote: Each team must also draft part of Laura's fundraising materials describing this potential contribution for prospective co-sponsors.
hypothesis: GUESS, as a checklist (not prose): (1) the committed floor, its form and maturity; (2) the expected upper part with probability and model; (3) date and currency (US$ binding, NT$ reference); (4) ten operating years already funded separately; (5) unfavourable-market behaviour (contribution falls toward floor, reserve never touched); (6) delay case; (7) what is not promised (facility cost, overruns, post-2042); (8) update schedule. Drop 8 then 6 if space is tight. Sources: Kresge, PKF, ASU 2018-08 (all VP).
would_change_detail: Structure of the FR fundraising part (the students write it).
north_star: Co-sponsors get everything they need in one reading, which is criterion 5 in practice.

text: Should the FR cite institutional readiness rules (for example Kresge's 20-50% raised before applying and written-pledge counting) rather than small-donor seed-money experiments as evidence that Laura's contribution helps?
anchor_quote: A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura's commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. This is new evidence against brief 8.17's objection (experiments are about households): institutions encode the same logic in their own rules (Kresge guide, VP). Caveat: the guide dates from 2011 and says the challenge grant 'is no longer the centerpiece of our work', so cite it as established practice, not current Kresge policy.
would_change_detail: FR evidence/citation choice and Works Cited.
north_star: The right evidence for the right audience shows judgement, not just research.

text: Should Laura's US$50k payments be described as unrestricted general operating support, since flexible operating money is what arts funders say is scarcest?
anchor_quote: Establishing the residency will require funding for the facility as well as reliable support for its early operations.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, within the case's 'operating expenses' wording. BS-17 (Kang 2026, VP in Phase A) says funders can give 'unrestricted operating money'. PwC notes that future-dated promises carry an 'implied time restriction' unless worded otherwise (VP), so the wording changes how the recipient may use the money. No number changes.
would_change_detail: One word/phrase in the FR co-sponsor draft describing the operating payments.
north_star: Her money is the kind funders value most, and we say so in their language.

text: Before more WInS notes are saved (they cannot be edited), should the team fix a three-tier certainty vocabulary (bought/locked, model-expected, possible) so no trade note says 'guaranteed' or 'safe' in a way the IPS and Final Report must later qualify?
anchor_quote: Teams should use each deliverable for its intended purpose while maintaining a clear and consistent investment strategy across all three.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. A4's glossary covers strategy words, not certainty words. The team's own definition is 'certain in nominal USD, barring U.S. Treasury default', so 'guaranteed' is too strong; 'locked in at today's prices' or 'matched' is defensible. Numeric/precise wording preserves credibility when surprises occur (Jenkins, Harris & Lark 2019, VP abstract, ideas.repec.org).
would_change_detail: Wording of every WInS trade note from now on, plus a one-page certainty glossary shared by TN, IPS and FR.
north_star: Laura, a statistics graduate, sees the same careful certainty words in October that she sees in December.

text: Since locking 100% of the sleeve in 2031 costs only about $1k of median 2033 value under the verified model's assumptions, should the 2031 lock share rise from 80% toward 100%, so the co-sponsor range reflects Laura's flexibility choice and currency rather than market risk?
anchor_quote: In 2031, however, the value of her portfolio in 2033 remains uncertain.
hypothesis: GUESS backed by a derived re-run of strategy_mc.py paths (ASSUMPTION inputs): at the median 2031 state, 80% locked gives 2033 p5/p50/p95 about $199k/$207k/$217k; 100% locked gives $206.1k with no market spread. Caveat: the model fixes the 2031 2y yield at 4.81%; D3 must test 3-4%.
would_change_detail: The floor share parameter in the IPS 2031 rule (80% vs 90-100%) and the FR range width.
north_star: Laura can tell co-sponsors a number that is already bought, the strongest credibility a founder can offer.

text: Should the 2031 floor be bought before Laura's very first co-sponsor conversation, so the first number any funder hears is already 'committed, imminent or backstopped', and what record proves it to a funder's due diligence?
anchor_quote: Laura plans to begin approaching potential co-sponsors in 2031, two years before the residency is established.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Kresge's Guide to the Challenge Grant (2011, VP) advises 'Have a significant amount of your campaign pledges committed before the general public ever hears about the campaign' and wants other sources 'committed, imminent or backstopped'. A floor bought after conversations begin means her first number was a forecast.
would_change_detail: Date of the 2031 floor purchase in the IPS rule (first trading days of 2031) and the FR element 'already set aside on [date]'.
north_star: She never walks back a number, because nothing is said before it is bought.

text: Which confidence level should the 2031 statement carry, and should it always use 'dual format' (a calibrated word such as the IPCC's 'very likely' plus its numeric band), never a verbal term alone?
anchor_quote: state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range.
hypothesis: GUESS: about 90%, always numeric, optionally paired with 'very likely'. Budescu et al. 2014 (VP abstract, 24 countries, 17 languages): laypeople read IPCC terms 'closer to 50% than intended'; adding numerical ranges fixes it. The IPCC AR5 note (VP) prefers 'a probability range (e.g., 90-95%)' when information allows.
would_change_detail: The stated confidence level in the FR range statement and a dual-format rule in the fundraising checklist.
north_star: Laura and every co-sponsor read the same probability from the same words.

text: What exactly does our confidence percentage refer to (paths of a stated model, or past two-year periods), and must the fundraising part name that reference class?
anchor_quote: They should also define what they consider a high degree of funding certainty, explain how they evaluated that level of certainty
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one clause giving a natural frequency with its source ('N in 10 simulated paths under named assumptions'). Gigerenzer et al. 2005 (VP abstract): 'even numerical probabilities can be interpreted ... in multiple, mutually contradictory ways ... experts need to specify the reference class'.
would_change_detail: FR method line and one required element of the fundraising checklist.
north_star: A statistician client sees her own discipline, 'what is the denominator?', applied to her promise.

text: Given that about 97% of the 2026-view uncertainty is resolved by 2031, should the Final Report show the 2031 range as a narrow band (about ±5%) for each of three 2031 starting states instead of the 2026-view $159k-$273k band?
anchor_quote: They should explain how favorable and unfavorable market outcomes could affect the amount she can provide.
hypothesis: GUESS with derived numbers from the verified model paths (ASSUMPTION inputs): only 2.8% of 2026-view variance remains after 2030. Conditional 2033 p5-p95: weak 2031 $162k-$177k, median $199k-$217k, strong $246k-$269k (each about 8.9% of its median). This is new evidence on B1a Q18 and B1b Q18.
would_change_detail: FR range width and presentation: a three-row 2031-state table replaces one wide 2026-view band.
north_star: Shows that two years is enough to make her promise precise, which is what the case's timing allows.

text: In NT$ terms, does 2031-2033 exchange-rate risk (2-year p5/p95 -12.1%/+10.6% since 2006) swamp the roughly -4%/+5% market band left in the USD range, so any NT$ figure needs its own band or an 'illustration at a dated rate' label?
anchor_quote: Teams must recommend the dollar range Laura should communicate
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Combined as independent (ASSUMPTION), the NT$ band is roughly ±12%, about 2.5 times the USD band. The USD promise is unchanged; Taiwanese partners should be told US$ is binding and NT$ is a dated illustration with a larger swing.
would_change_detail: FR fundraising currency element; possibly an NT$ band number.
north_star: Respects partners who budget in NT$ with a practical currency fact, not an identity gesture.

text: How should the two ends of the range be labelled so readers do not treat a result just outside a hard edge as a broken promise, without words like 'can' or 'up to' making the top sound likely?
anchor_quote: Rather than promising one exact amount, she wants to communicate a credible range for her potential contribution.
hypothesis: GUESS: hard bottom (bought), soft top described with its probability of being reached. Teigen, Løhre & Hohle 2018 (VP): outcomes 'falling outside a narrow range were deemed to be incorrectly predicted', but a 'can' upper limit made outcomes beyond it 'consistent with the forecast'. Teigen & Filkuková 'Can > will' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED): 'can' predictions are extreme yet believed probable.
would_change_detail: Labels of the floor and top in the FR fundraising part.
north_star: Nothing she says can later be read as a broken promise.

text: Because exceeding a promise earns no more credit than keeping it while breaking it is punished, should the draft treat the bottom as the only promise, and should it show a 'best estimate' at all?
anchor_quote: If Laura promises more than she can ultimately contribute, she could damage her credibility and lose the confidence or participation of co-sponsors.
hypothesis: GUESS: show the floor and the range with its probability in the co-sponsor part; keep the median in the FR analysis. Gneezy & Epley 2014 press release (VP, ScienceDaily): 'exceeding a promise isn't viewed any more highly than keeping a promise'. Dieckmann et al. 2015 (VP): a best estimate shapes the perceived distribution, and may become the remembered number.
would_change_detail: Whether the co-sponsor part shows a central estimate; how the range is positioned.
north_star: Protects Laura from a founder's most expensive public mistake.

text: Should the confidence statement give the chance of missing the range on each side separately (below the floor versus above the top), following the IPCC advice to give reciprocal statements?
anchor_quote: state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. IPCC AR5 note (VP): 'a 10% chance of dying is interpreted more negatively than a 90% chance of surviving ... Consider reciprocal statements'. Derived re-run at the median 2031 state, range from the bought floor to conditional p90: P(inside)=0.90, P(below)=0.000, P(above)=0.10. So every miss is on the harmless side.
would_change_detail: FR range statement reports two side-specific probabilities instead of one '90%'.
north_star: Co-sponsors see that the only surprise possible is a good one.

text: Would a capital funder count any part of Laura's range as money raised, or only a written floor, and should the fundraising part therefore lead with the floor rather than the range or its midpoint?
anchor_quote: A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura’s commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute.
hypothesis: GUESS: only the floor counts. Kresge's counting list (VP, 2011 guide) begins 'Written pledges or cash from individuals, corporations, businesses and foundations'; a forecast range is not on it. So the 'meaningful' signal is carried by the floor's size.
would_change_detail: Headline number of the FR fundraising part (the floor); priority on floor size over the midpoint in strategy design.
north_star: Her number is one a funder can put in its own spreadsheet.

text: Since capital funders expect 'project-cost estimates are firm' but the case leaves facility cost undetermined, what must the fundraising part say so her contribution reads as sized from her portfolio, not a share of an unknown budget, and fixed if costs change?
anchor_quote: The total cost of the facility has not been determined.
hypothesis: GUESS: two checklist elements: sized from what her portfolio can responsibly give, independent of final cost; and it does not rise with overruns (scope adjusts). Kresge readiness indicator 2 (VP): 'Your project-cost estimates are firm and construction timetables have been established.' No budget (out of scope).
would_change_detail: Two required elements in the FR fundraising checklist.
north_star: She sounds like a founder who knows what a funder will ask, without inventing a budget.

text: Should part of Laura's above-floor amount be offered as a 1:1 match for co-sponsor gifts, given field evidence that a match raises giving but larger ratios add nothing?
anchor_quote: Any remaining facility cost, and any operating support beyond Laura’s commitment, may come from co-sponsors, grants, collaborators, program fees, continued business income, or other sources.
hypothesis: GUESS: at most one line, 1:1, above-floor part only, capped at an already-bought amount, never touching the reserve; drop it if it fails 'complexity must earn its place'. Karlan & List 2007 (VP NBER abstract): match raises revenue and response; '$3:$1 and $2:$1 ... had no additional impact'. Evidence is for individual donors, not institutions.
would_change_detail: Whether the FR range design includes a challenge-match element.
north_star: Turns her upside into a lever for others' giving, but only if that is simple and honest.

text: Should the fundraising part state a two-way 'no substitution' rule: co-sponsor money never replaces Laura's ten operating payments, and her operating reserve is never drawn for the building?
anchor_quote: Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one element. The case's asymmetry is a firewall in both directions and answers both funder fears (being asked for running costs, BS-17; quiet backfilling of a founder's promise). 'Supplement, not supplant' is the U.S. public-grant phrase for this (ASSUMPTION, not verified).
would_change_detail: One firewall element in the FR fundraising checklist.
north_star: Shows we understood why the case splits the money the way it does.

text: How can the fundraising part sound confident without overpromising, given evidence that people prefer confident advisers but do not dislike advice given as ranges or numeric probabilities?
anchor_quote: communicates Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors
hypothesis: GUESS: be confident about the method and the floor, numeric about uncertainty, and ban vague hedges. Gaertig & Simmons 2018 (VP): participants 'did not dislike advisors who expressed uncertainty by providing ranges ... numerical probabilities'; 'Advisors benefit from expressing themselves with confidence, but not from communicating false certainty.' van der Bles et al. 2020 (VP): only a small trust drop, 'mostly for verbal uncertainty communication'.
would_change_detail: Tone rules for the FR fundraising part (no hedging words; numbers for uncertainty).
north_star: Sounds like Laura at her best: sure of the plan, honest about the numbers.

text: Which two or three drivers of change should the 2031 statement name in advance, given evidence that explaining uncertainty up front protects trust when numbers later change?
anchor_quote: They should explain how favorable and unfavorable market outcomes could affect the amount she can provide.
hypothesis: GUESS: returns on any unlocked part, the exchange rate for NT$ readers, and Laura's flexibility choice, each with its direction. Dries et al. 2024 (VP): 'communicating uncertainty buffers against a loss of trust when evidence changes'. Jenkins et al. 2019 (VP): numeric predictions least affected when an 'unlikely' outcome occurs.
would_change_detail: The 'what moves it' element of the FR fundraising part.
north_star: If a number changes in 2032, co-sponsors were already told why it might.

text: Should the fundraising part attribute the range and confidence to Laura's investment team, with an as-of date, key assumptions and limits, borrowing the disclosure elements regulated advisers use for hypothetical projections?
anchor_quote: Each team must also draft part of Laura’s fundraising materials describing this potential contribution for prospective co-sponsors.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one attribution/as-of element. The case gives the confidence to the team ('how confident they are') while the materials are Laura's. CFA Asset Manager Code: disclosures 'truthful, accurate, complete, and understandable' (VP via A3). SEC Marketing Rule: disclose 'criteria used and assumptions made' and 'risks and limitations' (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED; sec.gov 403). Borrowed as a checklist, not a legal claim.
would_change_detail: Attribution and as-of element in the FR fundraising part; decision on whose voice carries the confidence.
north_star: A fictional firm behaving like a real regulated one, as the Rules page asks.

text: What minimum checklist must the 'part of Laura's fundraising materials' meet to be credible to a funder's finance reader and a non-specialist at once, and what must be left out?
anchor_quote: Communicates Laura’s potential facility contribution to co-sponsors clearly and credibly.
hypothesis: GUESS checklist: (1) the bought floor in US$ with date and form; (2) the range above it with probability of reaching the top, in dual format, with reference class; (3) chance of missing on each side; (4) drivers named in advance; (5) ten operating years funded separately, plus the two-way firewall; (6) sized from the portfolio, fixed if costs overrun; (7) US$ binding, NT$ dated illustration; (8) who prepared it, when, assumptions and limits; (9) next update date. Leave out: facility cost, jargon, legal claims, personal details, AI-drafted text.
would_change_detail: Structure of the FR fundraising part.
north_star: A co-sponsor finishes reading knowing what Laura gives, how sure it is, and what is already done.

text: How wide can the stated range be before non-specialists find it useless, given that the preference for range forecasts peaks at low imprecision and falls as ranges widen?
anchor_quote: she wants to communicate a credible range for her potential contribution.
hypothesis: GUESS: a top-to-bottom ratio well under about 1.3 reads as informative; 1.7 reads as 'we don't know' (the threshold is an ASSUMPTION). Du et al. 2011 (VP): preference 'peaks for low levels of imprecision and diminishes when the range gets wider'. Yaniv & Foster 1995 (SNIPPET-UNVERIFIED): informative-but-wrong beats correct-but-wide. Derived ratios: 2026-view 1.72; median-2031 floor-to-p90 1.30; p5-p95 1.09.
would_change_detail: Range width chosen for the FR and how it is presented.
north_star: A range narrow enough to plan with is the difference between a pledge and a shrug.

text: Which single Final Report chart shows co-sponsors the floor, range and confidence most clearly: a fan chart from 2027, or a bought-floor bar with a range whisker for three 2031 starting states?

hypothesis: GUESS: bar plus whisker at three 2031 states for co-sponsors; a fan chart, if any, in the method section. Dieckmann et al. 2015 (VP): 'simple graphical representations can decrease the variance in distributional perceptions'. A fan from 2027 repeats the misleading 2026-view width. Fed SEP bands (VP) are the reference design for fans.
would_change_detail: Choice of the FR co-sponsor chart and the data it needs (Q3 table plus floors).
north_star: One picture a co-sponsor could redraw from memory.

text: Should every probability in the fundraising part be numeric, because numbers survive translation and verbal probability words do not, so a Mandarin-reading Taiwanese partner reads the same confidence without the team translating anything?
anchor_quote: In 2033, Laura plans to establish a collaborative creative residency in Taiwan.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Budescu et al. 2014 (VP): under dual format 'interpretations of the terms in various languages are more similar' across 17 languages. Translation stays out of scope; numbers make the text translation-proof at zero cost.
would_change_detail: A 'numbers for every probability' rule in the FR fundraising checklist.
north_star: The plan works for the people in Taiwan who will actually read it.

text: Should the 2031-2033 band be cross-checked against actual historical two-year outcomes of a sleeve-like mix, as the Fed's projection bands use past forecast errors, not only the i.i.d. lognormal model?

hypothesis: GUESS: yes; with about 20% of the sleeve unlocked for two years, even a 2008-type fall moves the 2033 amount by only a few percent. Fed SEP notes (VP): bands 'based on root mean squared errors ... over the previous 20 years' and 'may not reflect ... current assessments'.
would_change_detail: Stated confidence level and bottom of any market band in the FR; a historical worst case shown beside the model p5.
north_star: Laura can check our '9 in 10' against history herself.

text: Should every sentence of the fundraising part pass a 'floor test' (still true if 2033 lands exactly at the floor) and a 'top test' (nothing implies the top is expected), as a pre-submission check against overpromising?

hypothesis: GUESS: yes. It turns the Gneezy & Epley asymmetry (press release VP) and the Teigen et al. 2018 boundary effect (VP) into a five-minute student check.
would_change_detail: A review rule applied to the FR fundraising draft before submission.
north_star: Nothing in the letter she sends could ever become untrue.

text: Should the newly found 2026-27 Investment Competition Guide and Competition Infographic (public SMApply guide page, not in the repo or Phase A) be added to the official set, and which of their sentences change our checklists?

They add a trade-note content list, a hindsight rule, a seven-item 'recognizes' list and 'tradeoffs' as a scored element.

text: Does every WInS trade note from now on contain the four elements the Guide lists (strategy link, supporting research or analysis, and a named role in growth, liquidity, risk management or future funding), and does our Trading Notes blueprint match?

hypothesis: GUESS: the council TN blueprint section 3 lacks an explicit 'supporting research or analysis' element; Wharton's 59-word example names a role and a risk but no evidence. Notes cannot be edited, so a missing element cannot be fixed later; a note citing one checked fact would stand out.
would_change_detail: Four-element spec for every WInS note written from today; update blueprint 01 section 3.
north_star: A note that shows its evidence proves our firm decides on research, not mood.

would_change_detail: Shift writing effort from architecture to Laura-fit and co-sponsor credibility in IPS and FR.
north_star: If thousands of firms offer the same ladder, Laura picks the one that explains it in her terms.

text: When the right answer (match the payments with Treasuries) is textbook, what counts as a 'clear and creative investment thesis' to the readers?

hypothesis: GUESS: creativity is scored on the thesis and its fit to Laura, not exotic instruments: e.g. the 2031 bought-floor-plus-stretch rule, a model-free certainty definition, reporting as a funded ratio. Older Wharton guidance: 'Your strategy should be unique to your team' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). 2018 readers highlighted metaphors and honest reflections as memorable.
would_change_detail: Choose the one creative element that leads the pitch and gets the FR's main chart.
north_star: A correct idea Laura has not seen from other firms is the reason to choose us.

text: Do the readers reward quantitative sophistication (algorithms, optimisation, ML) or restraint, and how many quantitative tools should the Final Report show?

Finale articles praise algorithms and optimisation, but semifinal judge Hahn (who read written reports) warned against 'hiding behind fancy terms and formulas', and 2024 judge Keswani valued 'a little bit of it, but a lot of depth and accuracy' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). One deeply checked ladder pricing plus one honest surplus simulation beats five methods.
would_change_detail: FR analysis list: keep / appendix / drop for bootstrapped forwards, rate models, four-model comparisons.
north_star: A statistics graduate trusts one analysis she can check over five she cannot.

hypothesis: GUESS: test = does it change a recommendation for Laura or a number a co-sponsor hears? DV01, bootstrapping, forward zeros, wrong-way risk fail as terms in the main text; the ideas survive in plain words. The council's 12 concepts are too many.
would_change_detail: FR structure and an IPS vocabulary list (allowed and banned words).
north_star: A plan Laura can repeat to a co-sponsor in one breath is the plan she will choose.

A stable ratio while rates moved proves the hedge worked regardless of P&L. Few teams will do this; it needs WInS values saved from Sept 28.
would_change_detail: Start a daily/weekly WInS value log now; FR chart spec: funded ratio of the WInS book over six weeks (data: WInS values, treasury.gov par curves, official_curve_pv.py).
north_star: Showing the promise stayed funded while markets moved is the proof Laura needs, far better than a return number.

hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Pick three labels now (the promise holdings, the growth sleeve, the floor) and never vary them. Drifting labels ('hedge', 'safe bucket', 'reserve', 'ladder') read as three strategies.
would_change_detail: Every WInS note from today; a glossary line in the FR.
north_star: One strategy told the same way three times is what makes Laura trust it.
