would_change_detail: Order and ask-structure of the Final Report fundraising draft.
north_star: Her own money moves first and is already in place: the strongest credibility signal a range can carry.

text: What does 'financial flexibility as the project develops' buy for someone who builds in stages (overrun buffer, option to expand after proof, or option to pivot), and should the held-back money's asset mix and horizon follow that answer?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops.
hypothesis: GUESS: option to expand first, overrun second. Evidence (VERIFIED-PRIMARY via B8a): 'Always start small'; festival 'way beyond our initial passion project'; 'shipped 10 features'; effectuation 'Lemonade'. Implies part of held-back money stays balanced after 2033 plus a short-Treasury overrun slice; other files size the share but not the use.
would_change_detail: Post-2033 asset mix and horizon of the held-back money; FR definition of flexibility.
north_star: 'Flexibility to grow what works' is a builder's word; a contingency fund is a banker's.

text: Does Laura tolerate losses only she bears (she helped launch an Anti-Resume Project to normalize failure) differently from shortfalls others see (range, payments), so post-2033 held-back money can carry more market risk than the 2031-33 range money?
anchor_quote: If Laura promises more than she can ultimately contribute, she could damage her credibility and lose the confidence or participation of co-sponsors.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes; high tolerance for her own visible failure, low for breaking promises to partners (Pulse Spikes reporter text via B8a, VERIFIED-PRIMARY there). Tension with the overrun-buffer use in Q8; resolve by splitting held-back money by use.
would_change_detail: Risk level of post-2033 held-back money; IPS principle that risk sits only on money nobody else relies on.
north_star: Draws the line where she draws it: between her own risk and other people's trust.

text: Since a -30% equity year in 2030 at 60% sleeve equity cuts the announced 2031 floor by ~18%, should sleeve equity step down in 2029-2030 rather than stay flat until the 2031 lock?
anchor_quote: demonstrates disciplined planning across Laura's changing time horizons and cash-flow needs
hypothesis: GUESS: a small step-down (60% -> 40% in 2030) may cost little median, but no promise breaks (range set after the fact), so it may not earn its complexity; D3 to test. DER: equities lag the locked 5.08% in 42-43% of JPM-model paths over 3-4 years. Investor.gov: shorter horizons 'may prefer to take on less risky or less volatile investments' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Time-based complement to B4a Q16's level triggers.
would_change_detail: Sleeve glide path 2029-2031 and the IPS 'planned changes' answer (R-I21).
north_star: Gives 'changing time horizons' a Laura-specific reason (the 2031 announcement) rather than a generic glide path.

text: Over what horizon and against what hurdle should the sleeve be judged, and should the hurdle be Laura's own riskless alternative (surplus locked at ~5.08%, ~$204k in 2033) rather than the S&P 500?
anchor_quote: This evaluates how that strategy was implemented
hypothesis: GUESS: yes; evaluation horizon 2031 with yearly monitoring; FR's WInS evaluation compares the equity sleeve with the same dollars in an intermediate Treasury fund over six weeks, stating six weeks prove nothing. CFA 2010: 'establishing a minimum time horizon for achievement of performance objectives clarifies when action may be needed to resolve underperformance issues' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Extends B7a Q11 with a client-specific hurdle.
would_change_detail: Final Report benchmark choice and the IPS monitoring clause.
north_star: 'Did the risk we took for you beat what you could have had for sure?' is the only performance question she should care about.

text: Does Laura accept that her facility absorbs every rate move before January 2027 one-for-one (each 25bp fall ~ +$7.3k ladder cost ~ -$9.9k 2033 facility; -100bp ~ -$41k), and should the IPS say so in one clause?
anchor_quote: After establishing the operating reserve in 2033, Laura must decide how much of the remaining portfolio she can responsibly contribute
hypothesis: GUESS: yes; this is the only real competition between her two goals under lock-early. DER from F-102 x forward factor 1.3513 (ASSUMPTION: factor held fixed); P(cost > $300k) ~24% (F-112, ASSUMPTION). Rule design is in B5a Q02/B4a Q06; new is stating the price in facility dollars.
would_change_detail: IPS priority clause naming the price of 'promise first'; supports the pre-2027 rate-rule decision.
north_star: Telling a client the exact price of putting her promise first earns her confidence.

text: In Taiwan building-cost terms, what is the locked-equivalent surplus worth ($204k in 2033 ~ $160k of 2026 construction cost at 3.54%/yr, ~$131k at the 2026 6.53% pace), and should every co-sponsor figure carry a today's-cost equivalent?
anchor_quote: the effect of inflation on portfolio projections and facility costs
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, quote pairs (2033 US$ and today's-building-cost US$). DER with ASSUMPTION rates from F-508; gap is 22-36% of the headline. Extends B1b Q20 with numbers.
would_change_detail: Co-sponsor figures in the Final Report fundraising draft and inflation-assumption section.
north_star: Co-sponsors plan in building costs; Laura would not want to overstate by a quarter.

text: Once the payments are bought, does Laura rank a bigger 2033 facility contribution or more held-back money higher, given the case gives flexibility her own voice ('She recognizes') and the signal a hedge ('may signal')?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility
hypothesis: GUESS: flexibility ranks slightly higher (word analysis VERIFIED-REPO-FILE; her stated values 'avoid siloing', 'fit work around life' via B8a, VERIFIED-PRIMARY there); argues for a clear minority held back and against 'all but a token'. B8b Q7/B4b Q23 size the share; this asks the ranking.
would_change_detail: Facility share of post-reserve surplus and its FR justification.
north_star: Ranking her goals from her own words is 'a thoughtful understanding of the client'.

text: Should the Final Report include a short table 'what the profile does not tell us -> what we assumed -> what changes if we are wrong' (outside resources, use of held-back money, affordable loss, other ideas, currency, who runs the residency)?
anchor_quote: identify the assumptions supporting their recommendation
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, 5-6 rows. CFA 2010: tolerance assessments use 'interviews or questionnaires' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY); contact is banned (R-W16), so stated assumptions replace the interview. One IPS clause 'where the profile is silent we assume…'.
would_change_detail: FR assumptions section table; one IPS clause.
north_star: Saying what you don't know and how the plan survives being wrong makes her feel understood rather than analysed.

text: Should the 500-word IPS be organised on the IPS guide's own five client items (goals, time horizons, liquidity needs, desired funding certainty, need for flexibility) rather than the CFA grid, with legal/tax/unique circumstances in one clause?
anchor_quote: It should reflect your client’s goals, time horizons, liquidity needs, desired degree of funding certainty, and need for financial flexibility.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes; R-I6 is Wharton's own objectives-and-constraints grid (taxes/legal removed, certainty and flexibility added); one ~10-word out-of-scope clause (R-C97).
would_change_detail: IPS outline/skeleton order.
north_star: Judges read against their own list and Laura reads for her goals; one structure serves both.

text: Laura 'has no shortage of ideas' and the case bars withdrawals before 2033: should the IPS present that as her own pre-commitment, with any new idea before 2033 funded outside the portfolio?
anchor_quote: Laura has no shortage of ideas for the future.
hypothesis: GUESS: one low-cost clause with moderate value; 'commitment device' is general behavioural-finance knowledge (ASSUMPTION; D6 to source on a primary page).
would_change_detail: IPS governance clause.
north_star: Treats her many ideas as a strength the plan protects, not a risk it ignores.

text: Does 'the capital required for her goals' grow in 2031, when the announced range's low end becomes a public commitment, so the IPS defines protected capital as reserve (from 2027) plus announced floor (from 2031)?
anchor_quote: protecting the capital required for her goals
hypothesis: GUESS: yes; one definition explains both the 2027 ladder and the 2031 floor purchase and why risk falls after 2031; derives 'bought, not forecast' (brief 8.7) from the case's own words (INTERPRETATION).
would_change_detail: IPS definition of protected capital.
north_star: One definition read straight from her brief carries the whole design.

text: Why is the longest-horizon money (reserve, to 2042) invested most safely while the facility money (needed by 2031-33) takes the risk, and which one line answers a reader who expects 'longer horizon = more stocks'?
anchor_quote: each payment is a fixed $50,000 and is not adjusted for inflation.
hypothesis: GUESS: a fixed nominal promise is matched, not grown; horizon matters for wants, not bought needs. Investor.gov: longer horizons 'may feel comfortable taking on riskier' investments (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). DER: even over 10 years equities lag the locked rate in ~38% of JPM-model paths. B4b Q08 covers practitioner side.
would_change_detail: One explanatory sentence in the FR and possibly one IPS clause.
north_star: Anticipates the first objection an educator would raise.

text: If Laura runs the residency from 2033 ('the next chapter of her career'), may her 'continued business income' shrink exactly when the project needs flexibility, and should the held-back share assume smaller outside income after 2033?
anchor_quote: who is planning the next chapter of her career
hypothesis: GUESS: state as an assumption row (Q15), not a number; nudges the held-back share up. Her 2025 'short break from writing' to teach (B8a, VERIFIED-PRIMARY there) shows her income mix shifts; scenario is fictional (R-W4), so no real plans imported.
would_change_detail: FR assumption statement; possibly the held-back share.
north_star: Thinks about her career after the plan's big date, which few teams will.

text: Should the FR's client section open with one table (goal -> required or desired return -> risk she can bear -> horizon -> where the money sits -> stage when risk switches on/off) instead of a narrative biography?
anchor_quote: Tailors the strategy to Laura's circumstances, priorities, risk considerations, and residency goals
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, 4-5 rows (payments / 2031 floor / facility upside / held-back money); section 1 of the working file drafts the content (not wording). Wharton's old advice 'Don’t use precious space repeating known facts about your client' (B2b, VERIFIED-PRIMARY there).
would_change_detail: FR client-section structure and chart plan.
north_star: Answers 'why us?' in one exhibit: the firm that mapped her money by goal and by date.

text: What job is Laura hiring an asset-management firm to do: grow her money, or let her make public promises in 2031 that she never has to walk back?
anchor_quote: If Laura promises more than she can ultimately contribute, she could damage her credibility and lose the confidence or participation of co-sponsors.
hypothesis: GUESS: the second. Her 2028 money is reputation-driven (R-C27, BS-03). Wharton changed the criterion from 'would win him/her over' to 'earn her confidence' (B2b, VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Product managers frame needs as 'jobs to be done' (INTERPRETATION).
would_change_detail: The central idea of the 50-word IPS pitch and the IPS's first line would name her promise and her credibility, not the portfolio. The FR would open from the 2031 conversation and work backwards.
north_star: She would choose the firm whose plan is built around the thing she actually needs, a promise she can keep in public.

text: What is Laura's required return, and should the IPS say that her needs can be met at below today's Treasury yield?
anchor_quote: An Investment Policy Statement (IPS) outlines an investor’s financial goals, risk tolerance, and guidelines for managing a portfolio.
hypothesis: GUESS backed by derived numbers (IRR of the case flows, inputs VERIFIED-REPO-FILE): 1.05%/yr for the payments alone; 2.10% with a $50k facility in 2033; 3.15% with $100k; 5.25% with $200k; 6.28% with $250k. Treasuries yield 4.98-5.54% (F-001). So the payments plus roughly $190-200k of facility money are reachable at near-Treasury yields, and equity risk pays only for amounts above that.
would_change_detail: Add a 'required return' line to the FR client picture. The IPS risk/return sentence would say that growth is for the facility, not for the promise. This also anchors the top of the 2031 range.
north_star: Few teams will state her actual return objective; doing so shows professional client knowledge rooted in her own cash flows.

text: Should every recommendation be shown against an all-Treasury-sleeve 'control', and is the lift from 60% sleeve equity worth its 5th-percentile cost to Laura?
anchor_quote: she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance between pursuing growth and protecting the capital required for her goals.
hypothesis: GUESS from new evidence (scratch runs of the verified strategy_mc.py; inputs ASSUMPTION). Lock-early 2033 surplus p5/p50/p95, sleeve bonds at 4.0%: 0% equity $177k/$195k/$215k; 30% equity $174k/$202k/$235k; 60% equity $159k/$207k/$273k. At a 5.0% bond assumption: $183k/$201k/$222k (0%) vs $161k/$210k/$277k (60%). So 60% equity adds about +$9k at the median and +$55k at p95, and costs about -$22k at p5. A former A/B tester will ask for the lift over the control. 30-40% equity may be the better 'thoughtful risk'.
would_change_detail: Changes the sleeve equity weight (open in brief section 9) and therefore the WInS mix now. Adds control-vs-plan rows to the FR scenario table. The IPS names the trade-off as 'facility upside vs a lower floor'.
north_star: Showing the control and the lift is how she judged every feature she shipped; it proves our risk earns its place.

text: How should the IPS state Laura's risk tolerance, given that we must infer it without speaking to her, and which evidence would change our inference?
anchor_quote: Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career, she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance
hypothesis: GUESS: willingness is high for her career and the residency but moderate for this money. Her leaps came only after a secured base (B8a #4-#5, VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Ability is zero for the payments, high for the sleeve until 2031, and low for whatever she announces in 2031. A statistics graduate expects the inference to be stated as an inference, with what would change it.
would_change_detail: One IPS clause splitting willingness from ability; an FR 'what would change our view' line; the sleeve equity weight (with Q3).
north_star: An honest, evidence-labelled reading of her risk tolerance reads as understanding, not guesswork.

text: Which time-horizon stages should the IPS name, and at which boundary does Laura's ability to take risk step down?
anchor_quote: demonstrates disciplined planning across Laura's changing time horizons and cash-flow needs
hypothesis: GUESS: five stages. (1) Now to Jan 2027: rate risk before funding (F-111/F-112). (2) 2027-30: sleeve growth, high capacity. (3) 2031-33: the announced floor is bought, near-zero capacity on that part. (4) 2033-42: the reserve pays itself out. (5) The post-2033 flexibility pool. Most teams write 'long-term' once.
would_change_detail: The IPS 'planned changes' clause names the stages. The share of the sleeve locked in 2031 is decided stage by stage.
north_star: Naming her actual horizons, not a generic 'long term', directly scores 'changing time horizons'.

text: Is this portfolio all of Laura's investable wealth or one goal-dedicated pool, and what should the team assume and say?
anchor_quote: Laura’s living expenses and short-term financial needs will be covered by income and financial resources outside the portfolio.
hypothesis: GUESS: treat it as one dedicated pool. Assume nothing about the size of her outside resources, and never use that unknown wealth to justify extra risk. The scenario is fiction about a real person (R-W4), so her real finances must not be guessed.
would_change_detail: An IPS assumption clause. It rules out 'she can afford losses because she has other money' arguments in the IPS and FR.
north_star: Respecting what we do not know about her is part of earning her trust.

text: Should the IPS state one primary goal plus explicit guardrails that are never breached (all ten payments bought; no 2031 announcement above what is bought)?
anchor_quote: The proposed range must also protect the portfolio’s ability to fund the ten-year operating commitment.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. 'Primary metric plus guardrails' is how product teams run experiments. Her resume lists Twitter 'Abuse & Safety' and 'A/B testing' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). The structure fits in 500 words and reads as CFA objectives and constraints.
would_change_detail: Sets the order and shape of the IPS principles paragraph. Each TN reflection names the goal or guardrail its trade serves.
north_star: It speaks her professional language while staying plain English.

text: Should the IPS include a roughly 15-word 'non-goals' clause (not beating the market, not timing rates, not funding beyond 2042, not estimating facility cost)?
anchor_quote: Funding the residency beyond the final payment in 2042 is outside the scope of the competition.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, if it fits the word budget (R-AN39). Product specs list non-goals, and the clause shows that scope was a choice rather than an oversight.
would_change_detail: Adds one IPS clause and an FR scope line.
north_star: A clear scope is what a former PM trusts in a spec.

text: Should every key number in the Final Report carry an evidence grade (observed price / historical estimate / assumption, plus a quality word), as her own 'Match Quality' column does?
anchor_quote: identify the assumptions supporting their recommendation
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Her Rewriting Herstory page publishes 'The [unfinished] results' with a 'Match Quality' column graded Good/Unsure/Bad. Her dance study takes its definitions from the source and states its limits (VERIFIED-PRIMARY, lauragao.com, 2026-09-27).
would_change_detail: Adds a grade column to the FR assumptions table. The IPS says in words that certainty rests on observable prices, not forecasts.
north_star: The plan grades its own evidence the way she grades hers.

text: What rounding rule should the deliverables use so that no number looks more precise than the model behind it?
anchor_quote: state how confident they are that her 2033 contribution will fall within that range
hypothesis: GUESS from derived evidence. A 5.0% vs 6.7% equity assumption moves the median $207k to $200k (F-405); a 5% vs 4% sleeve-bond assumption moves it to $210k. Model uncertainty is about ±$7-10k, so dollar outcomes should go to the nearest $10k and probabilities to the nearest 5 points, with the model named. Treasury-priced costs may keep full digits because they are prices, not forecasts.
would_change_detail: Changes every forecast figure in the FR, the 2031 range and the co-sponsor draft, and adds a one-line rounding rule to the FR.
north_star: A statistics graduate rejects false precision on sight; honest rounding signals competence.

text: What can six weeks of WInS results honestly show a statistics graduate, and should the Trading Notes say that P&L is noise and point to hedge tracking instead?
anchor_quote: The focus should be on the quality of your reasoning and the intended role of each decision
hypothesis: GUESS from derived numbers (ASSUMPTION volatilities). One standard deviation of a 6-week return is about 5.6% for equities and about 2.5% (~$7.6k on $300k) for a 65/35 mix, so results under about $15k are chance. The only 6-week claim with signal is whether the Treasury holding tracks the present value of the ten payments (~$289/bp); B4a Q20 proposes that log.
would_change_detail: TN reflections avoid 'the trade worked' language. The hedge-tracking log starts with the first WInS trade.
north_star: We make only claims she could test, which is what a data-trained client trusts.

text: Should the Final Report attribute the WInS result to its causes (rate moves on the Treasury part, equity moves, commissions, cash drag), as she once attributed 1.5M unexplained ad transactions?
anchor_quote: Final Report. This evaluates how that strategy was implemented
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Resume: 'Investigated cause of 1.5M cases of transactions from unattributed ads' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). A four-bar attribution chart uses data effectively without claiming skill from noise, and it shows the bond moves were offset by the liability's value.
would_change_detail: Record weekly holdings snapshots from now until the Nov 6 freeze, and add an attribution chart to the FR chart list.
north_star: Explaining why the result happened, not just what it was, is the analysis she did professionally.

text: Should Laura's wrong-way income risk be shown as named scenarios (late, smaller, both with falling rates) rather than as a modelled income-market correlation that no data can estimate?
anchor_quote: She will contribute an additional $150,000 at the beginning of 2028, using earnings from publishing advances, speaking engagements, licensing, and other entrepreneurial ventures.
hypothesis: GUESS: scenarios. A correlation coefficient for one author's income against the S&P 500 would be invented, and a statistician would see through it. Three labelled team scenarios beyond the case: deposit 12 months late (her books slipped 9-12 months, B8a); deposit $75k; the joint tail of rates falling before Jan 2027 plus a late deposit.
would_change_detail: Sets D3's modelling approach, the rows of the FR stress table, and the 'timing of cash flows' assumption wording.
north_star: Honest scenarios instead of invented statistics respect her training.

text: Before submitting, should the team usability-test the co-sponsor paragraph and the IPS rules with about five non-finance readers and report what changed, as she tested products with nurses and doctors?
anchor_quote: communicates Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Resume: 'usability tests with nurses and doctors', 'Beta-tested MVP with 300K+ users' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). She also makes NPR explainer comics. A 30-minute restate-in-your-own-words test catches jargon and gives real Articulation evidence; few teams will do it. It involves no contact with Laura.
would_change_detail: Adds a test step before Dec 4. The Articulation section reports the finding (e.g. 'k of 5 misread X, so we changed Y') and the fundraising wording is revised.
north_star: We test our message the way she tests products, so co-sponsors understand it the first time.

text: Who exactly will read her 2031 fundraising material, and should the draft answer the first question of 2-3 named reader types (grant-maker, institutional partner, private donor) rather than 'co-sponsors' in general?
anchor_quote: A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura’s commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Her Philly Happy Hours project was built 'for various types of students', with persona sections such as 'For the student drowning in debt' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Viability, operations-funded and skin-in-the-game are the likely first questions of the three types; D5 to confirm.
would_change_detail: Sets the content checklist for the FR fundraising draft.
north_star: Writing for her real audiences makes the draft something she could actually use.

text: Should the Final Report include one simple visual of the promise (ten 'bought' blocks plus a facility-range bar) that she, as an illustrator, could redraw for co-sponsors?
anchor_quote: uses data effectively to support conclusions
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one visual only, simple enough to redraw by hand and carrying the core claim of bought vs estimated. She makes data visualisations and Tableau reports (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). A decorative infographic would fail her 'No more gimmicks.' test. The IPS bans graphics, so this goes in the FR only.
would_change_detail: Adds one FR chart spec: data = ten payment dates marked bought, the 2031 floor, and the p50/p95 band from D3.
north_star: It gives her a tool in her own medium, not a finance chart.

text: Should the co-sponsor wording be written to survive translation into Mandarin (no idioms, US$ every time, a dated NT$ reference, 'confidence' defined in words)?
anchor_quote: Teams must recommend the dollar range Laura should communicate
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, at near-zero cost. Her resume lists 'Languages: Mandarin Chinese' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY), the residency is in Taiwan, and 'dollar' is ambiguous there (BS-04). The team only writes translatable English and does not translate anything itself.
would_change_detail: Adds to the FR fundraising draft style checklist: US$ labels, an NT$ reference with its date, and no idioms such as 'skin in the game' or 'upside'.
north_star: It shows we thought about where her words will actually be read.

text: How should the team describe the growth sleeve's AI and mega-cap concentration and its own AI use, given that Laura has built ML and AI products?
anchor_quote: If you use AI to assist you in any way during the competition, how you use it must be recorded in your Works Cited pages.
hypothesis: GUESS: describe both neutrally and exactly. Index concentration is a diversification fact taken from the issuer's holdings page, not a values judgement on her behalf. AI use should be stated modestly: what AI did and what the students did. Resume: 'Growth ML (2018-2019)', client 'AI-powered online learning software' (VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Her public views on generative AI in art are unchecked (search budget exhausted).
would_change_detail: Shapes the FR concentration sentence and the Works Cited AI statement, and rules out an 'AI-avoidance' tilt without her stated preference.
north_star: No false assumptions about her values; overclaiming is what an ML practitioner distrusts.

text: What is the smallest set of rules that still passes all five case tests, and can each extra rule show a measurable improvement?
anchor_quote: Your goal is to present a clear, cohesive, and well-supported investment strategy.
hypothesis: GUESS: three rules may suffice: (1) buy the payments when the money arrives, with a rates-fall variant; (2) a fixed sleeve mix with a rebalancing band; (3) in 2031 announce only what is bought plus a stated upside. The TWD quote, Taiwan tilt and glide paths each must show a lift in a number or be dropped. This is her 'Always start small' and last year's lesson in one test.
would_change_detail: Sets the IPS rule list, and adds a 'lift' line per extra rule in the FR.
north_star: Least complexity for the most value is both her craft ethic and our design principle.

text: Does the plan show Laura, in one table, how each goal fails softly (payments, the 2031 announcement, the facility, flexibility), and who would notice?
anchor_quote: They should explain how favorable and unfavorable market outcomes could affect the amount she can provide.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, a four-row table. Payments fail only on a U.S. Treasury default; the announcement fails only if she announces more than is bought; the facility gets smaller but never negative; flexibility absorbs overruns. She co-founded an Anti-Resume Project to normalise failure and worked on Twitter safety (B8a; VERIFIED-PRIMARY), so she would likely trust calm disclosure of failure modes.
would_change_detail: Adds an FR fail-softly table and one bad-case line in the co-sponsor draft.
north_star: Showing how the plan fails gracefully earns more trust than hiding the failures.

text: Which rejected alternatives (growth-first, rolling short, equity-heavy, all-Treasury) should the Final Report show with one number each, as the team's experiment log?
anchor_quote: Judges want to understand not only what your team decided to do, but also the reasoning, assumptions, and tradeoffs behind those decisions. (2026-27 Investment Competition Guide p.5, VERIFIED-PRIMARY per B7a)
hypothesis: GUESS: three rejected arms, each with one number and the reason it was dropped (growth-first misses 3-8%; tiering +$20k per -100bp; the all-Treasury control from Q3). A product person reads a decision without alternatives as untested.
would_change_detail: Adds a small FR 'options we tested' table; one TN reflection can reference the test.
north_star: Showing the tested variants proves the decision process she would expect from any team she hires.

text: Which of Laura's own verified ideas can the strategy echo honestly, and which proposed echoes fail verification or become tokenism?
anchor_quote: The only person who needs to believe in something is yourself.
hypothesis: GUESS from VERIFIED-PRIMARY evidence. Fails: seed 17's 'fall safely'. The Kirby page says the heroine is a 'top rock climber' who 'suffers an injury that sidelines her', 'Falling' means falling in love, and 'Queen of Balance' is publisher copy about a fictional character. The pull quote is unattributed (B8a/B8b). Passes, sparingly: 'If what you want doesn’t exist, create it yourself' (no iBonds fund exists for 2038-42, F-206, so those rungs are built from individual Treasuries); her Match Quality grades; her floor-first career leap.
would_change_detail: Removes book-title metaphors from all deliverables. At most one citation-backed echo in the FR, in the team's words, and none in the IPS pitch.
north_star: Honest echoes feel like being understood; decorative ones feel like being analysed.

text: When she compares firms, would Laura trust one that says plainly which parts need almost no management (the bought payments) and which it actively manages, and discloses fees accordingly?
anchor_quote: At the beginning of 2027, Laura plans to invest $300,000 with an asset management firm.
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Saying that part of the plan runs itself is a costly honesty signal, and it fits her CFPB internship and financial-literacy teaching (B8a). The CFA Code requires fee disclosure (F.4.d via SH-25). A 0.5% fee cuts the median surplus by about $17k (A3 BS-01, ASSUMPTION).
would_change_detail: Adds a fee assumption to the FR projections and an IPS clause saying which parts are 'set and hold' and which are 'managed'.
north_star: Candour about what she does not need us for is exactly what makes her choose us.

text: How many sentences should describe Laura as a person rather than her goals, and what may each rest on, so that she feels understood rather than analysed?
anchor_quote: While the client is real, the financial scenario is developed specifically for the competition.
hypothesis: GUESS: very few, perhaps 2-3 in the FR and 1 in the IPS. Each must link a verified professional fact or case wording to a decision ('because her 2028 money depends on reputation, we...'). Psychological readings of her identity, or claims about her real plans, feel like being analysed and break the privacy and tokenism rules.
would_change_detail: Adds a checklist rule for all three deliverables: each sentence about Laura = fact + source + decision.
north_star: Understanding shows in the plan's fit, not in commentary about her.

text: Should the facility contribution be framed as an amount committed in 2033 and drawn as the project needs it, rather than a lump sum paid on 1 January 2033?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops.
hypothesis: GUESS: possibly. The undrawn part stays in short Treasuries, which keeps flexibility at little cost and matches her staged scaling of Pride in Panels ('We definitely hope to offer more as the festival grows', B8a, VERIFIED-PRIMARY). Use it only if D5 finds that funders accept staged founder pledges, since it adds a moving part.
would_change_detail: Sets the form of the FR facility recommendation and the verb in the co-sponsor draft ('commits..., drawn as construction proceeds').
north_star: It matches how she has actually grown institutions, and it protects her flexibility.

text: When every tested design has about the same median 2033 surplus, what rule should choose between them: the p5 Laura can accept, the p95 she hopes for, the floor co-sponsors can bank, or the simplest structure?
anchor_quote: she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance between pursuing growth and protecting the capital required for her goals.
hypothesis: Guess: the rule most like Laura is 'highest bought floor that still leaves real upside'. Across seven designs, medians sit within $201k-$214k while p5 runs $130k-$183k and p95 $222k-$332k (DER, B10a Appendix A). Her documented leap came after a secured base (Inverse 2022, VP). The co-sponsor task punishes a missed low end (R-C66). So at equal medians, prefer the higher known floor and fewer moving parts.
would_change_detail: IPS: one selection-rule sentence on how the balance was chosen; IPS answer to R-I11. The FR shows the design comparison table.
north_star: Laura sees her own rule (secure the base, then leap) become the plan's selection rule, not a generic 'moderate' label.

text: Should the sleeve become a barbell: in January 2028 lock a facility floor in a Treasury maturing just before 2033 and hold the rest 100% in broad equity, instead of a rebalanced 60/40 sleeve plus an 80% lock in 2031?
anchor_quote: Rather than promising one exact amount, she wants to communicate a credible range for her potential contribution.
hypothesis: Guess: yes, pending a fat-tail test. DER (JPM equities, sleeve bonds 5%, 5y 4.98%): current plan $161k/$210k/$277k (p5/p50/p95). Barbell 50% locked: $163k/$210k/$293k, with a ~$100k floor known in 2028. 65% locked: $175k/$208k/$265k. Under the Vanguard midpoint: current $157k/$204k/$269k, barbell 50% $159k/$203k/$280k. The cost is a wider 2031 range (equity at risk until 2033). A rough low end of floor + 75% of the 2031 equity value (~$172k at medians) is missed in ~3% of paths (ASSUMPTION lognormal, not yet simulated).
would_change_detail: Sleeve structure and floor timing, fixed before the IPS freeze on Nov 6; FR range tables; the WInS sleeve bond slot (see IBTM question).
north_star: It mirrors how Laura took her biggest career risk (contract first, then a full leap), where a 60/40 half-leap is what thousands of teams will write.

text: With Vanguard's June-2026 model giving U.S. equities 4.2%-6.2% a year (about today's 10-year yield) against JPM's 6.7%, should the FR show both houses, and should the IPS say that this year Laura's growth comes mostly from bond yields, with stocks adding range?
anchor_quote: use reasonable return assumptions consistent with their strategy.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. Vanguard VCMM (22 Jul 2026, VP): U.S. equities 4.2%-6.2%, developed ex-U.S. 4.5%-6.5%, EM 2%-4%. At the Vanguard midpoint: lock-early sleeve medians $201k/$204k/$204k at 0/60/100% equity; growth-first median $205k vs lock-early $204k, with a miss of 4.5% (DER). New versus brief section 8.5: a second house removes the median gain entirely.
would_change_detail: FR projection tables and assumptions list (two-house table, returns as a range); IPS risk/return sentence.
north_star: A statistics graduate trusts a plan whose conclusion survives the assumption that matters most. Rivals quoting one equity number look naive.

text: Should the IPS describe balance goal by goal (promise: no market risk; bought floor: none; upside: full market risk), because the blended equity share (~1.5% in 2027, ~20% in 2028-30, ~4% in 2031-32) would read to Laura as 'no growth'?
anchor_quote: Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career, she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance
hypothesis: Guess: yes. DER medians: equity 1.5% of the portfolio in 2027, 20.4% in 2028 (matches F-409), 4.1% after the 2031 lock. SMApply counts 'funding purposes' as diversification (R-AN45), which is the official hook for per-goal language.
would_change_detail: IPS risk-tolerance/balance sentences; FR allocation chart shows three pots over time, not one blended equity line; TN reflections name the pot each trade serves.
north_star: Laura feels her 'thoughtful risks' were placed where they belong, not ignored.

text: What does Laura pay our firm for when about two-thirds of her money sits in a hold-to-maturity ladder, and should the IPS state that the fee applies to the sleeve only or is flat?
anchor_quote: At the beginning of 2027, Laura plans to invest $300,000 with an asset management firm.
hypothesis: Guess: an honest fee line is a 'why us' asset. DER: no fee median $210k. 0.5%: sleeve-only $206k, all assets $193k. 1.0%: sleeve-only $202k, all assets $177k (-16%). A3 BS-01 found no fee assumption anywhere; the CFA Asset Manager Code requires fee disclosure (F.4.d, VP via A3).
would_change_detail: IPS/FR fee and governance line; FR surplus tables net of the stated fee.
north_star: She chooses the firm that is honest about what it earns and what it actually does; almost no team mentions its own fee.

text: Would a rival that holds the whole sleeve in Treasuries (facility fully bought by 2028) beat us on Investment Strategy by being simpler and more certain, or would judges mark it down for ignoring 'pursuing growth'?
anchor_quote: Teams may reach different conclusions about risk, asset allocation, liquidity, return expectations, funding confidence, the facility contribution, and the financial flexibility Laura should preserve.
hypothesis: Guess: it is the strongest attack from safety, but it loses on R-C37/R-C38 and almost removes the uncertainty the case asks teams to explain. DER: all-Treasury $183k/$201k/$222k vs ours $161k/$210k/$277k; under the Vanguard midpoint the median gap is only $3k. Our answer must say why we keep risk: the upside is the flexibility 'as the project develops'.
would_change_detail: FR 'alternatives considered': name this rival and the reason we rejected it; a possible decision if the reason proves weak.
north_star: Showing the safer plan we rejected, and why, proves our risk was chosen for her.

text: If 80-100% of the sleeve is a bought floor in 2031, the co-sponsor range shrinks toward one number: does that dodge the case's uncertainty task, and should the FR show the range narrowing from the 2027 view to 2031 to 2033?
anchor_quote: In 2031, however, the value of her portfolio in 2033 remains uncertain.
hypothesis: Guess: show the funnel. DER: a 100% floor makes the surplus equal the floor (a point). An 80% floor gives $129k/$167k/$219k, with the surplus at least 25% above the floor in 58% of paths. A 50% floor gives a $104k median floor. The 2027 view spans $161k-$277k.
would_change_detail: Floor share (80% vs lower); FR funnel chart of p5/p50/p95 by year; the co-sponsor uncertainty wording.
north_star: Co-sponsors see uncertainty shrink on a schedule: credibility shown, not claimed.

text: Should the 2031 pledge be tied only to money already bought, with the equity upside labelled as Laura's flexibility money (never promised), so the range cannot be missed at the low end and flexibility grows in good markets?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. One split answers two demands: the bought floor is the credible pledge, and the unbought upside is the flexibility. It fits her 'Always start small' staging (B8a/B8b, VP there). The barbell makes the split physical.
would_change_detail: What the top of the 2031 range is made of; FR fundraising checklist verbs ('set aside' for the floor, 'may add' for upside); an IPS rule.
north_star: Laura never has to un-promise anything, and her upside becomes an option she controls.

text: Should the facility floor be built by a ratchet (a third of the target locked each January 2029, 2030, 2031) instead of on one date in 2031, to protect Laura against a crash in the year before she pitches co-sponsors?
anchor_quote: They should explain how favorable and unfavorable market outcomes could affect the amount she can provide.
hypothesis: Guess: it helps at p5, but the barbell may make it moot. DER: one date gives $161k/$210k/$277k and a floor of $129k/$167k/$219k. Thirds give $171k/$208k/$259k and a floor of $137k/$165k/$201k. After a bottom-decile 2030, the floor median is $142k (one date) vs $156k (thirds). This gives B4a Q16 its first numbers.
would_change_detail: Floor timing rule; FR floor distribution; an IPS clause if adopted.
north_star: It protects Laura's good luck as well as her promise, at the moment her credibility is on the line.

text: If the ladder costs more than $300k on purchase day, is 'buy long rungs now, buy the 2033-36 rungs with the 2028 deposit' nearly riskless, and how big is the joint tail if the deposit then fails?
anchor_quote: She will contribute an additional $150,000 at the beginning of 2028
hypothesis: Guess: the rule is sound and the tail is small. DER (ASSUMPTION: 71bp yield vol, duration 5.2-6.4y, stock-rate correlation 0/0.4): with a $150k or $75k deposit, 0% of paths are short. With $0, 24-28% of paths are short by $8-10k on average (1.6-2.0% of $500k). Staging on purpose when the ladder is affordable adds only +$3k at the median. This sizes the brief's 'UNANSWERED' joint tail.
would_change_detail: FR risk register (joint tail ~$8-10k in ~1 in 4 zero-deposit paths); the IPS contingent rule written as a funded-ratio rule.
north_star: The plan names its one residual weakness and its size, which a statistics-trained client rewards.

text: Does any lock timing, for example buying the whole ladder with both deposits in January 2028, give Laura materially more upside?
anchor_quote: For long-term projections, teams should begin with Laura's $300,000 investment in 2027, add the $150,000 contribution in 2028
hypothesis: Guess: no. DER: a 2028 lock gives median +$4k, p95 +$54k, p5 -$31k. With a $75k deposit, payments are short in 0.6-1.6% of paths; with $0, in 37-39% (mean $24-29k). New versus brief 8.1: this tests the one-year delay with the deposit present.
would_change_detail: One FR 'alternatives considered' sentence (we tested waiting a year; ~+$4k median, payments exposed if the deposit fails). Confirms the decision.
north_star: Shows Laura we looked for more upside for her before recommending safety.

text: In WInS, should the growth money's short-Treasury slot be a defined-maturity fund ending December 2032 (the facility date) rather than a 1-3 year Treasury fund, so every holding has a job tied to a date?
anchor_quote: an intermediate-term U.S. Treasury bond ETF to reduce portfolio volatility and begin preparing for Laura's future operating commitment
hypothesis: Guess: yes if a dated floor is adopted. Primary IBTM (iShares iBonds Dec 2032; per S1, VP: duration 5.05y, YTM 5.09%, 0.07%, $555m, ~216k sh/day; not on the 2025-26 list). Alternate: a late-2032 Treasury note/STRIP. Alternate: keep VGSH (on the 2025-26 list, line 1113). PENDING APPROVAL CHECK: confirm on this year's WInS approved list/rules before trading. Watch the overlap with the Jan 2033 payment rung and the position limit.
would_change_detail: WInS-now: swap one security before notes are written; a TN candidate about the facility floor.
north_star: Every holding answers 'which of Laura's dates is this for?', the question she will ask.

text: Should the plan state that it locks at the highest 10-year Treasury yield since 2007, and pre-commit to no regret if rates rise after the lock?
anchor_quote: 10Y 5.18% on 2026-09-24 is the highest daily close since 2007-07-06 (F-004)
hypothesis: Guess: yes, as a checkable fact plus a written rule. A +100bp move after the lock means the ladder would have cost $264,890 instead of $292,264 (~$27k regret, invisible to the payments; F-102). Laura's own regret rule, 'you're always going to regret not doing it' (Overachiever 2021, VP via B8a), fits locking at a 19-year high.
would_change_detail: TN reflection on the first hedge trade; IPS 'why now' clause.
north_star: Gives Laura a fact she can check and a rule against second-guessing, not a rate forecast.

text: Should the WInS hedge be built in two dated steps under a rule written in advance, so the Trading Notes rehearse Laura's January-2027 lock decision and show a strategy 'tested or refined', without inventing a decision?
anchor_quote: This shows how selected investment decisions reflected, tested, or refined the team's developing strategy.
hypothesis: Guess: worth it only if the team would split the purchase even without notes. Laura's real problem is rate risk before the lock (the ladder cost > $300k on 173 of 185 days in 2026, F-111). Constraints: the day-trading ban, the position limit, and B8a 'No more gimmicks'.
would_change_detail: WInS-now order plan (one session vs two dated steps); TN notes 1-2 content.
north_star: The notes show Laura's hardest real decision practised in public, not a one-click portfolio.

text: Should the IPS justify where risk sits with the case's own asymmetry, that outside money may fill a facility shortfall but never an operating shortfall?
anchor_quote: Teams may not rely on co-sponsors, grants, program fees, or other outside funding to meet this requirement.
hypothesis: Guess: yes. 'Risk sits only where others can help' is a one-clause, case-derived reason for the whole design. R-AN6 notes the asymmetry, but no file uses it to justify where the risk sits.
would_change_detail: IPS principle sentence; pitch content checklist.
north_star: The plan's logic visibly comes from her case, not from a textbook.

text: Is part of 'pursuing growth' the growth of what the residency can raise, since a bought, credible floor may pull in co-sponsor money, and can the IPS say so without overclaiming?
anchor_quote: A meaningful personal contribution may signal that the residency is financially viable, demonstrate Laura's commitment to the project, and make potential co-sponsors more willing to contribute.
hypothesis: Guess: yes, as a mechanism only (brief 8.17: seed-money effect is not a prediction). A floor that cannot be missed may be worth more to co-sponsors than an expected value that might be missed. Keep it to one clause to avoid fancy framing.
would_change_detail: IPS balance sentence; FR fundraising checklist.
north_star: Reframes her growth as growth of the residency, which is what she actually wants to grow.

text: A pension at ~152% funded grows its surplus with no deadline, but Laura's surplus has a date (2033) and a public promise (2031): is the right professional analogue a pension surplus glidepath or a dated floor-plus-upside, and where should the FR say we depart from pension practice?
anchor_quote: Laura plans to begin approaching potential co-sponsors in 2031, two years before the residency is established.
hypothesis: Guess: Russell (Jul 2026, VP: 'lock down the benefits promised, then grow surplus assets with a prudent process and disciplined understanding of risk') fits the promise half. A pension's surplus has no deadline or audience, so a dated floor is needed for Laura.
would_change_detail: FR professional-practice paragraph: one sentence on the departure from pension practice.
north_star: Shows the team knows the professional template and exactly where Laura differs from it.

text: Do the barbell's and ratchet's advantages survive fat tails and real crash sequences (2000-02, 2008, 2022), or are they artefacts of the i.i.d. lognormal model?
anchor_quote: i.i.d. lognormal returns (no fat tails), no fees (brief section 11, known gaps in strategy_mc.py)
hypothesis: Guess: the barbell's p5 holds (its floor is bought regardless of path); its p95 depends on long bull runs; rebalanced 60/40 does better in choppy markets. A historical block bootstrap would settle it.
would_change_detail: Adopt the barbell or not; FR tables.
north_star: A statistics graduate trusts a design tested on history, not only on a smooth model.

text: Which single Laura-specific, checkable claim would make a judge who has read fifty 'lock + growth sleeve' plans say ours is different?
anchor_quote: Your team hopes to develop the investment strategy that Laura ultimately chooses
hypothesis: Guess: 'the co-sponsor floor is bought in 2028, so the low end of the range cannot be missed' (needs the barbell) or 'risk sits only where others can help'. The two-house returns and fee honesty are supporting evidence. Rivals using AI may converge on lock + sleeve (A3 BS-10).
would_change_detail: Pitch content checklist and IPS thesis line.
north_star: This is the North Star itself: one reason Laura can repeat to a co-sponsor.

text: With the 2028 deposit present (the case says she 'will' make it), a 70-95% lock also shows no payment shortfall in the model; what is our real reason to lock 100%, and where are we overstating it?
anchor_quote: Teams may reach different conclusions about risk, asset allocation, liquidity, return expectations, funding confidence, the facility contribution, and the financial flexibility Laura should preserve.
hypothesis: GUESS: full lock is still best, but for range and stressed-deposit reasons, not base-case certainty. DERIVED (research/insight_v1/scripts/B10b_designer_checks.py, JPM inputs, ASM): $150k deposit -> shortfall 0.00% at 100/90/80/70% lock, median surplus $210k/$212k/$213k/$214k, p5 $150k/$139k/$128k/$117k; 0% lock 2.10% shortfall, median $221k, p5 $34k. With $75k deposit 70% lock 0.08%, 50% 1.74%, 0% 11.72%. Price of certainty ~ $11k median (~5%) for removing ~2% break risk and +$116k at p5.
would_change_detail: IPS reasoning sentence for the full lock (drop any 'anything less fails' claim; state the price of certainty); FR comparison table adds the lock-share frontier and the 'why not a partial lock' answer.
north_star: A statistics graduate gets the true, priced trade-off instead of a claim she could disprove.

text: Should the IPS headline promise 'fully funded by January 2028 at the latest' rather than 'the $300,000 buys the promise', since the latter is true only at September 2026 rates?
anchor_quote: Above $300k on 173 of 185 trading days; at or below $300k only on the 12 days since 2026-09-10 (F-111)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes. Designers likely set round numbers before September, when $300k did not buy the ladder, so they expected both deposits plus growth. DERIVED (flat-curve parallel-shift ASM): ladder = $300k at 5.09% (-27bp); $300k + PV of 2028 deposit ($443k) covers it down to ~1.16% (-420bp); with a $75k deposit down to ~2.90% (-250bp). A funded-ratio headline survives any plausible January curve.
would_change_detail: Elevator pitch and first IPS sentence (what we promise and when); one FR sensitivity line with the break-even rate falls re-computed on the zero curve.
north_star: She gets a promise that does not depend on luck with the calendar.

text: Does answering the reserve question with 'it is the 2027 ladder and it changes by itself' satisfy the case's size / initial composition / change requirement, or will it read as a dodge?
anchor_quote: Teams must recommend its size and initial asset composition and explain how its composition should change, if at all, as the annual payments approach and are made.
hypothesis: GUESS: allowed and strong only if all three items are named with numbers: size (market value $394,930 on 1/1/2033 plus face $500k), composition (ten zero-coupon rungs, one per January), change (automatic maturity roll-down). DERIVED (flat 5.35% ASM): duration 4.07y (2033) -> 2.79y (2036) -> 0.97y (2040) -> 0 (2042), no trades.
would_change_detail: FR reserve section checklist (three named items + 'funded 2027, designated 2033' sentence) and a roll-down chart of value and duration by year.
north_star: She can see exactly what sits in her reserve every year and why it needs no trading.

text: Our whole-portfolio equity share runs about 1.5% (2027) to 20% (2028) to 4% (2031); will readers who expect the glide path in Wharton's own example read this hump as incoherent, and what one clause explains it?
anchor_quote: which principles will guide decisions as funding dates approach and payments are made (2026-27 Investment Competition Guide p.2)
hypothesis: GUESS: the hump is right (risk capacity switches on with the 2028 deposit, ~152% funded per B9a, then falls toward the facility date) but must be explained as two paths: zero risk on the promise, a glide path on the surplus. DERIVED: 2027 = 0.6 x $7,736 / $300k = 1.5%; 2028 = 20.4% (F-409); 2031 after 80% floor lock ~4.2% (ASM sleeve $190k, ladder $356,384).
would_change_detail: IPS sentence on how allocation changes over time; FR chart 'equity share by year, promise vs surplus'; TN reflection wording if WInS equity differs from the 2027 book.
north_star: A plan whose risk follows her cash flows, not a textbook age rule.

text: The case says teams 'must recommend the dollar range' and that the 2033 value 'remains uncertain' in 2031, yet our 2031 floor rule nearly removes that uncertainty; do we give a dollar range today, a rule, or both, without drifting into the 'one exact amount' the case rejects?
anchor_quote: In 2031, however, the value of her portfolio in 2033 remains uncertain.
hypothesis: GUESS: both. Today's-view dollar range with the model named (floor p5/p50/p95 $127k/$165k/$217k, F-402) meets the 'must'; the 2031 rule shows how she will say it; one sentence explains why it narrows (~+/-5% in a 2031 view, B6a/B6b). Remaining width should come from a stated flexibility choice, not markets. New vs B1a/B6: the designer-premise and literal 'must' framing.
would_change_detail: FR range section structure (dollar range + rule); the 2031 lock-share parameter treated as a communication choice.
north_star: She can say one sentence to funders that is still true in 2033.

text: Our facility rule is 'whatever the sleeve becomes' and flexibility is 'mainly leftover'; what explicit split rule should we state, and what should it be anchored to, so it does not read as generic next to rivals' crisp percentages?
anchor_quote: She recognizes that committing all remaining assets could limit her financial flexibility as the project develops.
hypothesis: GUESS: a rule of the form 'contribute the bought floor plus a stated share of the remainder; keep the rest as project flexibility'. Candidate anchors: the case's 'as the project develops', Laura's staged scaling (B9a Q8), needs/wants/wishes tiers (B4b). The share is the team's decision; without one, 'responsible' is only asserted.
would_change_detail: Team decision on the facility/flexibility split; one IPS clause; FR table of contribution vs kept flexibility under p5/p50/p95.
north_star: She keeps room to act as the residency grows, the way she has built everything else.

text: Under a floor-plus-cap range rule, where does good-market money go, and does sending it to 'flexibility' undercut the case's 'meaningful contribution' signal and its demand to show how favourable outcomes affect the amount?
anchor_quote: They should explain how favorable and unfavorable market outcomes could affect the amount she can provide.
hypothesis: GUESS: state the top of the range as a promise ceiling and any upside above it as her 2033 choice (extra gift or flexibility). Funders count only the unconditional part (B6a Q1), so the cap costs nothing with them, but the favourable case must visibly change something.
would_change_detail: Favourable-outcome sentence in the FR fundraising-draft checklist and the facility rule.
north_star: Good luck is hers to direct, and she never has to walk a number back.

text: Should the Final Report show that the reserve design many rivals will propose, an equity 'bucket' for the 2040-42 payments, needs 1.8-2.6 times the Treasury price?
anchor_quote: Portfolio Analysis: Demonstrates understanding and effective use of investment concepts and tools; integrates quantitative and qualitative analysis
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one line or a small table. DERIVED (JPM large cap 6.70%/16.47%, lognormal ASM; B10b_designer_checks.py): equity needed in 2033 per $50k payment at 95% = $61.5k/$60.4k/$59.1k (2040/41/42), at 99% ~ $81k; Treasury price $34.7k/$33.0k/$31.3k (flat 5.35% ASM) -> 1.77-1.89x (95%), 2.33-2.58x (99%).
would_change_detail: FR Portfolio Analysis: one sentence or table showing the tested-and-rejected alternative; also an Articulation example.
north_star: She sees we checked the tempting option with her own statistics toolkit.

text: A certainty definition that needs no model can look like skipping 'explain how they evaluated'; what stress table and residual-risk list prove it, and should the U.S. default residual carry a market-implied number?
anchor_quote: They should also define what they consider a high degree of funding certainty, explain how they evaluated that level of certainty, and identify the assumptions supporting their recommendation.
hypothesis: GUESS: a table where the payment row never moves (rates +/-200bp, equities -40%, 2028 deposit $0 or late, TWD +/-12%) plus a named residual list (Treasury default, operations, pre-purchase rate move, coupon reinvestment if no STRIPS). A CDS-implied default probability would give a number; the page tried (worldgovernmentbonds.com) loads data by JavaScript, so none verified.
would_change_detail: FR certainty-evaluation table; possibly one IPS clause stating a confidence number with its residual named.
north_star: A statistics graduate sees the certainty claim tested, not asserted.

text: Rivals who buy the reserve in 2033 at cautious rates will show reserves of about $405-440k; will a first-screen reader read our $395k as smaller and so riskier, and how do we show the rate was locked in 2027?
anchor_quote: Reserve needed on 2033-01-01 if bought then (annuity-due, flat rate): 5% $405,391; 4% $421,767; 3% $439,305 (F-110)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes for student evaluators. Show cost $292k (2027), value $394,930 (2033, F-106) and face $500k once, side by side, with the phrase that the rate was locked in 2027. New vs brief 8.9: the reader-comparison risk, not which number to report.
would_change_detail: One FR sentence or three-number table in the reserve section.
north_star: Her promise looks exactly as safe as it is.

text: Since lock early settles the promise in January 2027, does our IPS still show a full decision-making framework for 2027-2042, with trigger, action and record at each date the designers marked?
anchor_quote: A long-term strategy may include planned adjustments as funding dates approach, but it should not be rewritten simply because markets move or hindsight reveals a different outcome. (Competition Guide p.5)
hypothesis: GUESS: yes if written as rules: Jan-2027 purchase if cost > money; 2028 deposit order of use; sleeve rebalancing band; 2031 floor share; 2033 facility rule; flexibility rule; annual funded-ratio report. Without them, 'static lock + sleeve' reads as 'safe bucket + growth bucket' (council AI panel scored it 6/10 Creativity, low authority).
would_change_detail: IPS structure checklist: which pre-committed rules must fit in the 500 words (the Guide forbids redesign later).
north_star: She sees what we will do at each date she has marked, before it happens.

text: Will a first-screen reader see about 1.5% equity in 2027 (the year WInS represents) and about 20% after 2028 as timid for a client who 'has been willing to take thoughtful risks', and which one number reframes it?
anchor_quote: Although she has been willing to take thoughtful risks throughout her entrepreneurial career, she wants her investment team to recommend an appropriate balance between pursuing growth and protecting the capital required for her goals.
hypothesis: GUESS: reframe with '60% of the money the promise does not need' plus one reason her risk belongs elsewhere (career risk already in her income, B9a Q5). Never argue in total-portfolio percentages. New: the 1.5% 2027 figure is the one WInS literally shows.
would_change_detail: IPS risk sentence; order of numbers in the FR risk section.
north_star: Honours her risk appetite where it cannot hurt her promise.

text: Which argument will a fixed-income reader accept under 'uses appropriate diversification' for a 2027 book that is about 97% one issuer, the U.S. Treasury?
anchor_quote: Your team may consider diversification across asset classes, sectors, industries, market capitalizations, geographic regions, risk characteristics, and funding purposes.
hypothesis: GUESS: (a) diversification by funding purpose, in Wharton's own word list; (b) diversifying a matched hedge adds risk to a fixed-dollar promise; (c) the sleeve is broad. Do not add a foreign bond to look diversified.
would_change_detail: One IPS clause; FR Portfolio Analysis framing of diversification.
north_star: Shows we understand why her promise should not be spread around.

text: Can our three Trading Notes, drawn from a mostly-Treasury book, show distinct official roles (future funding, growth, risk management), and have we placed a growth trade with a role-worded note yet?
anchor_quote: the Trading Note should capture the reasoning behind the decision, including its alignment with your strategy, the supporting research or analysis, and its expected role in growth, liquidity, risk management, or future funding. (Competition Guide p.3)
hypothesis: GUESS: risk is three notes all saying 'future funding'. Plan one per role: hedge (future funding), sleeve equity (growth), rule-driven rebalance or position-limit split (risk management). Complements B7b Q6 (supported/tested/refined).
would_change_detail: Which trades are placed in the next two weeks and that each note names its role word.
north_star: Each dollar has a job she can name.

text: Wharton's example note says 'begin preparing' and 'reduce portfolio volatility'; what single fact lets our hedge note explain buying the promise all at once, now, without seeming to contradict the example?
anchor_quote: We are purchasing shares of an intermediate-term U.S. Treasury bond ETF to reduce portfolio volatility and begin preparing for Laura’s future operating commitment.
hypothesis: GUESS: the example encodes gradualism most teams will copy. Our note needs one number showing waiting is the risky choice: promise costs ~$292k of $300k (F-101); 27bp fall erases headroom (F-104); cost exceeded $300k on 173 of 185 days in 2026 (F-111). New vs B1a Q2: the word 'begin'.
would_change_detail: Wording checklist for the hedge trade note (written at trade time, uneditable) and its TN reflection.
north_star: Shows we chose against the template for a reason tied to her money.

text: Which is largest for what Laura's facility money buys by 2033: market risk, USD/TWD risk, or Taiwan construction inflation, and does a USD-only nominal range miss the assumption the case names?
anchor_quote: Teams should identify and explain their assumptions about investment performance, the timing of cash flows, outside funding, the effect of inflation on portfolio projections and facility costs, and the financial flexibility Laura should preserve.
hypothesis: GUESS: construction inflation dominates. DERIVED: CCI ~3.5%/yr since 2021 -> ~+27% by 2033 (1.035^7); Taiwan CPI at 2% -> +15%; 2y USD/TWD sd ~6.8% (F-513); 2031-view market band ~+/-5% (B6b). A fixed US$ amount buys roughly a fifth less building if the trend holds (ASM). Keep the range in US$ but add one purchasing-power assumption line; no cost estimate (R-C95).
would_change_detail: FR assumption sentence on facility-cost inflation and FX, possibly a small chart ranking the three risks.
north_star: She is told what her gift will really buy, where she is building it.

text: If rivals show $300k+ facility contributions from 8-10% return assumptions, should our Final Report include a same-assumptions chart (lock early vs growth-first vs partial locks) that shows what bigger numbers cost in payment risk?
anchor_quote: uses reasonable assumptions and projections to evaluate funding reliability, the facility contribution, and financial flexibility under varying market outcomes
hypothesis: GUESS: yes, one chart of median and p5 facility money against shortfall probability for 3-4 designs on JPM inputs (the Q4 frontier is the data). Turns 'our number is smaller' into 'our number is real'. Evidence of rival habits: 2025-26 semifinalist '70% chance' Monte Carlo and '9% annualized' targets (B7b, B1b).
would_change_detail: Include a comparison chart in the FR Portfolio Analysis section.
north_star: Shows her the honest price of a bigger promise.

text: Is lock early now the textbook answer AI tools give every team, and which 2-3 Laura-specific decisions in our plan are absent from a generic liability-matching answer?

hypothesis: GUESS: at 5% yields AI assistants often suggest a Treasury ladder + growth bucket + Monte Carlo 95%. Cheap test: paste the public case into 2-3 AI tools, record each architecture, log the use in Works Cited. Likely distinctive parts: bought 2031 floor, model-free certainty, funded-ratio headline, price-of-certainty frontier. Overlap: B7b field simulation (assumed); new: an actual test.
would_change_detail: Which ideas get the IPS's scarce 500 words and the pitch's 50.
north_star: The answer to 'why us' cannot be the part every rival also has.

text: Could part of the facility money go in a second tranche after 2033 tied to project milestones, or does the case's 2033 framing rule that out?
anchor_quote: At that time, she will need to describe how much she expects to contribute toward the facility in 2033.
hypothesis: GUESS: the co-sponsor range must describe the 2033 contribution, so a staged gift cannot be part of it; it can be named once as a possible use of the flexibility money. More than a sentence risks looking like a case misread.
would_change_detail: One FR flexibility sentence, or a decision to leave it out.
north_star: Fits a founder who ships in stages without bending the case.

text: The IPS guide names liquidity repeatedly; where is liquidity in lock early, and does one clause cover it better than a rival's cash bucket?
anchor_quote: It should reflect your client’s goals, time horizons, liquidity needs, desired degree of funding certainty, and need for financial flexibility.
hypothesis: GUESS: nil liquidity need before 2033 by the case; the reserve pays itself out each January; Treasuries are highly liquid if the plan is delayed (BS-07). STRIPS trade less actively than notes (D1 to check). One clause suffices.
would_change_detail: One IPS clause on liquidity.
north_star: No idle cash held for needs she has told us she does not have.
